If I know that we must die and not come round again,
(then) we should not waste ourselves clinging to the false world.
Let us speak the truth, speak what is right, and speak no falsehood;
the way the Guru shows, let us walk it as his disciples.
The handsome young men cross to the far bank, and (seeing it) the fair maiden's heart takes courage;
(but) those who turned to the side of gold were cut through with the saw.
O Sheikh, in this world no one's life has lasted for ever;
on the seat where we now sit, many have sat and gone.
Cranes in Katik, forest fires in Chet, lightning in Savan,
and in winter (a wife's) arms about her husband's neck look lovely.
(So) those who must go are going; reflect on this in your mind.
Six months it takes to shape (the body), a single instant to break it.
The earth asks the sky, O Farid: where have the boatmen gone?
(The answer:) they are passing their time in the graves, and the souls are bearing the reproaches.
489.1: There is one God, Ik Oankar, the One who pervades all and is ever the same; his Name is Sat (the One who truly is); he is the Creator, the Being who dwells in all, without fear, without enmity, his form beyond time, unborn, self-existent, realised by the Guru's grace.
Raag Gujri, Ghar 1, Chaupade, by the First Guru (Guru Nanak Dev Ji).
(O Lord,) I would make your Name the sandalwood, if my mind were the stone (to grind it on);
if good conduct were mixed in as the saffron, worship would be done within the heart itself.
The worship to be done is to meditate on the Naam; without the Name no worship is done.
The images of the gods are washed outwardly; if someone washes the mind (in that way),
his impurity is removed, the soul is scoured clean, and his journey is to liberation.
Beasts win praise: they eat grass and give Amrit (milk).
Cursed is the life of men empty of the Naam, and the deeds they do.
He is near; do not think him far; he ever looks after (us) and takes care (of us).
What he gives, that (we) eat; says Nanak, he alone is the True (Master).
489.2: Raag Gujri, by the First Guru (Guru Nanak Dev Ji).
Brahma sprang from the lotus at (Vishnu's) navel, and recites the Vedas with his mouth, his throat tuned;
(yet) the end of that (Lord) cannot be seen; (Brahma) keeps coming and going in darkness.
O Beloved, support of my breath of life, why should you slip from my mind?
(You are the One) whose devotion the perfect devotees perform, whom the sages serve through the Guru's wisdom.
The sun and the moon are his lamps; the one Light of Murari fills the three worlds.
Whoever becomes Gurmukh stays pure day and night; the manmukh is in the darkness of night.
The Siddhas go into Samadhi and are ever in strife; what can (one) see with the two eyes?
When the True Guru settles the strife, the Light within and the melody of the Shabad awaken.
O Master of gods and men, infinite, unborn, boundless One in the true mansion,
may Nanak meet (you) in Sahaj (natural, unshaken poise), O Life of the world; cast your glance of grace and carry (him) across.
490.1: Raag Gujri, Ghar 1, by the Third Guru (Guru Amar Das Ji).
Ik Oankar: God is One, the all-pervading Creator, realised through the True Guru's grace.
Cursed is such a life, in which love for the Lord is not gained,
(and cursed the) work in which the Lord is forgotten and one goes and clings to another.
O mind, serve such a True Guru, by serving whom love for Govind wells up and all else is forgotten;
the mind stays held to the Lord, there is no fear of old age, and the rank of (true) life is gained.
Through love for Gobind a (rare) Sahaj has welled up; see what a (wondrous) devotion has come about!
Through the self itself, self-conceit has been eaten up; then the mind became pure, and (its) light merged in the Light.
Without good fortune such a True Guru is not found, though everyone may long (for him).
(When) the wall of falsehood within is taken away, then there is peace for ever.
O Nanak, what service can that servant render such a True Guru? He lays his very life before the Guru,
(and) keeps the True Guru's will in his mind; the True Guru himself shows (him) grace.
490.2: Raag Gujri, by the Third Guru (Guru Amar Das Ji).
O brother, serve the Lord; serve no other.
By serving the Lord, the fruit the mind longs for is gained; in other service, life passes in vain.
O brother, the Lord is my love and my way of life; the Lord is my talk, the Lord my story.
By the Guru's grace my mind is soaked (in the Lord's love); this is the service that befits me.
The Lord is my Simriti, the Lord my Shastra; the Lord is my kinsman, the Lord my brother.
I hunger for the Lord; with the Lord's Name my mind is filled; the Lord is my kin, who becomes my companion at the end.
Without the Lord all other wealth is false; it does not go along at the time of departure.
The Lord is my wealth; he goes along with me; wherever I go, there he goes.
False is he who clings to the false; false are the deeds he does.
Says Nanak, (this) is the Lord's will that has come to pass; nothing can be said (of it).
490.3: Raag Gujri, by the Third Guru (Guru Amar Das Ji).
In the world the Naam is hard to obtain; it is obtained through the Guru.
Without the Name there is no liberation; let anyone weigh it and see.
To my Guru I am a sacrifice, for ever a sacrifice.
Meeting the True Guru, the Lord dwells in the mind, and one stays absorbed in Sahaj.
When (the Lord) puts his fear (in one), detachment (bairag) springs up and comes into the mind.
Through detachment the Lord is found, and one stays merged in the Lord.
They alone are liberated who conquer the mind; Maya does not come and cling to them again.
One who makes his dwelling in the Tenth Gate gains understanding of the three worlds.
Says Nanak, through the Guru (the disciple) has become the Guru; behold his will!
The Creator himself brings this about, and one's light merges in the Light.
491.1: Raag Gujri, by the Third Guru (Guru Amar Das Ji).
Everyone says Ram, Ram, but by (mere) saying Ram is not attained.
(When) by the Guru's grace Ram dwells in the mind, then one gains the fruit.
One in whom love for Govind takes hold within,
never forgets the Lord; (such ones) say Har Har ever in mind and heart.
Those in whose hearts deceit dwells, who outwardly have themselves called Sants,
their craving never ends at all; at the end, departing, they repent.
Though one strives at many places of pilgrimage, the Haumai within never goes.
The man whose duality does not go, Dharam Raj punishes him.
Only the one blessed with grace finds (him); through the Guru a rare one understands.
O Nanak, (when) one kills Haumai within, then that one meets the Lord.
491.2: Raag Gujri, by the Third Guru (Guru Amar Das Ji).
That person has peace and an ever steady understanding, whose pride (the Lord) takes away.
That person is pure who understands through the Guru and fixes his mind on the Lord's feet.
O heedless mind, remember the Lord, and the fruit you wish for will be yours.
By the Guru's grace you will find the Lord's sweet essence; if you go on drinking it, you will be at peace for ever.
When the True Guru is met, one becomes the paaras; having become the paaras, one is revered.
Whoever reveres him gains the fruit; he gives instruction and makes (others) understand the True One.
Without (becoming) the paaras there is no reverence; (yet one) whose own mind is not won over instructs others.
The ignorant blind man calls himself a guru; whom can he set on the path?
O Nanak, without (the Lord's) glance of grace nothing is gained; one on whom he casts his glance gains (it).
By the Guru's grace (the Lord) grants glory and dispenses his Shabad.
491.3: Raag Gujri, Panchpade, by the Third Guru (Guru Amar Das Ji).
Wisdom does not spring up (by going to) Kashi, nor is wisdom lost (by staying away from) Kashi.
Meeting the True Guru, wisdom springs up, and then one gains this understanding.
O mind, listen to the Lord's praises, and enshrine the Shabad in the mind.
(Then) this understanding of yours will hold steady, and doubt will go from within.
Enshrine the Lord's feet in your heart, and (your) sins will be destroyed.
If you bring under control the self made of the five elements (the mind), then you dwell at the place of pilgrimage.
The manmukh's mind is foolish; it gains no understanding at all.
He does not understand the Lord's Name, and in the end departs repenting.
This mind is Kashi, all the places of pilgrimage and the Simritis: the True Guru has made this understood.
The sixty-eight places of pilgrimage stay with the one in whose heart the Lord remains absorbed.
O Nanak, meeting the True Guru, the Hukam (God's will) is understood, and the One has come to dwell in the mind.
(O Lord,) all that pleases you is true; (one who knows this) stays merged in the True One.
492.1: Raag Gujri, by the Third Guru (Guru Amar Das Ji).
O pandit, the one Name is the treasure; hear it and learn it; he alone is true.
Whatever you read in the love of another, in reading and reckoning there is ever pain.
Stay attached to the Lord's feet; through the Guru's Shabad understanding comes.
Taste the Lord's sweet essence with your tongue, and the mind becomes pure.
Meeting the True Guru, the mind is content, and then there is no more thirst or hunger.
Whoever has found the treasure of the Naam goes to no one else's house.
Though the manmukh may talk and speak, he gains no understanding.
Through the Guru's teaching there is light in the heart; that one gains the Lord's Name.
Even hearing the Shastras you do not understand, and so you wander again and again.
He is a fool who does not know his own self, and does not set his love on the True One.
The True One has led the world astray; nothing can be said (of it).
O Nanak, he does whatever pleases him, as is his will.
492.2: Ik Oankar: God is One, the all-pervading Creator, realised through the True Guru's grace.
Raag Gujri, Ghar 1, Chaupade, by the Fourth Guru (Guru Ram Das Ji).
O servant of the Lord, True Guru, True Being, I make my plea before you, Guru:
we are lowly worms and insects, True Guru, come to your refuge; be merciful, and make the Naam shine (in us).
O my friend, divine Guru, make the Lord's Name shine in me.
May the Naam, received through the Guru's teaching, be the companion of my life, and the Lord's praise my provision for the road.
Great, very great, is the fortune of the Lord's servants who hold faith in the Lord, Har Har, and who thirst for the Lord.
On receiving the Name of the Lord, Har Har, they are fulfilled; and in the Sangat (the company of the holy), virtues shine forth in them.
Those who have not found the Lord's sweet essence, the Naam, are unfortunate, and in the grip of Jam (the messenger of Death).
Those who have not come to the True Guru's refuge and his Sangat: cursed is their living, and cursed their hope of life.
The servants of the Lord who have found the True Guru's Sangat had this written on their foreheads by the Lord from the start.
Blessed, blessed is the Sat Sangat (the company of the true), in which the Lord's sweet essence is found; O Nanak, meeting in it, the Naam shines forth within.
492.3: Raag Gujri, by the Fourth Guru (Guru Ram Das Ji).
Govind, Govind, the Beloved: the Beloved (dwells) in the mind; joining the Sat Sangat, through the Shabad, he captivates the mind.
Repeat Govind; Govind is the One to meditate on; that God alone gives gifts to all.
O my brothers, Govind, Govind, Govind has captivated my mind.
I sing the praises of Govind, Govind, Govind; meeting the Guru, in the Saadh Sangat, (the Lord's) servant shines.
Devotion to the Lord is the ocean of peace; by the Guru's teaching, Kaula (Lakshmi), riddhis and siddhis come to lie at (the devotee's) feet.
The Name of Ram is the servant's support; repeating the Lord's Name, he shines in the Lord's Name.
The evil-minded are unfortunate, their understanding insipid; hearing the Naam, anger rises in their minds.
Put the essence of Amrit before a crow, and it is satisfied (only) eating filth, dung in its beak.
The True Guru, who speaks the truth, is the pool of Amrit; bathing in it, the crow turns into a swan.
O Nanak, blessed, blessed and most fortunate are those whose hearts' filth the Naam, (received) through the Guru's teaching, washes away.
493.1: Raag Gujri, by the Fourth Guru (Guru Ram Das Ji).
The Lord's servants are exalted; exalted is the word they speak with their mouths, for the good of others.
Whoever hears it with faith and devotion, the Lord in his grace carries him across.
O beloved Ram, unite me with the Lord's servants.
My beloved, my breath of life, is the True Guru, the Perfect Guru; the Guru has carried me, a sinner, across.
The Gurmukhs are fortunate, most fortunate, whose support is the Name of the Lord, Har Har.
The Amrit of the Lord, Har Har, the Lord's sweet essence, they obtain; through the Guru's teaching (theirs are) the storehouses of devotion.
Those who have not had the sight of the True Guru, the True Being, are unfortunate, struck down by Jam.
They fall into the wombs of dogs, swine and donkeys; struck down by God, they are great slayers.
O Merciful to the meek, be kind to your servant; in your grace, save (him).
Servant Nanak is in the Lord's refuge; if it pleases the Lord, the Lord carries (him) across.
493.2: Raag Gujri, by the Fourth Guru (Guru Ram Das Ji).
(O Lord,) be merciful and attach my mind (to you), that night and day I may meditate on the Name of Ram, ever.
The Lord is all peace, all virtues, all treasures; repeating him, all pain and hunger depart.
O my mind, the Name of Ram is my friend, the Lord (my) brother.
Through the Guru's teaching I sing the praise of the Name of Ram; at the end (it is my) helper, and sets (me) free in the Lord's court.
You yourself are the Giver, God, the Knower of hearts; in your grace (you) have put a longing in my mind.
In my mind and body a longing for the Lord has taken hold; God has fulfilled the longing in the True Guru's refuge.
The human birth was gained through merit; without the Name it is cursed, cursed, and goes in vain.
Without the Name, (one) who eats the sweet and the savoury eats only pain; his mouth stays insipid, and spit upon spit is cast in his face.
To those servants who are in the refuge of the Lord God, Har Har, the Lord, Har Har, gives glory in his court.
God says to his servant: Blessed, blessed, well done! O servant Nanak, he clasps (him) to his bosom and unites (him with himself).
493.3: Raag Gujri, by the Fourth Guru (Guru Ram Das Ji).
O my Gurmukh friends and companions, grant me the gift of the Lord, who gives life to my breath.
May I be the servant, the slave, of the Guru's Sikhs who night and day have meditated on the Lord God, the all-pervading Being.
In my mind and body a longing for the feet of the Guru's Sikhs has taken hold.
O Sikhs of the Guru, my brothers, friends of my breath, instruct me, so that, brought (by you), the Lord may meet me.
When it pleases the Lord God, he unites (me) with the Gurmukhs, to whose minds the words of the Guru, the True Guru, are pleasing.
Most fortunate are the Guru's beloved Sikhs: (meeting) the Lord, who is free of desire, they have attained the state of nirban.
Dear to the Lord is the Guru's Sat Sangat, (the company) of those to whose minds the sweet Name of the Lord, Har Har, is pleasing.
Those who have not found the company of the True Guru's Sangat are unfortunate sinners, devoured by Jam.
God, the Merciful, himself shows mercy; the Lord himself, through the Guru, is met, brought (by him).
Servant Nanak utters the Bani of (the Lord's) virtues; through Gurbani he is merged in the Lord's Name.
494.1: Raag Gujri, by the Fourth Guru (Guru Ram Das Ji).
Of those who have (found) the True Guru, the Being, may one who has found the Lord God give me his teaching and make the Lord sweet to me.
Mind and body grow cool and are made wholly green in the fortunate one who meditates on the Lord's Name.
O brother, may someone come and meet me who will make the Lord's Name firm (within me).
To that beloved I would give my life, my mind, my body, everything, who would recite to me the praises of my Lord God.
Patience, dharma and the Lord are found, through the Guru's teaching, by the one who ever fixes his mind on the Lord's Name, on the Lord.
The True Guru's Bani is words of Amrit; whoever speaks it puts Amrit into his mouth.
The Name is pure, and through it no dirt clings; (whoever) repeats the Name by the Guru's teaching is lovingly absorbed (in the Lord).
Those who have not found the precious wealth of the Name are luckless and dead; (such a one) dies and is gone.
(You are) the root of bliss, the life of the world, the Giver; O Lord, you give bliss to all your servants, to each who meditates on you.
You are the Giver; all beings are yours. O servant Nanak, (the Lord) forgives and, through the Guru, unites (them with himself).
494.2: Ik Oankar: God is One, the all-pervading Creator, realised through the True Guru's grace.
Raag Gujri, Ghar 3, by the Fourth Guru (Guru Ram Das Ji).
Mother, father and son are all made by the Lord;
the Lord has made the bond among them all.
O my brother, all our strength has come to nothing;
body and mind, all is the Lord's; the body is in the Lord's power.
The Lord himself has given his devotees loving faith (in him),
and in the very midst of household life he keeps them detached.
When love for the Lord has formed within,
then all that (one) does pleases my Lord God.
To whatever task, whatever work the Lord sets us,
that we do, what he himself has us do.
Those whose devotion has pleased my God,
those people, O Nanak, are lovingly attuned to the Name of Ram.
495.1: Raag Gujri, Ghar 1, Chaupade, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
Ik Oankar: God is One, the all-pervading Creator, realised through the True Guru's grace.
O mind, why do you keep brooding over your efforts (to earn), when the dear Lord is engaged in the task (of caring for you)?
He has created creatures in rocks and stones, and set their food ready for them beforehand.
O my dear Lord (Madho), those who have joined the Sat Sangat have crossed over.
By the Guru's grace they have attained the supreme state; the dry wood has turned green.
Mother, father, people, sons, wife: no one is anyone's support.
The Master delivers sustenance to each and every one; O mind, why are you afraid?
(The crane) comes flying hundreds of kos (leagues), her little ones left behind.
Who is there to feed them, to give them grain to peck? She keeps them remembered in her mind.
All the treasures and the eighteen siddhis rest in the palm of the Master's hand.
O servant Nanak, let us be a sacrifice, a sacrifice, forever a sacrifice to him; (O Lord,) your extent has no end, no near shore and no far shore.
495.2: Raag Gujri, Ghar 2, Chaupade, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
Ik Oankar: God is One, the all-pervading Creator, realised through the True Guru's grace.
Worldly people perform rituals and the six rites, and are steeped in these;
(but) the filth of Haumai within is not washed away; without the Guru they lose the game (of their life).
Show mercy, my Master, and save (me).
Among millions, hardly one is (your) servant; all the others are traders (bargaining for their own ends).
(I) have searched the Shastras, the Vedas and the Simritis, all of them; all proclaim one thing:
without the Guru no one attains liberation; reflect on it in your mind and see.
(People) have dipped and bathed at the sixty-eight (places of pilgrimage) and wandered over the whole earth;
day and night they keep many rules of ritual purity, (but) without the True Guru there is darkness.
Running and running, (we) have roamed the whole world; now (we) have come to the Lord's door.
(the Lord) has wiped out evil-mindedness and lit up the understanding; O servant Nanak, through the Guru (he) has carried (us) across.
495.3: Raag Gujri, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
The Lord's wealth is (my) chanting, the Lord's wealth (my) austerity, the Lord's wealth the food that pleases (me).
I do not let the Lord, Har Har, slip from my mind for an instant; it was in the Saadh Sangat that (I) found (this wealth).
O mother, the son has come home with his earnings:
the Lord's wealth as he walks, the Lord's wealth as he sits, the Lord's wealth waking and asleep.
The Lord's wealth is (my) bathing at the holy places, the Lord's wealth (my) wisdom; (I) fix my attention on the Lord.
The Lord's wealth is the raft, the Lord's wealth the boat; the Lord, Har Har, ferries (me) to the far shore.
The Lord's wealth has made me forget my anxiety; the Lord's wealth has taken away (my) doubt.
From the Lord's wealth I have gained the nine treasures; the Lord, the whole store, has come into my hands.
Eat it and spend it, it never runs short; it stays with (one) in this world and the next.
The Guru has loaded up the treasure and given it to Nanak; this mind is dyed in the Lord's love.
496.1: Raag Gujri, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
The one in whose remembrance all sins are destroyed and the ancestors too are saved,
that Lord, Har Har, repeat always, who has no end and no far shore.
O son, this is (your) mother's blessing:
may the Lord, Har Har, never slip from your mind for an instant; remember the Lord of the world always.
May the True Guru be merciful to you, and your love be for the company of the Sants;
may the Supreme God guard (your) honour like clothing, and Kirtan (the singing of his praises) be (your) food every day.
Drink the Amrit and live long, for ever; remembering the Lord, (know) endless bliss.
(May you have) joy and delight and every hope fulfilled; may anxiety never touch you.
May this mind of yours become the bumblebee, and the Lord's feet the lotus;
servant Nanak clings to them, as the chatrik (rain-bird) blossoms at the raindrop.
496.2: Raag Gujri, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
(One) makes plans to go west, (but the Lord) takes (him) east instead.
In an instant he can set up and pull down; the last word is in his own hand.
Cleverness is of no use at all;
whatever my Master has determined, that is what comes to pass.
In the very midst of the desire to win lands and amass wealth, the breath departs;
leaving armies, deputies and attendants, all, (he) rises and departs for the city of Jam.
(Another), with his mind's stubborn resolve, turns from all else and makes a show of himself;
what was not to be condemned he condemned and gave up, and that very thing he eats again and again.
The one to whom (the Lord), of his own nature, has been merciful: that person's noose he has cut.
Says Nanak, (one who) has met the Perfect Guru is accepted, whether householder or renunciant.
496.3: Raag Gujri, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
Each one who has repeated the Naam, the treasure: their bonds have been cut away.
Lust, anger, the poison of Maya, the sense of mine: from these ailments they have turned back.
(The one who) has sung the Lord's praise, joining the Saadh Sangat:
by the Guru's grace (his) mind has become pure, and (he) has found the peace above all peace.
Whatever (God) has done, (he) accepts as good; such is the devotion (he) has practised.
Friend and foe are all alike (to him); this is the mark of the way of Yoga (union with God).
The all-pervading (Lord) fills every place; (he) has known no other anywhere.
(God dwells) within each and every body, in all, without a gap; (that servant) delights (in him) with love, dyed in his love.
When Gopal (the Lord who sustains all) became kind and merciful, (he) came into the home of the Fearless One.
In an instant strife and anguish were wiped away; O Nanak, (he) merged in Sahaj.
497.1: Raag Gujri, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
Whatever man I take my plea to is filled with his own sorrow.
The one who has worshipped the Supreme Lord in his heart has crossed the ocean of fear.
Apart from the Guru and the Lord, no one cuts away (the mind's) pain and sorrow.
If one forsakes God and becomes another's servant, by that, one's honour, greatness and good name decline.
The ties of Maya, friends and kin, were of no use whatever.
The Lord's servant, though of low birth, is high; in his company the fruits the mind longs for are gained.
(There may be) hundreds of thousands, millions of the delicacies of Maya: in them thirst was not quenched.
Remembering the Naam, a light as of millions shone, and the Thing beyond the reach of the senses came into view.
Wandering and wandering, (I) have come to your door, O Lord, my King, destroyer of fear.
(Your) servant longs for the dust of the feet of the Saadh (the Guru); Nanak has found this peace.
497.2: Raag Gujri, Ghar 2, a Panchpada, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
Ik Oankar: God is One, the all-pervading Creator, realised through the True Guru's grace.
First (one) dwells in the mother's womb; leaving that place, (one) comes onto the earth.
Painted halls, beautiful gardens, mansions: nothing of these goes along.
All other greed and craving is false;
the Perfect Guru has given the Lord's Name; this alone is the thing that becomes the soul.
Wrapped up in dear friends, kinsfolk, sons, brothers and wife, (one) laughs;
(but) when the final hour arrives, death seizes (him) before their very eyes.
Doing wrong upon wrong, (he) gathered riches, gold, silver and money;
the hired man got (only) his wage, and all the rest became another's.
Fine horses, fine elephants and chariots (he) collected, and took care to make them his own;
(but) once the long journey began, they do not go a single step (with him).
The Naam is wealth, the Naam the king of comforts, the Naam family and helper.
The Guru has given Nanak the riches of the Naam; it does not die, nor does it come and go.
497.3: Raag Gujri, Ghar 2, Tipade, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
Ik Oankar: God is One, the all-pervading Creator, realised through the True Guru's grace.
Sorrows are gone, peace has made its home (within), the burning of craving is quenched;
the True Guru has made the treasure of the Naam firm (in the heart); (one) neither perishes nor comes and goes.
Repeating the Lord's Name, the bonds of Maya have snapped.
My God became kind and merciful, and joining the Saadh Sangat (we) were set free.
At all hours (he) sings the Lord's virtues, drunk with the delight of devotion and love;
in joy and in grief alike (he) stands apart; (he) has recognised the Creator.
The one to whom (he) belonged has saved (him), and (his) whole way of life has come right.
Says Nanak, God, the Being, is merciful; (his) worth cannot be told.
498.1: Raag Gujri, Ghar 2, Dupade, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
Ik Oankar: God is One, the all-pervading Creator, realised through the True Guru's grace.
(God) has made the fallen pure and made them his own; all bow before them.
No one asks (their) varna or caste; (all) long for the dust of (their) feet.
O Master, such (is the power of) your Name.
(You) are called the Master of the whole creation, (yet) the side you take for your servant is beyond compare.
In the Saadh Sangat Nanak has gained (this) understanding: the Lord's Kirtan is the support.
Namdev, Trilochan, Kabir the humble servant, and the Chamar (Ravidas) have been set free.
498.2: Raag Gujri, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
There is no one able to understand (him); who knows what (he) is like?
Shiva, Brahma and all the silent sages cannot grasp (his) state.
The account of God is beyond reach and beyond fathoming.
(Of him) one thing is heard, and it is grasped in another way; (he) lies beyond all speaking and telling.
(He) himself is the devotee, himself the Master, absorbed in himself.
Nanak's God pervades all; (I) have seen (him) everywhere.
498.3: Raag Gujri, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
Counsel, consultation, other cleverness: the servant (of God) knows none of these.
Wherever an occasion arises, there (he) meditates on the Lord.
To love devotion is God's age-old way.
(He) cherishes (his servant) like a child, and lavishes his affection on him.
In place of repetition, austerity, self-restraint, rites and dharma, the servant has sung the Lord's Kirtan.
Nanak has sought the Master's refuge, and has received the gift of fearlessness, and peace.
498.4: Raag Gujri, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
Worship the Beloved day and night; do not delay even for the blink of an eye.
Serving the Sant (the Guru), let us set our faith (on the Beloved), giving up stubborn pride.
The Enchanting (Lord) is the pride of my life, ever full of joy.
He dwells close beside (my) heart; seeing his play, the mind is enchanted.
He in whose remembrance the mind finds bliss and the rust comes away from the mind:
Nanak cannot describe the glory of meeting him; it is beyond the farthest beyond.
498.5: Raag Gujri, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
Those who are called munis (silent sages), yogis and knowers of the Shastras: (Maya) has brought them all under her own sway.
The three gods and the thirty-three crore (gods): there was no end to their wonder.
Mighty (Maya) holds sway over the whole earth;
no one else knows her secret; by the Guru's grace it has been found.
Conquering and conquering, she has conquered every place; she clings to all the worlds.
Says Nanak, from the Saadh (the Guru) she has fled; becoming his handmaid, she clasps his feet.
499.1: Raag Gujri, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
Joining both hands, (I) made my plea and meditated on my Master;
giving his hand, the Supreme God has protected (us) and wiped out all the evil.
The Master himself has become merciful;
all is well, all has become bliss; the children of Gopal are saved.
Meeting the Husband (Lord), the brides have sung songs of joy, the Master's acclaim.
Says Nanak, I am a sacrifice to that Guru who has saved all.
499.2: Raag Gujri, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
Mother, father, brothers, sons, kinsfolk: their strength is slight.
(I) have seen Maya's many shows; not a shred of it goes along (with anyone).
O Master, without you I have no one.
I am without a protector and without virtue, with not one merit; I have longed for your support.
I am a sacrifice, again and again, to your feet; here and hereafter, your strength is (my stay).
Nanak has had the sight of you in the Saadh Sangat, and all dependence (on others) is gone.
499.3: Raag Gujri, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
(The Sant) makes one give up household entanglements, delusion and attachment, and joins one's love to God;
he makes this teaching firm in the mind: sing (God's) praises in Sahaj, ever in Sahaj.
O friend, such a helper is the Sant (the Guru):
meeting him, the bonds of Maya break, and (God) is never forgotten.
After trying again and again in many and various ways, (I) have settled on this as best:
whoever, meeting the Saadh (the Guru), sings the Lord's praise, O Nanak, crosses the world-ocean.
499.4: Raag Gujri, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
(God) can set up and pull down in an instant; his worth cannot be told.
In a moment he makes a king a pauper, and sets (his) light in the lowly.
Let us always meditate on our own Lord;
why worry and fret over that (world) in which (our stay) is but a moment?
O my perfect True Guru, I lean on you; (my) mind has fallen into your refuge.
Says Nanak, we are heedless, ignorant children; protect us, placing your hand (over us).
499.5: Raag Gujri, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
(O God,) you are the Giver of all beings; dwell within my mind.
Where (your) lotus feet are enshrined in the heart, there is no delusion and no darkness.
O Master, the moment I remember (you), you are right there.
Show mercy, O Sustainer of all, that I may ever praise God.
May I cherish your Name with every breath; O God, it is you alone I long for.
Nanak has come to lean on the Creator; he has cast off other hopes placed in others.
500.1: Raag Gujri, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
(O Master,) in your mercy grant me the sight of you, that I may sing your praise night and morning.
With my hair may I dust the feet of (your) servants: this is my one wish.
O Master, apart from you there is no second.
O Lord, I think of you in my heart, worship you with my tongue, and keep my eyes on you.
O merciful, all-pervading Being, Master of all, with joined hands I make this prayer:
may Nanak, your servant, keep repeating the Name; (so) he will be saved in the blink of an eye.
500.2: Raag Gujri, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
(Maya) has come rushing from the realm of Brahma, the realm of Rudra (Shiva) and the realm of Indra;
but she cannot so much as cast her eye on the Saadh Sangat; she rubs and washes (their) feet.
Now I have come and fallen into (the Guru's) refuge.
The hidden fire (of Maya) burns fiercely: this the True Guru has made known to me.
She stays wound about the necks of Siddhas, seekers, Yakshas, Kinnars and men.
(But) God the Creator has taken the side of his servant Nanak, he who has millions of such handmaids.
500.3: Raag Gujri, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
(Through remembrance) ill repute is wiped out, there is honour in the world, and a seat is found in the Lord's court.
The dread of Jam ends in an instant, and one goes home in peace and bliss.
(Remembrance,) through which no labour goes to waste:
remember your God at all hours; let us meditate on him always, with mind and body.
O destroyer of the pains of the poor, I am in your refuge; what you give, O God, that alone we receive.
O Nanak, (the Lord's servants) are dyed in love for (his) lotus feet; the Lord keeps the honour of his servants.
500.4: Raag Gujri, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
The Sustainer of the world is the Giver of all beings; (his) storehouses are full of devotion.
Service to him never goes without fruit; he saves (his servant) in an instant.
O my mind, be absorbed in (his) lotus feet;
ask of him alone, whom all beings worship.
O Creator, Nanak is in your refuge; you, O God, are the support of (my) life.
Whom you protect, becoming his helper, what can the world do to him?
500.5: Raag Gujri, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
(The Lord) himself has upheld the honour of his servant.
The Guru gave the Name of the Lord, Har Har, as medicine, and all the fever has gone.
In his mercy the Supreme God has saved Hargobind.
The illness is gone and every comfort has come, through ever dwelling on the Lord's virtues.
My Creator has taken (me) as his own; this is the greatness of the Perfect Guru.
The Guru has laid an unshakeable foundation, O Nanak, which rises higher day by day.
500.6: Raag Gujri, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
(I) never set my mind on the Lord;
my life has passed in worldly affairs, and (I) did not sing the Name of the treasure of virtues.
Scraping together penny by penny with deceit, (I) ran about, using many schemes.
How many of the sorrows that come from forgetting God can be counted? The great enchantress (Maya) has devoured (me).
Be kind, my Lord; do not count what I have done.
O Gobind, merciful, compassionate, ocean of peace, O Lord, Nanak has come to your refuge.
501.1: Raag Gujri, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
With your tongue keep uttering Ram, Ram;
leaving other, false dealings, worship the Lord God always.
The one Name is the devotees' support, their stay here and hereafter.
In his mercy Gobind has given (them) the Guru's wisdom and a discerning intellect.
(They) have grasped the refuge of him who is the Cause of creation, the all-powerful, Sridhar.
The dust of the Saadh's feet is the way to liberation; O Nanak, (they) have found the treasure of the Lord.
501.2: Raag Gujri, Ghar 4, Chaupade, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
Ik Oankar: God is One, the all-pervading Creator, realised through the True Guru's grace.
Give up all your cleverness and come into the refuge of the Saadh (the Guru);
sing the praises of God, the Supreme Lord, the Supreme God.
you will find every comfort and well-being, and all trouble will end.
Mother, father, son, friend, brother: apart from him, none is (your own).
Here and hereafter he is the soul's companion, he who pervades all.
Millions of efforts and devices are false; none of them is of any use.
In the Saadh's refuge one becomes pure, and through God's Name comes liberation.
God is beyond reach, merciful and lofty; he is able to give refuge to the holy.
O Nanak, he is found by the one for whom union was written from the very start.
501.3: Raag Gujri, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
Serving your own Guru, dwell ever on the virtues of Gobind;
with every breath worship the Lord, Har Har, and the mind's anxiety will lift.
O my mind, repeat God's Name;
you will find peace, Sahaj and bliss, and you will gain a pure abode.
In the Saadh Sangat save this mind, and worship (God) at all hours;
lust, anger and pride will be destroyed, and all trouble will end.
The Lord is unshakeable, indestructible and unfathomable; come into his refuge.
In your heart worship (his) lotus feet; fix your attention on the One.
Those on whom the Supreme Lord God showed mercy, he himself forgave,
and gave (them) the Lord's Name, which (brings) every comfort; O Nanak, repeat (the Name of) that God.
501.4: Raag Gujri, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
(Whoever) by the Guru's grace meditated on God, (his) doubt was shattered;
sorrows, darkness and fears were destroyed, and (his) sins ran out.
(One) whose mind holds love for the Name of the Lord, Har Har,
(and who,) meeting the Saadh (the Guru), meditates on Gobind through his word: most pure is (his) way of life.
Recitations, austerities and countless deeds find their fruit in remembering the Name.
Those whom (God) in his kindness has himself protected: (their) works are fulfilled.
May I never forget you at any breath, O Brahm, all-powerful God.
(His) virtues are many; what can the tongue tell of them? They are countless, ever beyond words.
Taking away the pain of the poor, (God) carries them across; he is merciful, the bestower of grace.
Remembering the Name, the everlasting state (is reached); O Nanak, hold firm to the refuge of the Lord, Har Har.
502.1: Raag Gujri, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
An ego-bound intellect and the dense (hold of) Maya: this is a great, lingering disease.
The Lord's Name is the medicine; the Guru has given the Name of him who is the all-able Cause of creation.
With mind and body let us long for the dust (of the feet) of the Lord's servants;
(through it) the sins of millions of births are washed away; O Gobind, fulfil (this) longing.
At the beginning, at the end and in between, hope is a fearsome she-dog.
Through the Guru's wisdom and singing the Kirtan of Gobind, the net of Jam is cut.
Those plundered by lust, anger, greed and attachment ever come and go (in birth and death).
Through love for God, devotion to Gopal and remembrance, the wandering through births is ended.
Friend, son, wife, dear well-wisher: the three fevers burn them all.
Repeating Ram, Ram, he ends his sorrows who meets the Lord's servants, the Sants.
Wandering every way, (people) cry out, but nowhere is there release.
Nanak has firmly grasped the refuge of the feet of the Lord, infinite God, (his) shelter.
502.2: Raag Gujri, Ghar 4, Dupade, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
Ik Oankar: God is One, the all-pervading Creator, realised through the True Guru's grace.
Worship Sridhar (the Lord), whose very form brings fulfilment, the all-able Cause of creation.
Uttering (his) praises and hearing (his) boundless glory, one is never parted (from him) again.
Through remembrance, strife and sorrow pass away; (so) cut the noose of Death's messengers.
Uttering the Lord's Name burns up the enemies (within); there is no other remedy.
Be kind, O my God; the Name is Nanak's (life's) purpose.
502.3: Raag Gujri, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
(O God,) you are all-powerful, the giver of refuge, the destroyer of sorrow, the king of peace.
Singing your pure praises, O God, troubles go, and fears and doubts are wiped away.
O Govind, without you there is no other place (for me).
Have mercy, O Supreme Lord, my Master, that I may repeat your Name.
Those who, serving the True Guru, cling to the Lord's feet have, by great good fortune, their attention fixed (on him).
In the Saadh Sangat the lotuses (of their hearts) have opened, and they have given up a corrupt intellect.
One who sings the Lord's praises at all hours and remembers (him), merciful to the meek,
crosses over himself; all his company is saved as well, and all his entanglements are destroyed.
O God, my Master, your feet are (my) support; God is with (me), through and through, like warp and weft.
Nanak has come to your refuge, O God; the Lord has given (him) his hand and kept him safe.
503.1: Raag Gujri, Ghar 1, Ashtapadis, by the First Guru (Guru Nanak Dev Ji).
Ik Oankar: God is One, the all-pervading Creator, realised through the True Guru's grace.
In the one city (of the body) five thieves dwell; though held back, (each) runs off to steal.
Whoever guards his wealth from the three (qualities of Maya) and the ten (senses), O Nanak, attains release and liberation.
Keep in mind Vasudev, Banwali (the Lord);
let the Lord (dwelling) in the heart be (your) rosary.
That (tree) whose root is above and whose branches are below, to which the four Vedas are attached,
falls away with ease from those, O Nanak, who stay awake, their attention fixed on the Supreme Lord.
In the courtyard of my house (my heart) is the Paarjat (the Lord), the Essence (of all), (the world its) flowers, leaves and branches;
(he is) the Light in all, the Pure One, Sambhu (the self-existent): give up your many entanglements.
Listen, you who seek instruction: Nanak prays, give up the net of Maya.
(One whose) attention, through reflection in the mind, is fixed on the One has neither birth nor death again.
That one alone is called Guru, Sikh and physician who understands the (patient's) sickness.
Because of that (remembrance), no work or business (binds him); not (caught) in the world's business, though a householder, he is a yogi.
He has cast off lust, anger and pride, greed, attachment and the thirst for Maya;
in his mind he has meditated on the Essence, the Unmanifest, and by the Guru's grace has found (him).
Knowledge (of God) and meditation are all spoken of as (his) gift; (before the one who has it) all the fiends (the vices) turn pale.
He savours the honey of the lotus that is God; he stays awake and does not sleep.
(That tree, the Lord,) is deep beyond measure, its leaves reach down to the netherworlds; O Nanak, it pervades all.
By my Guru's teaching, no more shall I come into the womb; making me leave the poison, he has given me Amrit to drink.
503.2: Raag Gujri, by the First Guru (Guru Nanak Dev Ji).
O God, the Giver, who are all those who beg of you? There is no end to their number.
Whatever the hunger deep within (a person), you, the True One, are able to give (to meet it), O Giver.
O dear Lord, you, the True One, are (my) chanting, austerity, self-discipline and support.
Give (me) the Name of the Lord, Har Har, (through which) peace is found; the stores of devotion to you are full.
(Then) you remained in the trance of Sunn, absorbed (in yourself); you alone, the One, reflected on your own Hukam.
There was then no water, land, earth or sky; O Creator, you yourself made yourself manifest.
Then there was no Maya, none absorbed (in it), no shadow (of it); no sun or moon, nor any other light.
The eye that sees all was within (you yourself); that single glance (of yours) keeps watch over the three worlds.
He made air, water and fire, and the forms of Brahma, Vishnu and Mahesh.
All are beggars; you, God, are the Giver, who gives gifts as he himself sees fit.
The thirty-three crore (gods) beg of you, O God, the Leader (of all); for all your giving, your stores never run short.
Nothing goes into a vessel turned upside down; into an upright one Amrit falls, by (his) gracious glance.
The Siddhas, in their trance, beg (of you); begging for riddhis and siddhis, they hail your victory.
Whatever the thirst within the mind, water of that kind you give.
Those of great fortune serve their Guru; there is no difference between the Gurdev and Murari.
Neither death nor Jam casts an eye on those who, within, grasp the Shabad through reflection.
Now and ever I ask nothing else of the Lord: O Pure One, lovingly give (me) the Naam.
Nanak, the chatrik, begs for the Amrit-water: O Lord, in your mercy grant (him) your praise.
504.1: Raag Gujri, by the First Guru (Guru Nanak Dev Ji).
O dear one, (a person) is born and dies, comes and goes again; without the Guru there is no liberation at all.
Mortals steeped in the Naam through the Guru have found liberation and honour through the Naam itself.
O brother, set your mind on the Lord's Name;
by the Guru's grace, beg (it) of the Lord God: such is the glory of the Naam.
O dear one, so many put on many garbs to beg for alms, to fill the belly.
Without devotion to the Lord there is no peace, O mortal; without the Guru, pride does not go.
O dear one, death stands ever over (your) head, the enemy in birth after birth.
Those steeped in the True Shabad are saved; the True Guru has given (them) understanding.
In the Guru's refuge, (Jam's) messenger can neither cast an eye on them nor torment them;
(they) are steeped in the Pure One, the unseen Master, and have fixed their attention on the Fearless.
O dear one, hold the Naam firm, fix your attention on the Naam itself, leaning on the True Guru's support.
Whatever pleases him, that alone he will do; the record of past deeds cannot be erased.
O dear Guru, we have come running to your refuge; no other, no second (support), pleases me.
Now and ever I call on the One alone, the companion from the beginning, from the beginning of the ages.
O dear Lord, keep the honour of your Name; my bond is with you alone.
In your mercy show (me) the sight of the Guru, that Haumai may be burnt away by the Shabad.
O dear Lord, what should I ask for? Nothing is seen to last; whoever has come into this world goes.
Give Nanak the treasure of the Naam, that he may make it the necklace of his heart.
504.2: Raag Gujri, by the First Guru (Guru Nanak Dev Ji).
O dear one, we are neither high nor low nor in between; (we are) in the Lord's refuge, the Lord's people.
Steeped in the Naam, we are wholly detached; sorrow, separation and sickness we have cast off.
O brother, devotion to the Master comes by the Guru's grace.
Through the True Guru's word the Pure Lord (dwells) in the heart; (then) there is no subjection to Jam, nor any account left owing to Jam.
With their tongues (the devotees) utter the Lord's praises, in God's company; in whatever pleases the Lord (they rest) in Sahaj.
Without the Lord's Name, life in the world is in vain; without the Lord, even a single moment is fruitless.
O dear one, the false have no place, at home or abroad; the slanderer has no liberation at all.
(Though the slanderer) rages, God does not withdraw his gift; day by day it grows ever more.
O dear one, none can erase the Guru's gift; my Master himself has had it given.
Slanderers, to whom the Guru's gift is not pleasing, have their faces blackened by slander.
O dear one, those who seek (his) refuge God forgives and unites (with himself), without delay of even half a mustard seed.
He is the source of bliss, the Master over the masters; the True Guru unites (one) in union (with him).
O dear one, (whoever) has remembered the ever-merciful (Lord), by his mercy, has had (his) wandering ended by the Guru's teaching.
Touching the paaras, metal turns to gold: (such) is the greatness of the Sat Sangat.
The Lord is the pure water, the mind the bather; (the one to whom) the True Guru is pleasing takes the plunge (in it).
In the company of (the Lord's) servants there is no birth again; (one's) light is merged in the Light.
(O Lord,) you are the great Being, the unreachable tree; we are birds (dwelling) in you.
O Pure One, give Nanak the Naam, that age after age he may praise (you) through the Shabad.
505.1: Raag Gujri, Ghar 4, by the First Guru (Guru Nanak Dev Ji).
Ik Oankar: God is One, the all-pervading Creator, realised through the True Guru's grace.
Those who worship the True One with loving devotion have a thirst (for him), a supreme love;
weeping and wailing, they make their prayers; in the loving feeling of their hearts they find peace.
O mind, repeat the Naam, (taking) the Lord's refuge.
The Lord's Name is the ship to carry (you) over the world-ocean: make it your life's work.
O mind, death itself wishes well to (one who) dwells on the Lord through the Guru's Shabad.
(For one who) dwells in the mind on the Lord's Name, the intellect knows the Essence, (and finds) the treasure of all good.
Wealth makes the mind fickle and sends it wandering; the world is lost in attachment and fondness (for it).
The Naam (alone) is lasting: (the devotees) make devotion firm in their understanding, and through the Guru's word are steeped in the Shabad.
Wandering, (the world's) doubt does not end; the world wastes away in the sickness of birth (and death).
The Lord is the abode free of (all) desire; the austerity of the Naam is true understanding.
This world is in the grip of attachment and fondness; great is (its) pain of birth and death.
Hasten to the True Guru's refuge, (and) dwell on the Lord's Name in your heart: (so) you will be saved.
(With) the Guru's teaching set unshaken in the mind, the mind takes to reflection on Sahaj.
Pure is that mind in which the True One (dwells); within it is the precious jewel of (divine) knowledge.
In (his) fear and love, through devotion, cross the world-ocean, O mind; fix your mind on the Lord's feet.
(Keep) the Lord's Name, holy and purifying, in your heart, (and say:) this body is in your refuge.
The capital of the Lord's Name in the mind drives off the waves of craving and greed.
Says Nanak: with the mind subdued, (I have come) to your refuge, yours alone, O Pure One.
506.1: Raag Gujri, Ghar 1, by the Third Guru (Guru Amar Das Ji).
Ik Oankar: God is One, the all-pervading Creator, realised through the True Guru's grace.
I dance, and it is this mind that I make dance;
by the Guru's grace I shed my self-centredness.
Whoever keeps the mind steady is set free; whatever I desire, that fruit I obtain.
Dance, O mind, before the Guru.
If you dance to the Guru's will, you will find peace, and at the end the fear of Jam will flee.
The one (the Lord) himself sets dancing is called a devotee; he himself instils his love (in him).
He himself sings, he himself makes (it) heard, and sets this blind mind on the way.
One who dances (so) night and day drives away Shakti (Maya); in the house of Shiv (the Lord) there is no sleep.
In the house of Shakti the world lies asleep; it dances, leaps and sings of other things; the manmukh has no devotion.
Gods and men dance on the side of worldly life, through their deeds; the sages dance, reflecting on knowledge.
Siddhas and seekers who have reflected with understanding through the Guru dance with their attention fixed (on him).
Continents and universes dance in the three qualities; those whose attention is fixed on you, O Lord, dance (too).
All beings and creatures dance; the four sources of life dance.
Those alone dance who please you, (O Lord,) who through the Guru have fixed their attention on the Shabad.
They are the devotees, they know the Essence, whom (the Lord) makes accept his Hukam.
Devotion is this: that the attention stays fixed on the True One; without service there is no devotion.
When one dies while living, then one reflects on the Shabad, and then one finds the True One.
For the sake of Maya many people dance; rare is one who reflects on the Essence.
By the Guru's grace that one alone finds (you), O Lord, on whom your mercy rests.
If the True One is forgotten for a single breath, that time goes to waste.
With every breath he should be cherished ever; he himself forgives, as he wills.
Those alone dance who please you, who through the Guru reflect on the Shabad.
Says Nanak: they find the peace of Sahaj on whom your gracious glance falls.
506.2: Raag Gujri, Ghar 2, by the Fourth Guru (Guru Ram Das Ji).
Ik Oankar: God is One, the all-pervading Creator, realised through the True Guru's grace.
Without the Lord my soul cannot live, as a child (lives) on the support of milk.
God, unreachable and beyond the senses, is found through the Guru; I am a sacrifice to my True Guru.
O mind, swim across (the world-ocean) through the Lord's praise.
The Amrit-water of the Naam is found through the Guru, (by those) on whom your mercy rests, (O Lord).
Sanak, Sanandan and the sage Narad serve (you); night and day they keep repeating (the Name of) Banwari.
Servants such as Prahlad came to (your) refuge, and (you) kept their honour.
The One, unseen and pure, pervades (all); the one Light of Murari (is in all).
All are beggars, you alone are the Giver; they beg (of you) with hands held out.
The word of the devotees is sublime; they ever sing the wondrous story of the Indescribable.
Their life has borne fruit; they have crossed over themselves and carried their families across.
The manmukhs are in the grip of duality and a corrupt intellect, with the darkness of attachment within them.
They do not care for the discourse of the Sants; they drown along with their families.
The slanderer, by slandering, washes away (others') filth; living on Maya, he is an eater of filth.
Those caught up in slandering the Sants are on neither this shore nor the other.
All this expanse, this play, the Creator has made; the Lord, the Creator, has set his power in it all.
The Lord's one thread runs through the world; (when) he draws the thread out, (only) the One Creator (remains).
With love, with love and relish, (the devotees) sing the Lord's praises; their tongue holds the Lord's sweet essence.
Nanak asks for nothing but the Lord; dear (to him) is the love of the Lord's essence.
507.1: Raag Gujri, Ghar 2, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
Ik Oankar: God is One, the all-pervading Creator, realised through the True Guru's grace.
Among kings you are called the King; among lords of the land, the Lord of the land.
Among masters yours is the mastery; over all the noble clans, yours is the noblest.
My Father is the great Master, beyond reach.
What praise of you can be offered, O Creator? Beholding (you), we are lost in wonder.
Among the happy you are called the Happy One; above all givers, the Giver.
Among the radiant you are called the Radiant One; among those who savour delights, the one steeped (in delight).
Among heroes you are called the Hero; among enjoyers, the Enjoyer.
Among householders you are the great Householder; among yogis, the Yogi.
Among makers you are called the Maker; among keepers of religious observance, the Observant One.
Among bankers you are the true Banker; among traders, the Trader.
Among courts yours is the Court; of all who shelter those seeking refuge, you are the crowning mark.
How much wealth is yours cannot be counted; I cannot count (your) coins.
Among names, O God, yours is the Name; among the wise, the Wise One.
Among ways of life, O God, yours is the Way; among bathers (at holy places), the Bather.
Among the Siddhas, O God, yours is the siddhi; above all deeds, your deed.
Among all bidding, O God, yours is the bidding; above all commands, your Command.
As you make us speak, so we speak, O Master; what power have we?
In the Saadh Sangat, which is most dear to God, Nanak has sung (his) praise.
508.1: Raag Gujri, Ghar 4, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
Ik Oankar: God is One, the all-pervading Creator, realised through the True Guru's grace.
O Master, Narhar, Kin of the lowly, divine Purifier of the fallen,
Destroyer of fear and dread, Merciful One, Treasure of virtues: fruitful, O Master, is your service.
O Lord, Gopal, great Gobind,
merciful Keshav, (I have come) to the refuge of your feet; carry (me) across the world, the ocean of existence.
Remover of lust and anger, burner of pride and attachment, O Murari, the flower's nectar (makrand) to the mind,
put an end to (my) birth and death, O Upholder of the earth (Dharnidhar); keep (my) honour, O Supreme Bliss.
(We are) burning in the countless waves of Maya; O Lord, (set) the Guru's wisdom as the mantra in (our) hearts.
Cut away (our) proud intellect, O Compassionate One; erase (our) anxiety, O infinite Being.
Remember the Almighty every moment and every instant; meditation on God is the samadhi of Sahaj.
O Merciful to the lowly, ever gracious, all-pervading One: let us beg (of you) the dust of the Saadhs' feet.
Attachment is false, hope ends in evil, desire is full of vice;
keep my faith (safe from them), tear doubt out of (my) mind, and save (me), O Lord, Formless One.
O Lord, those who had not even a cloth (to cover them) become rich and wealthy, with storehouses, through your treasure.
The wicked, the ignorant and the foolish, by your glance, O Sridhar, have become virtuous, wise and steadfast.
Repeat (the Name of) the Lord of the world, O mind, and be free while living (jivan mukat); hold faith in (your) heart.
Kindness and compassion to (all) beings, (seeing the Lord) pervading everywhere: this is the way of the supreme swans (Param Hans).
(The Lord) grants the sight of himself, his praise to the ears, the utterance of the Name to the tongue;
the Lord is ever beside (them), close to every limb; O Nanak, God's touch saves the fallen.
508.2: Gujri ki Vaar: by the Third Guru (Guru Amar Das Ji); to be sung to the tune of the vaar of Sikandar and Birahim.
Ik Oankar: God is One, the all-pervading Creator, realised through the True Guru's grace.
Salok, by the Third Guru (Guru Amar Das Ji).
This world is dead in the sense of mine; it does not know how to live.
Whoever walks in the Guru's will: such ones attain the state of (true) life.
Those servants live for ever and ever who fix their minds on the Lord's feet.
O Nanak, the Gracious One dwells in (their) minds, and (those) Gurmukhs remain merged in Sahaj.
508.3: By the Third Guru (Guru Amar Das Ji).
Within (the self-willed) there is anxiety and pain; they have brought the beating of worldly affairs on their own heads.
Asleep in the love of another, they never wake; their attachment and love are for Maya.
They neither remember the Naam nor reflect on the Shabad: such is the conduct of the manmukh.
They have not found the Name of the Lord and have wasted their life in vain; O Nanak, Jam strikes them and brings them to ruin.
509.1: He brought himself forth; at that time there was no other.
Counsel and deliberation he held with himself alone; what he did came to be.
Then there was neither sky nor underworld, nor the three worlds.
Then the Formless One alone was, by himself; nothing had been brought forth.
As it pleases him, so he does; apart from him there is no other.
509.2: Salok, by the Third Guru (Guru Amar Das Ji).
My Master is for ever; he is seen by living the Shabad.
He never perishes; he neither comes nor goes.
Let us serve, for ever and ever, the One who pervades all.
Why serve some other, a second, who is born and dies?
Barren is the life of those who, with their minds set on others, do not know their own Master.
O Nanak, there is simply no knowing how great a punishment the Creator deals (them).
509.3: By the Third Guru (Guru Amar Das Ji).
Let us meditate on the True Name; the True One pervades everything.
O Nanak, one who understands the Hukam and is accepted (in his court) then obtains the true fruit.
(But) one who goes about only talking and speaking, and does not understand the Hukam at all, is blind, wholly unripe.
509.4: He made union and separation, and (so) laid the root of creation.
By his Hukam he fashioned the creation, and blended (his) light into the light (of beings).
From that light alone is all light; this is the Shabad the True Guru has made heard.
Having created Brahma, Vishnu and Mahesh, he set them to the work of the three qualities.
He made the root of Maya; (but) peace was found (only) in the fourth state (turiya).
509.5: Salok, by the Third Guru (Guru Amar Das Ji).
That alone is japa, that alone is penance, which pleases the True Guru.
Walking in the True Guru's will, one gains glory.
O Nanak, giving up self, such a one merges in the Guru.
509.6: By the Third Guru (Guru Amar Das Ji).
Only a rare one takes the Guru's teaching:
O Nanak, the one to whom (the Lord) himself gives (this) glory.
509.7: Attachment to Maya is ignorance, very hard and heavy.
With a heavy load of sins like stones, how is one to swim across?
Those steeped in devotion night and day, the Lord carries across.
Through the Guru's Shabad, casting off Haumai and vice, the mind becomes pure.
Let us meditate on the Name of the Lord, Har Har; it is the Lord, Har Har, who saves.
509.8: O Kabir, the door of liberation is narrow, a tenth part of a mustard seed;
but the mind has become a maddened elephant: how can it pass through?
If such a True Guru is met, who, well pleased, shows his grace,
then the door of liberation is wide, and I come and go (through it) with ease.
509.9: By the Third Guru (Guru Amar Das Ji).
O Nanak, the door of liberation is very small; only one who becomes tiny passes through.
The mind has grown stout with Haumai; how can it go through that (door)?
On meeting the True Guru, Haumai has gone, and the light has come to fill all (within).
(Then) this soul is free for ever, and remains absorbed in Sahaj.
510.1: God, having made the world, has kept it under his own sway.
God is not found by reckoning; (through it one) wanders in the love of another.
On meeting the True Guru one dies while living, and, understanding (the truth), merges in the True One.
Through the Shabad Haumai is shed, and one is joined in union with the Lord.
He knows all, he himself does (all), and he himself delights (in it).
510.2: Salok, by the Third Guru (Guru Amar Das Ji).
One who has not set his mind on the True Guru, in whose mind the Naam has not come to dwell:
cursed is a life like that; what did he gain by coming into this age?
Maya is counterfeit capital; in a moment its false show is stripped away.
Once it is lost from one's hands, the body darkens and the face fades.
In those who have joined their minds to the True Guru, peace has come to dwell.
With love they meditate on the Lord's Name, and keep their loving attention fixed on the Lord's Name.
O Nanak, (the Lord) has entrusted to the True Guru that wealth which abides within his very being;
(whoever receives it from the Guru) is dyed in a deep colour (of love), whose hue grows ever brighter.
510.3: By the Third Guru (Guru Amar Das Ji).
Maya has become a she-serpent, coiled about (all) in the world.
Whoever serves her is the very one she then devours.
Some rare Gurmukh is a snake-charmer (gararu); he has crushed and trampled her and put her under his feet.
O Nanak, they alone are saved who keep their loving attention fixed on the True One.
510.4: The bard (dhadhi) cries out and makes God hear (his plea);
within (him) patience grows, and he will find the Perfect One.
As is the writ written from the start, so are the deeds he will do.
When the Master is merciful, he will find (the Lord's) mansion, (his true) home.
That God of mine is very great; through the Guru he will unite (him with himself).
510.5: Salok, by the Third Guru (Guru Amar Das Ji).
All (soul-brides) have one Husband, who is always present beside (them).
O Nanak, if she does not obey his Hukam, then though he is within her very home, he is far away.
Those alone will he bring to obey his Hukam on whom his gracious glance falls.
She who has found peace by obeying the Hukam becomes a happy soul-bride, full of love.
510.6: By the Third Guru (Guru Amar Das Ji).
She who did not give her love to her Husband has burned and died all through the night (of life).
O Nanak, the happy soul-brides whose beloved Husband is the Lord, the King, dwell in peace.
510.7: I have wandered over the whole world and seen: the Lord alone is the Giver.
By no device is he found, the Lord who shapes (each) by their deeds.
Through the Guru's Shabad the Lord dwells in the mind, and the Lord is known with ease.
From within, the fire of craving is put out for one who has bathed in the Lord's pool of Amrit.
Great is the glory of the Great One: through the Guru he makes (us) speak (his praise).
510.8: Salok, by the Third Guru (Guru Amar Das Ji).
What love is this between the body and the swan (the soul), that (the soul) leaves (the body) lying where it falls?
Why speak falsehood to feed it, when it does not go along at the time of departure?
The body is dust, and blind; go and ask the breath (the soul).
(It answers:) I, lured by Maya, come and go again and again;
O Nanak, I did not know the Master's Hukam, through which I might stay merged in the True One.
511.1: By the Third Guru (Guru Amar Das Ji).
The wealth of the Naam alone is unshakable; other wealth comes and goes.
No thief can so much as eye this wealth, nor can a snatcher carry it off.
This wealth of the Lord is woven into the soul, and goes along with the soul.
It is obtained from the Perfect Guru; it does not fall into the manmukh's lap.
O Nanak, fortunate are the traders who came here and earned the Naam as their wealth.
511.2: My Master is exceedingly great, the True One, deep and profound.
The whole world is in his power; everything rests on his support.
By the Guru's grace the unshakable, lasting wealth (of his Name) is found.
By (God's) grace the Lord comes to dwell in the mind, (when) the valiant Guru is met.
The virtuous have praised him: the Lord is ever steady, unmoving and perfect.
511.3: Salok, by the Third Guru (Guru Amar Das Ji).
Cursed is the life of those who cast aside the peace of the Lord and forsake it, and earn pain, committing sins in Haumai.
The ignorant manmukhs are caught in attachment to Maya; no understanding comes to them.
They find no peace in this world or the next; at the end they depart in regret.
If someone meditates on the Naam by the Guru's grace, Haumai leaves him from within.
O Nanak, one for whom it is so written from the first comes and falls at the Guru's feet.
511.4: By the Third Guru (Guru Amar Das Ji).
The manmukh is an upturned lotus; in him is neither devotion nor the Name.
He moves within Shakti (Maya), and falsehood is all his striving.
His inner being and his mind are not softened (by love), and from his mouth come insipid words.
Such people, though joined to righteousness, do not blend with it, for within them is falsehood and self-interest.
O Nanak, the Creator has made this design: the manmukhs drown, speaking falsehood again and again, and the Gurmukhs cross over, repeating the Lord's Name.
511.5: Without understanding (that he is found by the Guru's grace), one falls into the great round (of births), and comes and goes again.
One who has not served the True Guru departs at the end in regret.
When (God) grants his grace, the Guru is found, and one loses self-conceit from within.
The thirst and hunger (for Maya) are lifted from within, and peace comes and settles in the mind.
(Then) one praises (God) for ever and ever, with the heart's attention fixed (on him).
511.6: Salok, by the Third Guru (Guru Amar Das Ji).
One who serves his own True Guru is revered by everyone.
Above all means is this means: that the Lord's Name is obtained.
(Through the Name) coolness and calm dwell within; repeating (it), there is peace in the heart for ever.
The Amrit (of the Name) becomes (his) food, the Amrit (his) clothing; O Nanak, the Name becomes (his) glory.
511.7: By the Third Guru (Guru Amar Das Ji).
O mind, listen to the Guru's teaching, and you will find the Lord, the treasure of virtues.
The Lord, the giver of peace, will dwell in the mind, and Haumai and pride will go.
O Nanak, (God) is found through his glance of grace; then the attention stays fixed (on him) night and day.
512.1: The Gurmukh is made pure: (he gains) truth and contentment, and (sees) the True One everywhere.
Deceit and vice have gone from within him, and he has conquered his mind with ease.
There the Light shines forth, the relish of bliss (is tasted), and ignorance is destroyed.
Night and day he utters the Lord's virtues, and (those) virtues are made manifest (in him).
(He knows that) the Giver of all is One; the Lord alone is the Friend.
512.2: Salok, by the Third Guru (Guru Amar Das Ji).
One who knows Brahm (God) is the one to be called a Brahmin: one who keeps his attention fixed on the Lord night and day.
He seeks the True Guru's counsel, practises truth and self-restraint, and his disease of Haumai departs.
He sings the Lord's virtues, gathers virtues, and keeps his light merged in the Light.
In this age rare is the Brahm Giani (one who knows God), who erases Haumai and merges (in God).
O Nanak, by meeting one who meditates on the Lord's Name night and day, lasting peace is found.
512.3: By the Third Guru (Guru Amar Das Ji).
Within the ignorant manmukh is deceit, and with his tongue he speaks falsehood.
The Lord, the Purakh, is not won over when deceit is practised; as his very nature, he sees and hears (all) at all times.
In the love of another he goes and instructs the world, out of self-interest, for the poison of Maya and attachment.
Living this way he suffers pain for ever; he is born and he dies, and comes and goes again.
His dread never ends at all; he burns and is consumed in filth.
The one on whom my Lord shows grace, he has him hear the Guru's teaching.
(Such a one) meditates on the Lord's Name, sings only the Lord's Name, and the Lord's Name alone sets (him) free at the end.
512.4: Those whom (God) has made to obey his Hukam are the perfect ones in the world.
They serve their Master, reflecting on the perfect Shabad.
The Lord's service and attendance (are done) through love of the true Shabad.
They have attained the Lord's mansion who have killed Haumai within.
O Nanak, the Gurmukhs stay united (with him), repeating the Lord's Name and keeping it in the heart.
512.5: Salok, by the Third Guru (Guru Amar Das Ji).
In the Gurmukh wells up the strain of focused attention and of Sahaj; he has fixed his mind on the true Name.
The Gurmukh stays dyed in (the Lord's) love night and day; the Lord's Name is pleasing to his mind.
The Gurmukhs behold the Lord, the Gurmukhs utter (the praise of) the Lord, the Gurmukhs, in Sahaj, have set their love on the Lord.
O Nanak, the Gurmukh gains true knowledge, and the deep darkness of ignorance is driven away.
The one on whom perfect grace rests from the first: that Gurmukh has meditated on the Lord's Name.
512.6: By the Third Guru (Guru Amar Das Ji).
Those who have not served the True Guru, who have not come to love the Shabad,
who have not meditated on the Name in Sahaj: what did they come into the world for?
Again and again they are cast into births, and are ever wretched in filth.
Attached to false greed, they reach neither this shore nor the far shore.
O Nanak, the Gurmukhs are saved, whom the Creator himself has united (with himself).
513.1: The devotees look beautiful at the True One's door, held steady there by the true Shabad.
Love for the Lord has sprung up in them; the Lord's love draws them.
They remain in the Lord's love, ever dyed in (his) love, and (their) tongues drink the Lord's sweet essence.
Fruitful is the birth of those who have known the dear Lord through the Guru and enshrined him in the heart.
Without the Guru (the world) wanders wailing, led astray by the love of another.
513.2: Salok, by the Third Guru (Guru Amar Das Ji).
In Kalyug the Name is the treasure; (one who) has earned it through devotion has attained the highest state, (union with) the Lord.
Serving the True Guru, (he) has enshrined the Lord's Name in the mind, and meditated on the Name night and day.
By the Guru's word he is detached in the very midst of the household; he has burnt away Haumai and attachment.
He has crossed over himself and has carried the whole world across; blessed is the mother who bore him.
Such a True Guru is found only by one on whose forehead the Lord has written it from the first.
Servant Nanak is a sacrifice to his Guru, who set him, astray in doubt, on the path.
513.3: By the Third Guru (Guru Amar Das Ji).
Seeing Maya of the three qualities, (people) have gone astray, as the moth, seeing the lamp, is burnt up in its flame.
The pandits, straying again and again, keep their eyes on Maya: let us see whether someone has brought something and offered it.
In the love of another they read every day only of Maya, the poison; God has led them away from the Name.
The yogis, the jangams and the sannyasis too have gone astray; their egotism and pride have grown great.
They will not accept clothing and food given as alms in good faith; through the stubbornness of their minds they have wasted their lives.
Among all these, that person alone has reached the steady state who has meditated on the Name through the Guru.
O servant Nanak, to whom can one say this and make it heard, when all act as (the Lord) makes them act?
513.4: Attachment to Maya is a ghost, (and so are) lust, anger and egotism.
These are all Jam's subjects; over them falls Jam's hard rod.
The manmukhs, to whom the love of another is dear, are put on Jam's road.
In the city of Jam they are bound and beaten, and no one hears (their) cries.
One on whom (God) shows grace meets the Guru; through the Guru comes release (from them).
513.5: Salok, by the Third Guru (Guru Amar Das Ji).
Haumai and possessiveness are an enchantress who has devoured the manmukhs.
Those who fix their minds on attachment to another, she has seized and clings to them.
If she is burnt away through the Guru's Shabad, then she leaves from within.
(Then) body and mind become bright, and the Name comes to dwell in the mind.
O Nanak, the remedy that kills (the poison of) Maya is the Lord's Name; it is obtained through the Guru.
513.6: By the Third Guru (Guru Amar Das Ji).
This mind has wandered for so many ages; it does not stay steady, and keeps coming and going.
It pleased the Lord, and so he made it wander, fashioning the deceiving world and bringing forth this play.
When the Lord forgives, then (it) meets the Guru, and stays steady, merged (in God).
O Nanak, through the mind itself the mind has been won over; (now) nothing dies and nothing is born.
514.1: The body is a boundless fortress, obtained only by good fortune.
Within the body (God) himself dwells; he himself is the enjoyer of its pleasures.
(Yet) he himself is detached and untouched; the Lord is free of all ties and yet joined (with all).
Whatever pleases him, he does; what the Lord does, that comes to pass.
Meditate on the Lord's Name through the Guru, and the separations (from God) are lifted.
514.2: Salok, by the Third Guru (Guru Amar Das Ji).
The True One himself has (us) say Waah Waah, through the Guru's Shabad.
Waah Waah is (his) praise and glory; rare is the one who understands (this) through the Guru.
The Bani of Waah Waah is (the form of) the True One; (through it) comes union with the True One.
O Nanak, saying Waah Waah, God is found; (yet this praise) is obtained by his grace.
514.3: By the Third Guru (Guru Amar Das Ji).
The tongue that says Waah Waah is made beautiful by the Shabad.
Through the perfect Shabad, God has come and been met.
From the mouths of the very fortunate, (God) has Waah Waah brought forth.
Those who say Waah Waah are the beautiful ones; the people come to worship them.
Waah Waah is obtained by (God's) grace; O Nanak, (through it) honour is won at the True Door.
514.4: In the body-fortress of the proud are hard (adamantine) doors of falsehood and deceit.
The blind, ignorant manmukhs, deluded by doubt, do not see (these doors).
By no means are (they) found; those who wear religious garb have worn themselves out with their garbs.
Through the Guru's Shabad (the doors) are opened (for those) who repeat the Lord's Name.
The dear Lord is a tree of Amrit; those who have drunk (its Amrit) are satisfied.
514.5: Salok, by the Third Guru (Guru Amar Das Ji).
Saying Waah Waah, the night (of life) passes in peace.
Saying Waah Waah, there is bliss for ever, O my mother.
Saying Waah Waah, the attention is fixed on the Lord.
Only by (God's) grace does (one) say Waah Waah, as (he himself) has it said.
O Nanak, Waah Waah comes only by the True One's will.
514.6: By the Third Guru (Guru Amar Das Ji).
The Bani of Waah Waah is (the form of) the True One; the Gurmukh has searched and found it.
Through the Shabad he utters Waah Waah, and Waah Waah with his heart.
Saying Waah Waah, the Gurmukh has searched with ease and found the Lord.
O Nanak, very fortunate are they who keep the Lord, Har Har, cherished in their hearts.
514.7: O greedy mind, so very greedy, you are ever steeped in greed.
Longing for enticing Maya, you roam in all ten directions.
Hereafter, (your) name and caste will not go (with you); as a manmukh you suffer pain.
With your tongue you have not tasted the Lord's sweet essence, and you speak insipid words.
Those who have tasted the Amrit (of the Name) through the Guru are satisfied.
514.8: Salok, by the Third Guru (Guru Amar Das Ji).
Let us say Waah Waah to the One who is true, deep and profound;
let us say Waah Waah to the One who is the giver of virtues, steady in understanding;
let us say Waah Waah to the One who pervades all;
let us say Waah Waah to the One who brings sustenance to all.
O Nanak, knowing him as the One alone, let us praise with Waah Waah him whom the True Guru has shown (us).
515.1: By the Third Guru (Guru Amar Das Ji).
The Gurmukhs ever say Waah Waah; the manmukhs eat poison and die.
Waah Waah does not please them; (their life) passes in sorrow upon sorrow.
Through the Guru, Amrit is (their) drink; with loving attention fixed, they say Waah Waah.
O Nanak, the servants who say Waah Waah are pure; they gain understanding of the three worlds.
515.2: By the Lord's will the Guru is met, and one's service and devotion take shape;
by the Lord's will the Lord dwells in the mind, and the essence (of the Name) is drunk in Sahaj;
by the Lord's will peace is found, and the Lord's profit is earned every day;
(one) is seated on the Lord's throne, and dwells for ever in one's own home (within).
They alone have accepted the Lord's will who have met the Guru.
515.3: Salok, by the Third Guru (Guru Amar Das Ji).
Those servants ever say Waah Waah whom (God) himself gives understanding.
Saying Waah Waah, the mind becomes pure, and Haumai leaves from within.
The Gursikh who says Waah Waah every day obtains the fruit the mind longs for.
Beautiful are the servants who say Waah Waah; O Lord, join (me) to their company,
that within my heart I may utter Waah Waah, and say Waah Waah with my mouth as well.
To those who say Waah Waah, Nanak offers his body and mind.
515.4: By the Third Guru (Guru Amar Das Ji).
Waah Waah! The Master is true, whose Name is Amrit.
Whoever has served (him) has obtained the fruit; I am a sacrifice to them.
Waah Waah! He is the treasure of virtues; only the one to whom he gives (it) partakes of it.
Waah Waah! He fills the waters and the land; through the Guru he is found.
O Gursikhs, all of you, say Waah Waah every day; Waah Waah is pleasing to the Perfect Guru.
O Nanak, whoever says Waah Waah in mind and heart, Jam's servant does not come near him.
515.5: The dear Lord is true, ever true; true is the Guru's Bani.
Through the True Guru the True One is recognised, and (one's attention) merges in the True One, in Sahaj.
(Such ones) keep awake night and day and never sleep; the night (of their life) goes by as they keep awake.
Those who have tasted the Lord's sweet essence through the Guru's teaching are blessed beings.
Without the Guru no one has found (him); the ignorant have wasted away and died.
515.6: Salok, by the Third Guru (Guru Amar Das Ji).
The Bani of Waah Waah is (the form of) the Formless One; none other is as great as he.
