Waah Waah! He is unreachable and fathomless; Waah Waah! He alone is true.
Waah Waah! He is free of all care; Waah Waah! What he does comes to pass.
Waah Waah! The Name is Amrit; some rare one obtains it through the Guru.
Waah Waah is obtained by (God's) grace; he himself gives (it) in his mercy.
O Nanak, Waah Waah is obtained through the Guru; (the one who obtains it) takes the Name night and day.
516.1: By the Third Guru (Guru Amar Das Ji).
Without serving the True Guru, peace does not come; there is no other place (to find it).
However much one may long, without (his) grace (he) cannot be found.
Those within whom is the vice of greed are led astray in the love of another.
Their birth and death do not end; in Haumai they suffer pain.
Of those who have fixed their minds on the True Guru, not one is left empty.
They are not summoned by Jam, nor do they suffer pain.
O Nanak, through the Guru they are saved; they merge in the True Shabad.
516.2: Only the one who holds love for the Master should be called a bard;
standing at (his) door he serves, and reflects through the Guru's Shabad.
The bard who keeps the True One enshrined in his heart will reach (the Master's) door and home.
Lofty is the bard's dwelling, through love for the Lord's Name.
The bard's service and duty (is this): he repeats (the Name of) the Lord, and the Lord carries him across.
516.3: Salok, by the Third Guru (Guru Amar Das Ji).
When a Gujri, a woman of rustic caste, finds her own Husband,
(it is) by reflecting on the Guru's Shabad and repeating the Lord's Name night and day.
She whom the True Guru meets is filled with the fear (of God); that woman is of noble family.
She alone on whom the Creator has shown grace recognises the Hukam of her Husband.
That (other) one, without good ways and of ill traits, the Husband has cast off and left.
When the fear (of God) takes hold, the filth (of the mind) is cut away and the body becomes pure.
There is light within and the understanding becomes noble, repeating (the Name of) the Lord, the deep ocean of virtues.
She sits in the fear (of God), she lives in the fear, and in the fear she does her work.
Here (she has) peace and honours, and in the Lord's court the door of liberation.
Through the fear, the Fearless One is found, and (her) light merges in the boundless Light.
O Nanak, she who pleases the Master is the good one: she on whom the Creator himself bestows his grace.
516.4: By the Third Guru (Guru Amar Das Ji).
Let us praise (him) for ever and ever; I am a sacrifice to the True One.
O Nanak, let that tongue burn which forsakes the One and clings to another.
516.5: He created the partial incarnations, and he made the love of another.
As kings rule their kingdoms, (so they ruled), and fought over pain and pleasure.
Shiva and Brahma serve (him), yet they did not find his end.
The Fearless, Formless One is beyond all sight; he is revealed through the Guru.
There, sorrow and separation do not touch; (such a one) becomes steady in the world.
516.6: Salok, by the Third Guru (Guru Amar Das Ji).
All this, as much form as there is, is coming and going.
Whoever has written this account (in the mind) has been approved.
O Nanak, whoever sets himself up (as great) is a fool, an ignorant one.
516.7: By the Third Guru (Guru Amar Das Ji).
The mind is an elephant, the Guru its driver, and (the Guru's) wisdom the goad; wherever (the driver) pulls, there it goes.
O Nanak, an elephant without the goad strays into the wilderness again and again.
516.8: My prayer is offered to him who created (all).
By serving my own True Guru, I have received every fruit.
I have meditated always on the Lord's Name, the Amrit;
in the company of the Sants I have erased (my) pain.
Nanak has become free of care, having secured the Lord's imperishable wealth.
517.1: Salok, by the Third Guru (Guru Amar Das Ji).
In the field the embankments are high, with an eye on the high house, the cloud;
(so) when devotion is at home in the bride, the Friend comes (to her) as a guest.
O cloud, if you are to rain, rain (now); why would you rain afterwards?
Nanak is a sacrifice to those who, through the Guru, have found (the Lord) within the mind.
517.2: By the Third Guru (Guru Amar Das Ji).
Sweet is what pleases; a friend is one who is true and straight.
O Nanak, (this) is understood through the Guru by the one in whom (God) himself makes light.
517.3: This is the servant's prayer before God: (O Lord,) you are the true Master.
You are the protector for ever and ever; I meditate on you.
Every being and creature is yours; you pervade them all.
Whoever slanders your servant, you strike him down and destroy him.
O Nanak, give up worry and stay free of care, clinging to (the Lord's) feet.
517.4: Salok, by the Third Guru (Guru Amar Das Ji).
Hoping and hoping, the world has died, yet hope neither dies nor departs.
O Nanak, hopes are fulfilled by fixing the mind on the True One.
517.5: By the Third Guru (Guru Amar Das Ji).
Hope and desire will die (only when) he who made them takes them away.
O Nanak, nothing is lasting except the Lord's Name.
517.6: He himself created the world, giving it a complete design.
The Lord himself is the banker, himself the trader, and himself the shop.
He himself is the ocean and the ship, and he himself the boatman.
He himself is the Guru and himself the disciple; he himself shows the landing-place (on the far shore).
O servant Nanak, meditate on the Naam, and cut away all sins.
517.7: Raag Gujri Vaar: by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
Ik Oankar: God is One, the all-pervading Creator, realised through the True Guru's grace.
Salok, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
To dwell on the Guru within, and with the tongue to repeat the Guru's Name;
to behold the True Guru with the eyes, and with the ears to hear the Guru's Name;
steeped in (the love of) the True Guru, one finds a place in the Lord's court.
Says Nanak, (God) gives this gift to the one on whom he shows grace;
such ones are counted the best in the world, but they are rare, a very few.
517.8: By the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
Those whom the Protector protected, he himself has rescued;
placing (them) at the Guru's feet, he has set their affairs right.
He himself became merciful and did not put them out of his mind;
in the company of the holy, he carried them across the world-ocean.
The Saakats (those who have turned from God), the slanderers and the wicked he destroyed in an instant.
In Nanak's mind is the support of that Master,
remembering whom there is peace, and all sorrows go.
518.1: (O Lord,) you are without lineage, stainless, the all-pervading Being, unreachable and boundless.
You are true, wholly true; you are seen to be true, ever true.
Nothing of what you have established seems false.
The Giver gives to all, as many as he has created.
Stringing (all) on a single thread, he has set his light (in them).
By (his) Hukam (beings are) in the world-ocean; by (his) Hukam (they) are carried across.
O dear God, he alone meditates on you who has good fortune (written) on his forehead.
Your state and extent cannot be perceived; I am a sacrifice to you.
518.2: Salok, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
O Merciful One, when you are pleased, you come to dwell in the mind, unsought;
O Merciful One, when you are pleased, (we) find the nine treasures in (our own) home;
O Merciful One, when you are pleased, then (we) live by the Guru's mantra;
O Merciful One, when you are pleased, then, O Nanak, (we) merge in the True One.
518.3: By the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
Many sit on (royal) seats, and sound a great many instruments;
O Nanak, without the True Name the honour of none has lasted.
518.4: (O God,) the Vedas, along with the Kateb, stand and meditate on you;
those who lie at your door are beyond all counting.
The Brahmas meditate on you, and the Indras on their thrones;
Shiva, Vishnu and the incarnations utter the Lord's praise with their mouths;
so do the pirs, the prophets, the sheikhs, the elders and the saints (auliya).
O Formless Lord, woven through all like warp and weft, you blossom in every heart.
Through falsehood one works one's own ruin; through righteousness one stands firm.
To whatever you yourself attach (us), to that alone we are attached.
518.5: Salok, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
(The heedless one) is lazy in doing good, and bold as a lion in doing evil.
O Nanak, today or tomorrow the heedless one's foot will be caught in the noose (of death).
518.6: By the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
However many (my) wrong ways, (your) love does not stay hidden.
Says Nanak: you, my Husband Lord, the true Friend within the mind, have covered (them).
518.7: O Merciful One, I ask this of you: make me the slave of your servants.
I obtain the nine treasures and a kingdom; by uttering (your Name) I live.
The treasure of the Amrit Naam is plentiful in the homes of (your) servants.
In their company I am delighted, hearing (your) praise with my ears.
I do their service, and (my) body is made pure.
Waving the fan, (carrying) water, grinding (the corn) and washing (their) feet, I rejoice.
By myself nothing can be done; O God, look on (me) with your glance of grace,
and let me, who have no virtue, be given a place in the dharamsal (house of worship) of the Sants.
518.8: Salok, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
O Friend, may I ever remain the dust of your feet.
In your refuge, may Nanak see you ever present.
518.9: By the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
Countless fallen ones become pure when (their) mind is attached to the Lord's feet.
God's Name is the sixty-eight places of pilgrimage; O Nanak, (it comes to the one) on whose forehead good fortune is (written).
518.10: With every breath and every morsel, let the Name of the Sustainer be repeated always.
The one on whom he shows mercy, he does not forget.
It is he who creates, and he himself who destroys.
The Knower knows everything; understanding, he gives it thought.
In an instant he sets up the creation in countless forms.
The one he joins to the Truth, him he saves.
The one on whose side he stands never loses.
His court stands forever, never broken; I bow to him.
519.1: Salok, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
Lust, anger and greed should be given up; let them be burned in the fire.
O Nanak, while we live, let us repeat the True Name every day.
519.2: By the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
Remembering his God again and again, he has obtained all the fruits;
O Nanak, the one who has worshipped the Naam has been united (with God) by the Perfect Guru.
519.3: He is liberated (while living) in the world, whom the Guru has instructed.
His affliction is gone, (his) anxieties are erased.
Beholding the sight of him, the world is delighted.
In the company of (God's) servant one is delighted, the filth of sins washed away.
There the True Name, the Amrit, is repeated.
The mind finds contentment, and the hungry one is satisfied.
The one in whose heart the Name has come to dwell has his bonds cut away.
By the Guru's grace, only some rare one earns the wealth of the Lord.
519.4: Salok, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
In my mind I think this thought: that I should rise each day and make the effort;
O Lord, Friend of Nanak, give (me) the occupation of the Lord's Kirtan.
519.5: By the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
Those whom God has kept safe by casting his glance (of grace): their mind and body are dyed in the Primal Lord.
O Nanak, (so it is with) those who are pleasing to God; I, poor one, am dying in pain.
519.6: Whatever pain there is in your heart, lay it before the Guru in prayer;
give up all your cleverness, and offer up your mind and body (to him).
Worship the Guru's feet, and evil-mindedness burns away.
In the company of the holy, cross the terrible world-ocean.
Serve the True Guru, the divine one; you will not die of fear in the hereafter.
In an instant he brings delight, filling the empty to the brim.
The mind finds contentment when the Lord is meditated on always.
He alone takes up the True Guru's service on whom (God's) grace rests from the very beginning.
519.7: Salok, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
(My love) is fixed in the right place; the Joiner has joined it.
O Nanak, the other waves number hundreds of thousands, (but) my Beloved does not let (me) drown.
519.8: By the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
In the dreadful forest I have found one companion: the Lord's Name, the remover of pain.
I am a sacrifice, a sacrifice, to the beloved Sants; (through them) Nanak's tasks are fulfilled.
519.9: All treasures are obtained by being dyed in your love.
Repeating your (Name), there is no regret.
No one can reach (the standing of) your servants, who lean on you.
Praise, praise to the Perfect Guru! Remembering (him) in the mind, I find peace.
The treasure of praise is with the Guru; it is obtained by (God's) grace.
When the True Guru looks (on one) with his glance of grace, there is no more wandering.
The Merciful One himself protects (them), making them his own servants.
I live by hearing, again and again, the Name of the Lord, Har Har Har Har.
520.1: Salok, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
You, my Husband Lord, have given (me) the silk robe of love to keep my honour covered.
My Master is wise and all-seeing; Nanak does not know your worth.
520.2: By the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
Through remembering you I have found everything; I have seen no hardship.
O Nanak, the one whose honour the True Master keeps, no one can erase (it).
520.3: Great peace comes when the Merciful Lord is meditated on;
heaps of diseases are destroyed when the Lord's praises are sung;
coolness pervades within when God comes to mind;
hope is fulfilled when the Name is enshrined in the mind.
No obstacle comes in the way when self-conceit is lost;
the treasure of divine wisdom (comes) when understanding is received from the Guru.
He alone has obtained all things to whom (God) himself has had them given.
(O God,) you are the Master of all; all are in your shelter.
520.4: Salok, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
As I cross the (world-) river, my foot does not sink (in the mire), for within me is love for you.
O Husband Lord, I have stitched my heart to your feet; for Nanak, the Lord is the raft and the boat.
520.5: By the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
Those at whose sight evil-mindedness departs: they alone are our friends.
I search the whole world; O servant Nanak, (such friends) are a rare few.
520.6: (O God,) seeing your devotees, the Master comes to mind;
dwelling in the Saadh Sangat, the mind's filth is cut away;
repeating the Shabad of (God's) servant, the fear of birth and death is cut away.
The Sants untie the bonds, and all the demons run and hide.
They attach (our) love to him who upholds all (creation),
the unreachable, the infinite, whose seat is the highest of the high.
With palms joined, day and night, he should be meditated on with every breath.
When he himself becomes merciful, then the company of the devotees is found.
520.7: Salok, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
In the alien wilds there is stifling heat and turmoil, and cries ring out on the roads.
O Husband Lord, my cord is tied to you; (so) Nanak passes through the forest in bliss.
520.8: By the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
True fellowship is with those in whose company the Name is repeated.
O Nanak, no company should be kept with those who care (only) for their own ends.
520.9: Approved is that moment in which the True Guru is met.
When the company of the Saadh is found, pain does not strike again.
The unshakeable place is found, and one does not lie in the womb again.
The One, Brahm, is seen in all.
The essence of wisdom (comes) by fixing the attention (on God) and drawing the gaze in (from outward things).
It is all the repetition of (God's Name), whatever is spoken by the mouth.
Understanding the Hukam, one is delighted, and dwells in peace upon peace.
Those whom (God) has tested and placed in (his) treasury are never counterfeit again.
520.10: Salok, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
The pangs of separation are pincers (of torture), so harsh they cannot be borne.
If that Master is met, O Nanak, then truly (there is) every comfort.
521.1: By the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
The earth dwells in water; wood keeps fire (within it).
O Nanak, (such) is that Husband Lord, on whose support everyone rests.
521.2: (O God,) the works you have done are within your power alone;
that alone comes to pass in the world which you have ordained from the very start.
We are struck with wonder and awe, seeing your creation.
(We,) your servants, have fallen at your refuge; be gracious, that I may be set free.
The treasure is in your hands; you give it to the one who pleases you.
Those on whom (you) become merciful, they alone receive the Lord's Name.
O unreachable, imperceptible, infinite (Lord), your end cannot be found.
The one on whom you are gracious meditates on the Naam.
521.3: Salok, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
The ladles move about (in the food) but do not know its taste; they stay empty.
Those faces alone look (lovely), O Nanak, that are dyed in the relish of love.
521.4: By the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
Through the tracker (the Guru) I have traced the footprints (of those who) had laid (my field) waste.
You, my Husband Lord, have given (it) a fence; O Nanak, the field is not laid waste (now).
521.5: Worship that True One, in whose keeping is everything.
He himself is the Master of both ends (this world and the next), and in an instant he sets (all affairs) right.
Give up all (other) devices, and take hold of his shelter;
run and fall into his refuge, and gain the joy of all joys.
(Good) deeds, dharam and the knowledge of the essence: (all) come with the company of the Sants;
when the Amrit Naam is repeated, no obstacle stands in the way.
The one to whom he himself is kind: in that one's mind he comes to dwell;
when the Master is pleased, all treasures are obtained.
521.6: Salok, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
I have found the One worth finding, for my Beloved has shown grace.
There is one Creator alone; O Nanak, no second is seen.
521.7: By the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
Drawing the arrow of Truth, throw down the wretched sins;
keep the Guru's sweet mantra in mind, O Nanak, and sorrow will not come.
521.8: Praise, praise to the Creator, who himself has brought cool peace.
Always repeat (the Name of) him who is kind to all beings and creatures.
The Mighty One has shown mercy, and the wailing and lament are over;
fevers, sorrows and diseases have fled, through the glory of the perfect Guru.
Honouring the lowly and setting them firm, he has given (them) his own protection;
he himself has set (them) free, cutting away all bonds.
Craving is quenched, hope is fulfilled, the mind is sated with contentment.
The boundless Master is the greatest of the great; neither virtue nor sin leaves a stain on him.
521.9: Salok, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
Those on whom God becomes merciful, they alone repeat (the Name of) the Lord, Har Har.
O Nanak, as soon as they meet the Saadh Sangat, their love is drawn to Ram.
521.10: By the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
Remember Ram, O fortunate ones; he is in the water, on the land and in the sky.
O Nanak, when the Name is worshipped, no obstacle stands in the way.
521.11: What the devotees say is approved; it finds acceptance in the Lord's court.
(O Lord,) your devotees lean on you; they are dyed in the True Name.
The one to whom he is merciful: that one's pain departs.
O Merciful One, the devotees are your own; you bestow your kindness on them.
Pain, suffering, grave disease and Maya do not touch such a one.
This is the devotees' support: they sing the praises of Govind;
for ever and ever, day and night, meditating on the One alone,
and drinking the Amrit Naam, (the Lord's) servants remain sated with the Naam.
522.1: Salok, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
Millions of obstacles beset the one who forgets the Name;
O Nanak, (such people) wail night and day, like a crow in a deserted house.
522.2: By the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
When union with the Beloved comes about, that alone is the lovely season.
May he not be forgotten for a moment or an instant; O Nanak, let him be remembered always.
522.3: (The five vices) are brave warriors and heroes, whom no one has held back;
the five have gathered a mighty, stubborn army;
the ten women (the organs) make even ascetics who have renounced the world cling (to pleasures);
conquering (all) one by one, they take them into their own ranks: this alone is what they want.
(The world of) the three qualities is in their power; no one has turned them back.
Doubt is (their) fort and Maya the moat: say, by what means can it be broken?
By worshipping the perfect Guru this fearsome army is smashed.
Before him I would stand day and night with joined hands.
522.4: Salok, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
Sing (his) praises day after day, and all sins are washed away;
O Nanak, if the Name is forgotten, millions of torments spring up.
522.5: By the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
O Nanak, when the True Guru is met, the way (of life) becomes perfect;
(then,) while laughing, playing, dressing and eating, liberation comes in the very midst (of it all).
522.6: Blessed, blessed is that True Guru, who has torn down the fort of doubt.
Praise, praise to that True Guru, who has joined (us) to the Lord.
The Guru gives the Naam, the treasure that never runs out, as medicine;
it is he who has destroyed the great and dreadful disease.
The treasure of the Naam is found, a vast store of riches;
this priceless (human) birth is won, and one's own self is recognised.
The greatness of the mighty Guru, the Divine One, cannot be told;
the Guru is the Supreme Lord, the Supreme God, beyond the farthest beyond, unseen and unfathomable.
522.7: Salok, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
Making the effort, live (the true life); practising (it), enjoy peace;
meditating, meet God; O Nanak, (so) anxiety is lifted.
522.8: By the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
Good thoughts, the uttering of Gobind's praises, the pure company of the Saadh (be mine);
have mercy, O Lord, that I, Nanak, may not forget the Naam for even a moment.
522.9: (O Lord,) if (all) that happens is your doing, why should we be afraid?
The one meeting whom the Name is repeated: to that one let (our) soul be offered.
When the Master beyond count comes to mind, (the heart) is filled with joy.
Who can harm the one on whose side the Formless Lord stands?
Everything is in his power; no one is outside (it).
That (Lord) has come to dwell in the minds of the devotees; through Truth he is absorbed (in them).
Your servants meditate on you; you are (their) Protector.
Almighty over all, you make (them) glad with your glance of grace.
523.1: Salok, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
(O God,) take away lust, anger, intoxication (of pride), greed, attachment and evil desires;
keep (me) safe, O my own God; Nanak is ever a sacrifice (to you).
523.2: By the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
Eating and eating, the mouth has worn out; wearing (clothes), the whole body (too);
O Nanak, cursed is the life of those whose love has not been fixed on the True One.
523.3: As your Hukam is, just so it has to be;
wherever you yourself keep (us), there (we) must go and stand.
In the love of your Name, evil-mindedness is washed away;
repeating you over and over, O Formless Lord, doubt and fear are cast away.
Those who are dyed in your love are not yoked to births (again);
within and without, their eyes behold the One.
Those who have recognised the Hukam never have to weep;
O Nanak, they string the Name, (God's) gift, into their minds.
523.4: Salok, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
While alive he did not remember (the Lord); dead, he mingles with the dust;
O Nanak, the foolish and unclean Saakat has passed (his life) with the world.
523.5: By the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
(The one who) remembered the Lord while living, and in dying (stayed) in the Lord's love,
has carried the precious gift of birth across, O Nanak, in the company of the Saadh.
523.6: From the beginning, from the start of the ages, (God) himself is the Protector;
the Creator's Name is True, and the True One pervades (all).
Nowhere is he lacking; he fills every single heart.
Merciful and mighty, he himself makes (us) do the labour (of devotion).
Those in whose minds he himself has come to dwell are at ease for ever.
Having made the creation himself, he himself has cherished it;
he himself is everything, endless and boundless.
With the support of the perfect Guru, Nanak has kept (him) in remembrance.
523.7: Salok, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
In the beginning, in the middle and at the end, the Supreme God has protected (his servant);
the True Guru has given (him) the Lord's Name, and (he) has tasted the Amrit.
(His is) the boundless company of the Saadhs, and night and day he dwells on the Lord's virtues;
he has gained every wish of his heart, and does not wander through births.
All lies in the Creator's hands, who brings about (every) cause.
Nanak begs for this gift: that by the dust (of the feet) of the Sants he may cross over.
523.8: By the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
Enshrine in your mind the One who created (you).
Whichever servant has meditated on the Master has found peace;
that Gurmukh's life has borne fruit, and his coming (into the world) is accepted.
Understanding the Hukam, he is in bliss: (the Hukam) the Master has decreed.
The one to whom (God) himself has become merciful does not wander in doubt;
whatever the Master has given, he has found it to be joy.
O Nanak, the one to whom the Friend is kind, he makes (him) understand the Hukam;
those whom he himself leads astray die over and over and are ever born again.
523.9: (God) struck down the slanderers at once, and did not let them stand for even an instant.
God cannot bear (his) servant's pain: seizing (the slanderers), he has yoked them to births.
By the hair of their foreheads he has dashed them down, and cast them on the road of Jam.
Struck by pain, they cry out, and lie in dreadful hell.
Hugging (his) servants to his breast, O Nanak, the True Lord has kept them safe.
524.1: Salok, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
Repeat (the Name of) Ram, O fortunate ones; he fills the water and the land.
O Nanak, when the Name is meditated on, no obstacle stands in the way.
524.2: By the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
Millions of obstacles beset the one who forgets the Name;
O Nanak, (such people) wail night and day, like a crow in a deserted house.
524.3: Remembering the Giver over and over, (my) heart's aims are fulfilled;
the wish and the hope of the mind are fulfilled, and the sorrows are gone.
The treasure of the Naam is found, which (I) was seeking;
(my) light has merged with the Light, and the toil is over.
In that house peace, Sahaj and bliss have come to dwell;
coming and going have ended; there is no birth there, nor death.
Master and servant are seen to be one and the same;
by the Guru's grace, Nanak has merged in the True One.
524.4: Raag Gujri, the hymns of the Bhagats.
Ik Oankar: God is One, the all-pervading Creator, realised through the True Guru's grace.
Ghar 2, a Chaupada of Sri Kabir Ji.
With four feet and two horns, and a mouth that cannot speak, how then will you sing of (the Lord's) virtues?
Whether you rise or sit, the stick will fall on you; where then will you hide your head?
Without the Lord, you will become an ox in another's hands,
with torn nostrils and broken shoulders, eating the chaff of kodo millet.
Roaming the forest all day long, even then your belly will not be full.
You do not heed what the devotees, the Lord's servants, tell you; you will reap what you yourself have done.
Going through pain and pleasure, sunk in great delusion, you will wander through countless births.
You have thrown away the jewel of (human) life and forgotten God; where will you find this chance again?
Going round and round like an oil-presser's ox, the night (of your life) will pass without release.
Says Kabir: without the Name of Ram, you will beat your head and regret.
524.5: Raag Gujri, Ghar 3, the hymn of Bhagat Kabir Ji.
Kabir's mother weeps, sobbing again and again:
O Raghurai (the Lord), how will these children live?
Kabir has left off all his work, the setting of the warp and the weaving,
and has written the Lord's Name upon his body.
Kabir answers: as long as I am running the thread through the eye of the bobbin,
so long does Ram, the Beloved, slip from my mind.
My understanding is shallow, and by caste I am a weaver,
(yet) the Lord's Name is the profit I have gained.
Says Kabir: listen, O my mother:
for us and for these (children) the Giver is the one Raghurai.
525.1: Raag Gujri, Ghar 1, Pade of Sri Namdev Ji.
Ik Oankar: God is One, the all-pervading Creator, realised through the True Guru's grace.
(O Lord,) if you give (me) a kingdom, what glory is that (to me)?
If you make me beg for alms, what would I lose?
O my mind, worship the Lord, (in whom is) the state of nirban;
your coming and going will not happen again.
(O Lord,) you created all, and you have led all astray in doubt;
the one to whom you give (it), that one alone has understanding.
If the True Guru is met, doubt goes.
Whom shall I worship? No other comes into my sight.
One stone is treated with love,
(and) on another stone the foot is set.
If that one is a god, then this one too is a god.
Says Namdev: as for me, (I am in) the Lord's service.
525.2: Raag Gujri, Ghar 1, the hymn of Bhagat Namdev Ji.
No stain of dirt is on him; he is beyond all dirt; like a fragrance, he has come and settled (in every heart), O sister.
No one saw him coming; who can know (him), O sister?
Who can describe him? By whom can he be understood? The beautiful Lord (Ramaiya) fills all, O sister.
As the track of a bird in the sky cannot be traced,
as the path of a fish in water cannot be seen,
as a pot in the sky, filled with the water of a mirage, (cannot be grasped),
(such is) Bithal, the Master of Nama, who has burned away the three (fevers).
525.3: Raag Gujri, Ghar 3, Pade of Sri Ravidas Ji.
Ik Oankar: God is One, the all-pervading Creator, realised through the True Guru's grace.
The calf has already made the milk its leavings, at the very udder;
the flower the bumblebee has spoiled, and the water the fish.
O mother, what shall I bring to offer in the worship of Gobind?
I find no other flower, none beyond compare.
The sandal trees of Malaya have snakes coiled round them;
poison and Amrit live side by side.
Incense, lamps, food offerings: their fragrance (has already been taken);
how, then, are your servants to worship you?
I offer up my body and mind; this is the worship I lay before (you);
by the Guru's grace I attain the Pure One.
Worship and adoration (with such offerings) are not mine to give you;
says Ravidas: what, then, will my state be?
525.4: Raag Gujri, Ghar 1, Pade of Sri Trilochan Ji.
Ik Oankar: God is One, the all-pervading Creator, realised through the True Guru's grace.
(If) the inner self, filthy (as it is), has not been made pure, (and) outwardly (one wears) the garb of a renunciate,
(if) the lotus of the heart and Brahm within the body have not been recognised, why become a sannyasi?
(The world) has strayed in doubt, O Jai Chand;
it has not, not at all, recognised the Lord of supreme bliss.
(One) ate from house to house and fattened the body, (put on) the patched coat and the earrings, (all) for Maya;
(one) smeared on the ashes of the cremation ground, (but) without the Guru the essence was not found.
Why do you chant, why do you practise austerities, why do you churn water?
Remember the One beyond desire, who created the eighty-four lakh (forms of life).
Why (carry) the water-pot, O wearer of the patched robe? Why wander to the sixty-eight (places of pilgrimage)?
Says Trilochan: listen, O mortal: where there is no grain, why spread (the sheaves) for threshing?
526.1: Raag Gujri, the hymn of Bhagat Trilochan Ji.
One who at the very end thinks of wealth, and dies in such thoughts,
is born again and again as a snake.
O sister, may the Name of Gobind not be forgotten.
One who at the very end thinks of (his) wife, and dies in such thoughts,
is born again and again as a prostitute.
One who at the very end thinks of (his) sons, and dies in such thoughts,
is born again and again as a pig.
One who at the very end thinks of mansions, and dies in such thoughts,
is born again and again as a ghost.
One who at the very end thinks of Narayan, and dies in such thoughts,
says Tilochan: that man is liberated; Pitambar, the Lord, dwells in his heart.
526.2: Raag Gujri, Ghar 4, a Pada of Sri Jaidev Ji.
Ik Oankar: God is One, the all-pervading Creator, realised through the True Guru's grace.
(He is) the Supreme, the Origin (of all), the all-pervading Being, beyond compare, endowed with truth and every such quality;
supremely wondrous, beyond Prakriti (the stuff of the world), beyond the reach of thought, reaching everywhere.
Only the Name of Ram, which delights the mind,
utter: it is Amrit, the very essence;
by remembering it, the fear of birth, of old age, of (the mind's) ills and of death no longer torments (one).
If you wish to overcome Jam and his kind, (then) praise (the Lord): that is well-being, that is the good deed to do.
In the present, the past and the future he is wholly imperishable; he is supreme, and ever in bliss.
Greed and the rest, the eye cast on another's home, conduct that goes against what is right,
give up all evil deeds and evil thinking, and run to the refuge of Chakradhar, the Holder of the discus.
The Lord's own devotees are wholly pure, in heart, in deed and in word;
what (is gained) by yoga, what by sacrifices, what by charity, what by austerities?
Repeat Gobind, Gobind, O man: (he is) the abode of all spiritual powers.
Jaidev has come openly to his (refuge), who in the present and the past reaches everywhere.
527.1: There is one God, Ik Oankar, the One who pervades all and is ever the same; his Name is Sat (the One who truly is); he is the Creator, the Being who dwells in all, without fear, without enmity, his form beyond time, unborn, self-existent, realised by the Guru's grace.
Raag Devgandhari, Ghar 1, by the Fourth Guru (Guru Ram Das Ji).
Those whose love is fixed on the Master have become his servants, his devotees.
(O Lord,) how fortunate, how very fortunate, are the faces of those who speak your praise by the Guru's teaching.
Maya's bonds and nooses snap when the love is fixed on the Name of the Lord, Ram.
The Guru, the Enchanter, has captivated my mind; coming face to face with him, I am lost in wonder.
All the dark night I lay asleep; with the least grace of the Guru, I have woken.
O God, beautiful Master of servant Nanak, no one else seems to me your equal.
527.2: Raag Devgandhari, by the Fourth Guru (Guru Ram Das Ji).
Tell me, in which lane can my Beautiful One be met?
O Sants of the Lord, show me the way, and I will walk close behind you.
She to whose heart the Beloved's words are sweet: this way of hers has become good.
Wayward and slight as she may be, she has pleased the Master; that beautiful one, bending low, has met the Lord.
The Husband is One, and all the companions belong to that Beloved; she who pleases the Husband is the good one.
What can poor, humble Nanak do? On whatever road pleases the Lord, on that road he walks.
527.3: Raag Devgandhari, by the Fourth Guru (Guru Ram Das Ji).
O my mind, let us utter Har, Har, Har with the mouth.
Dyed through the Guru in the deep red colour, (the soul-bride's) bodice, (her heart,) is soaked in the Lord's love.
I roam about crazed and distraught for the sake of that darling, the Lord.
If anyone brings me together with my dear Beloved, I am the slave of that one's slaves.
Win the favour of your own True Guru, the Being, and drink the Lord's Amrit, savouring it.
By the Guru's grace servant Nanak has found him: searching within the body, he has come upon the Lord.
527.4: Raag Devgandhari, by the Fourth Guru (Guru Ram Das Ji).
Now, beaten and weary, I have come to the Master.
Now that I have come into God's refuge, O God, save me or slay me.
The cleverness and the praise of the world: all of it I have burnt in the fire.
Let anyone call me good or call me bad: I have laid down my body (before him).
O Master, O God, whoever comes into your refuge, you protect in your mercy.
Servant Nanak is in your refuge, O dear Lord; O Murari (the Lord), keep (his) honour.
528.1: Raag Devgandhari, by the Fourth Guru (Guru Ram Das Ji).
I am a sacrifice to the one who sings the Lord's virtues.
I live by beholding, again and again, the sight of the Saadh, the Guru, in whose heart is the Name of Murari.
You are pure and holy, O God, my Master, present in all; how can we, the defiled, meet you?
One thing is in our heart and another in our mouth; we are luckless, and deal in falsehood.
Our outward mark is the Name of the Lord, the Master, but within the heart is wickedness upon wickedness.
Keep me as it pleases you, O Master; servant Nanak is in your refuge.
528.2: Raag Devgandhari, by the Fourth Guru (Guru Ram Das Ji).
Without the Lord's Name, a beautiful woman is one whose nose is cut off (disgraced),
as a son born in a courtesan's house is given the name of base-born.
Those in whose hearts the Lord, the Master, is not, are misshapen lepers;
as one without a Guru may know much to say, yet in the Lord's court he is fallen.
Those to whom my Master has been merciful touch the feet of the holy Saadhs.
O Nanak, joining the Sangat, the fallen become pure, and following the Guru, the True Guru, they are set free.
528.3: Raag Devgandhari, Ghar 2, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
Ik Oankar: God is One, the all-pervading Creator, realised through the True Guru's grace.
O mother, let us fix our consciousness on the Guru's feet.
When God is merciful, the lotus (of the heart) blossoms; let us meditate on the Lord for ever and ever.
Within is the One alone, without is the One alone; in all, the One is contained.
Pervading every heart and every place, the Lord, the all-filling Brahm, is seen.
So many servants and sages sing your praises, yet your limit is found nowhere.
O Master, Giver of peace, Destroyer of sorrow, servant Nanak is ever a sacrifice to you.
528.4: Raag Devgandhari, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
O mother, whatever is to be, comes to be.
God is absorbed in his own creation: here there is gain, there is loss.
Here joys bloom, there are sorrows born of vice; at times there is laughter, at times weeping.
At times the proud are smeared with filth, at times it is washed away in the company of the Saadh.
No one can undo what God has done; no second (like him) is to be seen.
Says Nanak, I am a sacrifice to that Guru by whose grace one sleeps in peace.
529.1: Raag Devgandhari, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
O mother, hearing (of it), I am filled with worry and fears; I am afraid.
(So) let me give up mine-and-yours and pride, and stay in the Master's refuge.
Whatever he says, that I accept as good; I speak no word against it.
May he not slip from my heart even for the blink of an eye; forgetting him, I die.
The Giver of peace, the perfect God, the Creator, bears with my great foolishness.
Without virtue, unlovely and of no family am I, Nanak; (yet my) Husband, the Master, is bliss itself.
529.2: Raag Devgandhari, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
O mind, sing the Lord's praise for ever.
As they sing, hear and repeat it, (the Lord) saves all, those within the castes and those outside them.
(The soul) merged in the One from whom it sprang only when it came to know this way.
Wherever this body was taken on, it never found a lasting stay.
Peace came, and fears and doubts were destroyed, when God became merciful.
Says Nanak, my hopes are fulfilled: in the Saadh Sangat (the company of the holy) I have given up greed.
529.3: Raag Devgandhari, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
O mind, may I please my God in whatever way I can:
becoming the lowest of the low, very low and very small, and humble, I call on him.
Maya's many shows are in vain; I lessen my love for them.
In whatever my own Master takes pleasure, in that I find my glory.
Slave of his slaves am I, the dust of his slaves' feet; I serve his humble servants.
All comforts and glory (lie in this): I, Nanak, live by calling on him with my mouth.
529.4: Raag Devgandhari, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
Dear God, by your grace I have cast off doubt.
By your grace everyone is my own: this is what I have come to see in my mind.
By serving you, millions of sins have been wiped away; the sight of you has taken away (my) pain.
Repeating the Naam I have found supreme peace, and torn out the sickness of anxiety.
Lust, anger, greed, falsehood and slander I have forgotten in the company of the Saadh.
The bonds of Maya have been cut by the Treasure of mercy; O Nanak, he himself has saved (me).
529.5: Raag Devgandhari, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
O mind, all my cleverness is at an end;
Nanak has taken the shelter of the Master, who does and causes all to be done.
Erasing self-conceit, we have come into (his) refuge; this counsel the Saadh (the Guru) gave.
Obeying God's command, (we) have found peace, and the darkness of doubt has lifted.
O all-knowing, wise Master, my God, I have sought your refuge.
O you who set up and pull down in an instant, the worth of your power cannot be reckoned.
529.6: Raag Devgandhari, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
O Lord, God of my life-breath, Giver of peace,
by the Guru's grace only a rare one has known you.
Your Sants, O Beloved, are your own; death does not devour them.
They have turned deep red in your love, intoxicated with the essence of the Name of Ram.
Great sins, millions of faults and diseases, O God, are struck down by your glance.
Asleep and awake they have sung Har, Har, Har; O Nanak, they have fallen at the Guru's feet.
530.1: Raag Devgandhari, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
That God I have seen with my own eyes, wherever I look:
the Giver of peace, the Giver to all beings, whose words are Amrit.
The Sants have cut away the darkness of ignorance; the Guru has given the gift of life.
In his mercy (God) has made me his own, and the burning (heart) has grown cool.
No religious rite or duty sprang up in me, nor did any pure conduct arise.
Giving up cleverness and self-discipline, Nanak has fallen at the Guru's feet.
530.2: Raag Devgandhari, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
Repeat the Name of the Lord, Ram, and reap the profit.
You will reach the high state, (know) peace, Sahaj (natural, unshaken poise) and bliss, and the nooses of Jam (the messenger of Death) will be cut.
Searching and searching, I have searched it out and reflected: (this profit) is with the Lord's Sants.
This treasure comes only to those in whose destiny it is written by (God's) grace.
They are the fortunate, they are the honoured, they alone are the perfect bankers;
O Nanak, handsome, wise and fair of form are they who have bought the Name of the Lord, Har Har.
530.3: Raag Devgandhari, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
O mind, why are you puffed up with pride?
Within (the body) are stench, impurity and filth; whatever is seen is ashes.
Remember him who made you, O mortal, who has given support to your soul and breath.
Forsaking him, you cling to others; you die and are born again, you ignorant fool.
(I am) blind, dumb, lame and without understanding; O God, the Protector, protect (me).
(You are) the Almighty, who does and causes all to be done; what is Nanak, a helpless creature?
530.4: Raag Devgandhari, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
That God is nearer than the nearest.
Hold him in remembrance and in meditation, sing the virtues of Gobind (the Lord of the universe), day and night, at dusk and at dawn.
Save this body, so hard to obtain: in the company of the Saadh, keep repeating the Name of the Lord, Har Har.
Let not a ghari, a muhat, not even a chasa (ever smaller spans of time) be lost in delay; death keeps watching you, day after day.
Pull (me) out of the dark hole, O Creator; what is there not in your house?
Give Nanak the support of the Naam, (in which are) bliss and peace in abundance.
530.5: Raag Devgandhari, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
O mind, whoever has met the Guru and worshipped the Naam
has laid the foundation of a life of peace, Sahaj, bliss, joy and delight.
In his mercy (God) has made him his own servant and cut away the nooses of Maya.
With loving devotion, singing the virtues of Gobind, he has mastered the road of Jam.
Grace was shown, the rust is gone, and the priceless treasure has been found.
Nanak is a sacrifice, a hundred thousand times, to my Master, beyond reach and beyond fathom.
531.1: Raag Devgandhari, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
O mother, the one who sings God's virtues
has come (into the world) to good purpose and gains the fruit of life; he keeps his love fixed on the Supreme Lord.
Handsome, wise, brave and knowing is he who finds the company of the Saadh.
He utters the Lord's Name with his tongue, and does not run through births again.
The all-filling Brahm pervades his mind and body; no other comes into his sight.
O Nanak, hell and disease do not befall the one whom (God) attaches to the hem of (his) robe, in the company of (his) servants.
531.2: Raag Devgandhari, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
The fickle (mind) is entangled in a mere dream.
It never grasps even this much, that it must depart; it has grown frantic in the company of Maya.
It revels in the pleasure of the flower's colour and company, and strives after one thing alone, Maya.
Hearing of something to covet, it takes it for joy in the mind, and rises and rushes there at once.
Wandering and wandering, it grew very weary, and came to the door of the Sant (the Guru).
The Supreme Lord, the Master, showed mercy; O Nanak, he has merged (it) into himself.
531.3: Raag Devgandhari, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
All peace lies in the Guru's feet,
(which) cast out the filth of sin and give the mind support; with this support I am to cross over.
Worship, offerings, service and obeisance: this service (of the feet) is all I have to do.
The mind blossoms, light dawns (within), and one does not fall into the womb again.
I touch the fruit-bearing form of the Sants; this is the meditation I am to keep.
Merciful has the Master become to Nanak; he has come to the refuge of the Saadh.
531.4: Raag Devgandhari, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
(O brother,) let us make our prayer to our own Lord;
(from him) are received the four great gifts (padaarath), treasures of bliss and joy, peace, Sahaj and the siddhis (miraculous powers).
Casting off pride, I cling to the Lord's feet; let us hold fast to the hem of that God's robe.
No heat from the ocean of fire touches (us) if we long for the refuge of the Master.
God endures, time and again, millions of offences from the utterly ungrateful;
the Supreme God is all compassion, perfect; O Nanak, let us seek his refuge.
531.5: Raag Devgandhari, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
(When) the Guru's feet came to dwell in the heart,
illness, sorrow and every pain were wiped out, and all afflictions lifted.
The sins of birth after birth are destroyed; (this is) millions of holy dips and bathings.
(I have found) the treasure of the Naam; singing the praises of Gobind, my attention has settled in Sahaj.
In his mercy (God) has made (me) his own servant, breaking (my) bonds and setting (me) apart, free.
Repeating the Naam, your Bani, again and again, I live; servant Nanak is a sacrifice (to you).
531.6: Raag Devgandhari, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
O mother, let me gaze on God's feet;
be gracious, my Master, so that I never cast (you) out of my mind.
May I put the dust (of the feet) of the Saadh (the Guru) on my face and forehead, and burn up the poison of lust and anger;
may I hold myself lowest of all, and keep this peace in my mind.
Let us sing the praises of the imperishable Master, (and so) may I sweep away all my sins.
May Nanak receive the gift of the Naam, the treasure, and, clasping it to his neck, keep it in his heart.
532.1: Raag Devgandhari, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
O dear God, may I see the sight of you;
may I fix my mind on (your) beautiful (form) day and night, dearer (to me) than life and breath.
I have looked into the Shastras, the Vedas and the Puranas, and pondered the essence of the Smritis;
O Master of the lowly, Lord of life, Perfect One, (you) are the one who lifts (us) out of the world-ocean.
From the beginning, from the start of the ages, the devotees and servants have had their support in him.
Nanak longs at all times for the dust (of the feet) of such servants; the Supreme God is the Giver (of it).
532.2: Raag Devgandhari, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
(O Lord,) your servant is drunk with Ram (the Lord), the home of all delights;
one in whom the treasure of love's delight has sprung up does not leave it to go anywhere.
Sitting, it is Har Har; sleeping, Har Har; the Lord's sweet essence is the food he eats.
He has taken the bath at the sixty-eight places of pilgrimage: he has bathed in the dust (of the feet) of the Saadh.
Fruitful is the birth of the Lord's servant, who has made the Creator a father blessed with a (worthy) son.
Taking with him all the multitudes, he is carried across; O Nanak, he has recognised the all-filling Brahm.
532.3: Raag Devgandhari, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
O mother, without the Guru divine knowledge is not attained;
(people) wander about wailing in many ways, (but) do not meet the Lord of the world.
The body is bound by attachment, disease and grief, and (one) is made to wander through many lives.
Without the Sat Sangat (the company of the true), (one) finds no resting place; before whom can one go and weep?
(When) my Master shows his favour, the mind is fixed on the feet of the Saadh (the Guru);
dreadful troubles are cut away in an instant, and, O Nanak, (one) merges in the sight of the Lord.
532.4: Raag Devgandhari, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
The Master himself has become merciful;
there is well-being, and all has become bliss; the children of Gopal (the Lord who sustains all) are saved.
Joining both hands, (I) made (my) prayer, and meditated in (my) mind on the Supreme Lord;
giving his hand, the Supreme God has kept (us) safe, and erased all sin.
United with the Husband (the Lord), the bride has sung songs of rejoicing, the Master's song of victory.
Says Nanak, let us be a sacrifice to the servant (of God) who brings deliverance to all.
533.1: Ik Oankar: God is One, the all-pervading Creator, realised through the True Guru's grace.
Raag Devgandhari, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
I made my plea to my own True Guru;
the Destroyer of pain became kind and merciful, and all my anxiety is gone.
We are sinners, hypocrites and greedy; (yet he) has borne all our merits and faults.
Placing (his) hand on (our) forehead, he has shaped (us) and honoured (us); the wicked who would destroy (us) have died.
(He) does good to others and sustains all; fruitful is (his) sight, and (he) gives Sahaj.
Says Nanak, (he) gives to those without virtue; I have enshrined (his) lotus feet in my heart.
533.2: Raag Devgandhari, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
O Master of the masterless, our God,
I have come to your refuge, O Protector.
Protect (me) on every side, O Murari,
in the world hereafter and in this one, and at the final hour.
Whenever I reflect, (it is on) your (virtues);
cherishing them, my mind finds its support.
Hearing the Guru's words, I sing (your praises);
I am a sacrifice, a sacrifice, to the sight of the Saadh (the Guru).
In my mind I keep one support (alone):
O Nanak, (that support is) my God, the Doer of all.
533.3: Raag Devgandhari, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
O God, this is my wish:
O treasure of grace, O merciful One, grant me (this): make (me) the servant of the Sants.
At early dawn may I fall at the feet of (your) servants, and night and day have the sight of them;
offering body and mind, may I serve (your) servants, and with my tongue sing the Lord's praises.
With every breath may I remember my God, and let us ever remain in the company of the Sants.
The Naam is my one support and my wealth; O Nanak, this is the bliss to be gained.
533.4: Raag Devgandhari, Ghar 3, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
Ik Oankar: God is One, the all-pervading Creator, realised through the True Guru's grace.
O friend, I have found such a dear Lord:
he never leaves and goes away, he is always with (me); meeting the Guru, I sing of him night and day.
I have met the Enchanter of the mind, the home of all peace; he does not forsake (me) to go anywhere.
I have seen many, of many and many kinds, (but none) equals a single hair of the Beloved.
In the temple (of the heart) there is good fortune, at the door there is glory, and the unstruck melody chimes softly.
Says Nanak, (one who has) settled for ever in the Beloved's home ever enjoys the joy of love.
533.5: Raag Devgandhari, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
My mind longs for the sight (of the Lord) and for (his) Name.
It has wandered through every place, O brother, and, longing, has now fallen in behind the Sants.
Whom shall I serve, whom shall I worship? Whatever is seen passes away.
Let us seek the refuge of the Saadh Sangat; the mind craves the dust of (their) feet.
I know no way (across), and have no virtue at all; Maya is so very hard to cross.
Coming to the Guru, Nanak has fallen at his feet; then all evil desire was lifted.
534.1: Raag Devgandhari, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
Your words, O Beloved, are Amrit;
O utterly beautiful, enchanting Beloved, (you are) within all, (yet) apart.
I do not want kingship, nor do I want liberation; (may) love for (your) lotus feet (dwell) in my mind.
Brahma, Shiva, the Siddhas, the sages and Indra (may be sought by others); for me, the sight of the Master alone.
Lowly, I have come to (your) door, O Master; worn out, I have fallen into the refuge of the Sants.
Says Nanak, God, the Enchanter of the mind, has met (me); my mind is cooled and in bloom.
534.2: Raag Devgandhari, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
Repeating the Lord's (Name), the servant has been carried across;
God, merciful to the meek, has become his own, and does not make him die again in (another) birth.
Let us sing the Lord's praises in the Saadh Sangat; (so) the jewel of human life is not lost.
Singing God's praises, (he) has crossed the poisonous waters of vice, and saved all his generations.
The lotus feet (of the Lord) dwell in his heart; with every breath and every morsel he has uttered (the Name).
Nanak has taken the shelter of the Lord of the world, and is a sacrifice (to him) again and again.
534.3: Raag Devgandhari, Ghar 4, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
Ik Oankar: God is One, the all-pervading Creator, realised through the True Guru's grace.
(Some) wander in the forests wearing holy garbs, (yet) Mohan (the Enchanting Lord) stays apart (from them).
(Some) expound and recite, and sing lovely songs, (but) harbour filth in their minds.
(Some) are very handsome, very clever and wise, with learning and a graceful tongue.
Free of pride, attachment and (the sense of) mine and yours: this path is (walking) the edge of a double-edged sword (khanda).
Says Nanak, that one has crossed the world-ocean (who has), by God's grace, the company of the Sants.
534.4: Raag Devgandhari, Ghar 5, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
Ik Oankar: God is One, the all-pervading Creator, realised through the True Guru's grace.
I have seen, O sister: Mohan is high, higher than all.
No other comes up to his level; I have searched a great deal, until weary.
He is utterly boundless, exceedingly great and deep; he has no bottom, and is high beyond grasp.
He cannot be weighed on any scale, nor bought at any price; where is the Delight of the mind to be found?
Countless have searched, many have practised austerities, (but) without the Guru none has reached (him).
Says Nanak, (when) the Master showed grace, meeting the Saadh (the Guru), I savoured (his) delight.
535.1: Raag Devgandhari, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
I have looked in many ways, O sister: there is no other at all.
He pervades all the regions and continents, and fills all the worlds.
He is beyond reach, utterly beyond reach; who (can tell) his greatness? Hearing of his glory, the mind comes alive.
(Those of) the four ashrams (stages of life) and the four varnas (castes) have been liberated, serving him.
The Guru has made the Shabad firm (within), and the supreme state is attained; duality is gone, and there is peace.
Says Nanak, the world-ocean has been crossed, and the Lord, the treasure, found in Sahaj.
535.2: Raag Devgandhari, Ghar 6, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
Ik Oankar: God is One, the all-pervading Creator, realised through the True Guru's grace.
O brother, know the Lord as One, the One alone;
O brother, through the Guru know him as One.
Why do you wander? Do not wander, brother; he pervades, O brother, he pervades every place.
As fire is in the wood, (yet) without the right method it does not get the work done,
(so) without the Guru (none) will find the door of the dear Lord.
Joining the Sangat and casting off pride, says Nanak, (one) has found the supreme treasure.
535.3: Raag Devgandhari, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
Where can I show (him) by any cleverness? Those who try to describe (him) are left wonderstruck upon wonderstruck.
The ganas (Shiva's attendants), the gandharvas (heavenly singers), the Siddhas and the seekers,
godlike men, the gods, Brahma and the gods like him,
and the four Vedas declare, by day and by night,
that the Master is beyond reach, beyond reach, and unfathomable.
Says Nanak, (his) virtues are endless, endless; (they) cannot be told; (he) is beyond the beyond.
535.4: Raag Devgandhari, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
(One who) meditates on the Creator and sings (his praises)
has no fear, (but) peace, Sahaj and bliss; O brother, he alone is the many: cherish (him), the One.
The Guru, whose presence bears fruit, (has his hand) upon my forehead;
wherever I look, there (he is) with me.
(His) lotus feet are the support of my life.
My God is all-powerful, fathomless and great;
the Master is near, within each and every heart.
Nanak has looked to the refuge and support of God, who has no end, no near shore and no far shore.
535.5: Raag Devgandhari, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
Turn back, O mind, turn back;
turn yourself away from the Saakat (one who has turned from God).
The love of the false one is false: it breaks off, O mind, it surely breaks off; in the Saakat's company there is no release.
As a house kept filled with lampblack blackens whoever goes into it, (so is the Saakat's company);
he has fled from it while still far off, the one whose trikuti (the frown of inner fretting) has left him on meeting the Guru.
O merciful one, treasure of mercy, I beg (this) gift of you: that my face may never be joined to a Saakat's.
Make servant Nanak the slave of (your) slaves; my head shall lie in the dust beneath the feet of the Saadhs.
536.1: Raag Devgandhari, Ghar 7, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
Ik Oankar: God is One, the all-pervading Creator, realised through the True Guru's grace.
O Bithal (God, who stands beyond Maya), I am a sacrifice, a sacrifice, (to those) who at all times are able (to show) the path:
your Sants, who sing (your praise) and are dear to you; may I lie at their feet.
O you who are all compassion, (they are the ones) who have no craving, who delight in Sahaj, whose place is in the One, the infinite, the incomparable.
Riddhis (wealth and plenty), siddhis and the treasures are in the palms of your hands, O Life of the world, Master of all, (you of) countless Names.
Show kindness, tenderness and grace to Nanak, that I may live by hearing your praise again and again.
536.2: Ik Oankar: God is One, the all-pervading Creator, realised through the True Guru's grace.
Raag Devgandhari, by the Ninth Guru (Guru Tegh Bahadur Ji).
This mind does not do even a little of what it is told.
I have given it counsel as best I could, and am worn out; it does not turn from its evil understanding.
Gone mad with the intoxication of Maya, it does not utter the Lord's praise;
practising deceit, it cheats the world and fills its own belly.
Like a dog's tail, it never becomes straight; it pays no heed to what it is told.
Says Nanak, worship the Name of Ram always, by which (life's) purpose is fulfilled.
536.3: Raag Devgandhari, by the Ninth Guru (Guru Tegh Bahadur Ji).
All of it is a dealing only of the living:
mother, father, brothers, sons, kinsmen, and the wife of the house as well.
When the life-breath parts from the body, they cry out aloud and call (him) a pret (the dead).
No one keeps (him) even half a ghari; they put (him) out of the house.
The making of the world is like a mirage (the deer's thirst): reflect on this in your heart and see.
Says Nanak, worship the Name of Ram always, by which deliverance comes.
536.4: Raag Devgandhari, by the Ninth Guru (Guru Tegh Bahadur Ji).
In the world I have found love false.
All are attached only to their own comfort, be it wife or friend.
Everyone keeps saying, mine, mine; the mind is bound by attachment.
Yet at the last moment no one is a companion; this is a strange way (of the world).
O foolish mind, even now you do not understand, though I have grown weary of counselling you day after day.
O Nanak, when (a person) sings the songs of God, he crosses the terrifying world-ocean.
537.1: There is one God, Ik Oankar, the One who pervades all and is ever the same; his Name is Sat (the One who truly is); he is the Creator, the Being who dwells in all, without fear, without enmity, his form beyond time, unborn, self-existent, realised by the Guru's grace.
Raag Bihagra, Ghar 2, Chaupade, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
Keeping company with the evil ones (lust and the rest)
they have laid waste to many.
That is why I have uttered the Lord's Name, Har Har,
and so I have found the peace of Sahaj (natural, unshaken poise).
(The mortal) is held by false attachment;
he calls what is other (than God) his own,
and stays caught in the whirlpool.
gathered together under one tree (the world),
and they lie in many bonds.
Ever abiding is the assembly of the holy,
where the Lord's Kirtan is sung.
Nanak has come to its refuge.
537.2: Ik Oankar: God is One, the all-pervading Creator, realised through the True Guru's grace.
Raag Bihagra, by the Ninth Guru (Guru Tegh Bahadur Ji).
No one knows the Lord's state (what he is);
yogis, celibates and ascetics have worn themselves out and given up, and many clever people too.
In an instant he makes a beggar a king, and casts a king down to beggary;
he fills the empty and empties the full: this is his daily way.
He himself has spread out his Maya (the world's illusion and lure), and he himself is the one who beholds it;
many-hued, he takes many forms, and remains apart from all.
He is beyond count, boundless, unseen and stainless, he who has set the whole world wandering in doubt.
Says Nanak, O mortal: cast off all doubt and fix your mind on his feet.
537.3: Raag Bihagra, Ghar 1, Chhants, by the Fourth Guru (Guru Ram Das Ji).
Ik Oankar: God is One, the all-pervading Creator, realised through the True Guru's grace.
The Name of the Lord, Har Har, is to be meditated on, O my dear soul; through the Guru the priceless Name (is found).
The mind pierced through with the Lord's essence is dear to the Lord; such a mind plunges and bathes in the Lord's essence, in the Name.
By the Guru's teaching the mind should be held steady, O my dear soul; (then) it does not waver anywhere else.
O Nanak, whoever speaks the Bani of the Lord God's virtues has found the fruit the mind longed for.
Whoever, through the Guru's teaching, has the Amrit (of the Name) dwelling in the mind, O my dear soul, speaks words of Amrit with the mouth.
The Bani of the devotees is Amrit, O my dear soul; it should be heard with the mind, with attention fixed on the Lord.
(Such a one) has found the Lord God, so long parted, who meets him in an embrace, in Sahaj and in love.
O servant Nanak, bliss has come into (that one's) mind, O my dear soul, and he sounds the unstruck (Anhad) Shabad within.
O my friends and companions, O my dear soul, may someone bring the Lord God and unite (me with him);
to that one I would give my mind, O my dear soul, who would tell me the story of the Lord God's praise.
Through the Guru ever dwell on the Lord in adoration, O my dear soul; (so one) finds the fruit the mind longs for.
Says Nanak: hasten to the Lord's refuge, O my dear soul; it is one of great fortune who meditates on the Naam.
Be gracious, God, and come and meet me, O my dear soul; through the Guru's teaching the Name shines forth.
Without the Lord I am forlorn, O my dear soul, as lotuses droop without water.
The perfect Guru has brought about the meeting, O my dear soul; the Lord, the Friend, the Lord God, is close at hand.
Blessed, blessed is the Guru: he has pointed out the Lord, O my dear soul, and servant Nanak blossoms through the Name.
538.1: Raag Bihagra, by the Fourth Guru (Guru Ram Das Ji).
The Name of the Lord, Har Har, is Amrit, O my dear soul; this Amrit is obtained through the Guru's teaching.
Haumai (ego) and Maya are poison, O my dear soul; by the Lord's Amrit the poison is washed away.
The withered mind has turned green, O my dear soul, by meditating on the Name of the Lord, Har Har.
By great fortune, as was written, the Lord is found, O my dear soul; O servant Nanak, (such a one) merges in the Name.
My mind is pierced through by the Lord, O my dear soul, as a baby clings to its milk.
Without the Lord no peace is found, O my dear soul, just as the chatrik (rain-bird) cries out without water.
Go and fall at the True Guru's refuge, O my dear soul; he tells of the virtues of the Lord God.
(The Guru) has united servant Nanak with the Lord, O my dear soul; in the home (of the heart) many strains of the Shabad resound.
The manmukhs (the self-willed) are parted (from the Lord) through Haumai, O my dear soul; they are bound in poison, in the net of Haumai.
As the bird, the pigeon, has had itself caught (in the net), O my dear soul, so all the manmukhs are in the power of death.
Those who fix their minds on attachment to Maya, O my dear soul, are manmukhs, foolish, out of step (with the true measure of life).
The Lord's servants come to his refuge, crying: save us, save us, O my dear soul; O Nanak, the Guru and the Lord are their protectors.
The Lord's servants are saved by keeping their attention on the Lord, O my dear soul; by great fortune, (written) from the beginning, they have found the Lord.
The ship is the Name of the Lord, Har Har, O my dear soul; through the Shabad the Guru, the boatman, has carried (them) across.
The Lord, the all-pervading Being, is merciful, O my dear soul; the Guru, the True Guru, has made him seem sweet (to them).
Be gracious and hear (my) prayer, O Lord, Har Har; servant Nanak has meditated on the Naam.
539.1: Raag Bihagra, by the Fourth Guru (Guru Ram Das Ji).
In the world the noblest deed is (God's) praise, the Naam, O my dear soul; hold the Lord's praise, the Lord, in your mind.
The Name of the Lord, Har Har, is pure, O my dear soul; repeat the Name of the Lord, Har Har: it carries (one) across.
(The Name) has cut away all wrongs, sins and sorrows, O my dear soul; through the Guru one washes off the filth with the Name.
By great merit the Lord is meditated on, O servant Nanak; (the Lord) has carried us across, foolish and witless as we are.
Those who meditate on the Name of the Lord, O my dear soul, have the five (passions) brought under their control.
Within (them) is the Naam, (like) the nine treasures, O my dear soul; the Guru, the True Guru, makes the unseen (Lord) seen.
The Guru has fulfilled (their) hopes and longings, O my dear soul; the Lord has been met, and all hunger is gone.
(The one) on whose forehead the Lord God wrote (it) from the beginning, O my dear soul, sings the Lord's virtues, O servant Nanak.
We are sinners and deceivers, O my dear soul, betrayers of others, cheats for the sake of Maya.
By great fortune we have found the Guru, O my dear soul; through the perfect Guru we have found the high state and the way to it.
The Guru has let the Lord's Amrit trickle into (our) mouths, O my dear soul; the one who was dying he has brought back to life again.
O servant Nanak, (the Guru) has taken away all the sorrows, O my dear soul, of those who have met the True Guru.
Supremely sublime is the Lord's Name, O my dear soul; by repeating it, sins are destroyed.
With the Lord('s Name) the Guru has made the fallen pure, O my dear soul; they have become known in all four quarters and in all four ages.
All the filth of Haumai is washed away, O my dear soul, from those who bathe in the Lord's Amrit, in the Lord's pool.
Wrongdoers and sinners are saved, O my dear soul, O servant Nanak, when for a moment they are dyed in the Lord.
539.2: Raag Bihagra, by the Fourth Guru (Guru Ram Das Ji).
I am a sacrifice to those, O my dear soul, whose support is the Name of the Lord, Har Har.
It is the Guru, the True Guru, who has fixed the Name firmly in them, O my dear soul; he is the one to carry (them) across the poisonous, terrifying world-ocean.
Those who have meditated on the Lord with a single mind, O my dear soul: those Sants win acclaim.
O Nanak, by repeating the Lord('s Name) peace is found, O my dear soul; he is the one who takes away all sorrows.
That tongue is blessed, blessed, O my dear soul, which sings the virtues of the Lord God.
Good and graceful are those ears, O my dear soul, which hear your Kirtan, O Lord.
Good, pure and holy is that head, O my dear soul, which goes and bows at the feet of the Guru.
Nanak is a sacrifice to the Guru, O my dear soul, who has brought the Name of the Lord, Har Har, to (his) remembrance.
Those eyes are good and approved, O my dear soul, which behold the holy True Guru.
Those hands are holy and pure, O my dear soul, which write the praise of the Lord, Har Har.
Ever worshipped are the feet of such a servant, O my dear soul, feet that walk on the path of dharma.
Nanak is a sacrifice to those, O my dear soul, who, hearing of the Lord, put their faith in the Lord's Name.
Earth, the nether regions and the sky, O my dear soul: all of them meditate on the Name of the Lord, Har Har.
Air, water and fire, O my dear soul, ever sing the praise of the Lord, Har Har Har.
Forest, grass, all that has form, O my dear soul, meditates with its mouth on the Name of the Lord, Har Har.
O Nanak, those are robed (in honour) at the Lord's door, O my dear soul, who through the Guru fix their minds on devotion.
540.1: Raag Bihagra, by the Fourth Guru (Guru Ram Das Ji).
Those who have not remembered the Name of the Lord, Har Har, O my dear soul, are manmukhs, foolish and ignorant.
Those who fix their minds on attachment to Maya, O my dear soul, depart at the end in regret.
They find no shelter in the Lord's court, O my dear soul, those manmukhs lured into sin.
O servant Nanak, meeting the Guru, (beings) are saved, O my dear soul; repeating the Lord('s Name) they merge in the Lord's Name.
All of you, go and meet the True Guru, O my dear soul, who fixes the Name of the Lord, Har Har, firmly within.
In repeating the Lord('s Name) one should not delay even a moment, O my dear soul; who knows whether the next breath will come or not?
Fruitful is that time, that hour, that moment, that instant, O my dear soul, in which my Lord comes to mind.
Servant Nanak has meditated on the Naam, O my dear soul; Jam's servant (the messenger of Death) does not come near (him).
The Lord ever sees and hears everything, O my dear soul; the one who has committed sins is the one afraid.
One whose inner heart is pure, O my dear soul, has thrown off all fears.
(One whose mind) is won over by the Name of the fearless Lord, O my dear soul: let all the wicked and quarrelsome rail in vain.
It is the perfect Guru that Nanak has served, O my dear soul, he who has brought them all and laid them at (his) feet.
Such a Lord should be served always, O my dear soul, who is the Master greater than all.
Those who have worshipped the One with a single mind, O my dear soul, are beholden to no one at all.
By serving the Guru the Lord's mansion is reached, O my dear soul; let all the slanderers and the cunning rail in vain.
Servant Nanak has meditated on the Naam, O my dear soul; the Lord had written (it) on (his) forehead from the beginning.
541.1: Raag Bihagra, by the Fourth Guru (Guru Ram Das Ji).
All beings are yours, and you pervade (them), O my Lord God; you know what is done in the heart.
The Lord is with (us) within and without, O my dear soul; he sees everything, yet in the mind one denies (it).
To the manmukhs the Lord is far away, O my dear soul; all their toil is wasted in vain.
Servant Nanak has meditated (on him) through the Guru, O my dear soul, (and so) the Lord is seen present (everywhere).
They are the devotees, they the servants, O my dear soul, whom my God holds dear in his mind.
They are robed (in honour) in the Lord's court, O my dear soul; day and night they remain merged in the True One.
In their company filth is washed away, O my dear soul; they are dyed in (his) love and bear the mark of his grace.
Nanak's prayer to God, O my dear soul, is this: that, joining the company of the holy, (he) may be filled and satisfied.
O tongue, repeat (the Name of) Gobind (the Lord of the universe), O my dear soul; repeating Har Har, craving departs.
On whom my Supreme Lord shows mercy, O my dear soul, in that one's mind he makes the Naam dwell.
One who meets the perfect True Guru, O my dear soul, obtains the wealth of the Lord, the treasure.
By great fortune one joins the Sangat (the company of the holy), O my dear soul; O Nanak, (such a one) sings the Lord's virtues.
In every place and in all between he pervades, O my dear soul, the Supreme Lord God, the Giver.
His end cannot be found, O my dear soul; he is the perfect Being, the Creator.
He cherishes all beings, O my dear soul, as father and mother their child.
He is not met by a thousand clever ways, O my dear soul; servant Nanak has come to know him through the Guru.
541.2: Raag Bihagra, Ghar 1, Chhants, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
Ik Oankar: God is One, the all-pervading Creator, realised through the True Guru's grace.
I have beheld a single marvel of the Lord, O my dear beloved: all he does, he does by righteousness and justice.
The Lord has set up the stage, the arena (of the world), O my dear beloved, and has made coming and going the lot of all.
Coming and going he alone has made, who created the earth.
Some he unites with the True Guru and calls into his mansion; others wander, lost in doubt.
(O Lord,) you alone know your limit; you pervade all.
Nanak speaks the truth; listen, O Sants: the Lord acts by righteousness and justice.
Come, my companions, and meet together, O my dear beloved, and adore the Name of the Lord, Har Har.
Serve the True Guru, knowing him to be perfect, O my dear beloved; (so) the road of Jam is made passable.
Making the hard road passable through the Guru, one wins honour in the Lord's court.
Those for whom the Creator wrote (it) from the beginning keep their attention fixed (on him) night and day.
Haumai, possessiveness and attachment fell away when (one) joined the company of the holy.
Says servant Nanak: adoring the Name of the Lord, Har Har, one is set free.
Gather together, O Sants, and join your palms, O my dear beloved; let us worship the imperishable Being.
I have searched out worship of many kinds, O my dear beloved; (now) let this mind and body, all of it, be offered (to him).
Mind, body and wealth all belong to God; what can anyone offer him in worship?
One to whom the Master is gracious and merciful merges in God's embrace.
One on whose forehead good fortune is (written) has love for the Guru.
Says servant Nanak: let us join the Saadh Sangat (the company of the holy) and worship the Name of the Lord, Har Har.
We roamed, searching in the ten directions, O my dear beloved; coming home (to the heart), we have found the Lord.
The dear Lord has built the Lord's temple (the body), O my dear beloved; the Lord abides in it.
The Master himself pervades all; through the Guru he has become manifest.
Darkness is dispelled and sorrow has fled; the Lord's essence, Amrit, has trickled in.
Wherever I look, there is the Master; the Supreme Lord is in every place.
Says servant Nanak: the True Guru has united (us with him); coming home (to the heart), we have found the Lord.
542.1: Raag Bihagra, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
Most dear is (the Lord), the enchanter of the mind; he shines in every heart and is the support of life.
The glory of the beloved, merciful Gopal is beautiful, boundless and beyond all limit.
O Gopal, merciful Gobind, my Beloved, my Husband, meet me, the lowly one.
My eyes yearn for the touch of your sight; sleep does not come, and the night wears on.
The collyrium of wisdom and the food of the Naam have become all my adornments.
Nanak makes his plea and speaks to the Sant (the Guru): unite me with my Husband.
As long as the Lord does not meet me, I bear a hundred thousand reproaches.
I try many ways to meet him, but no effort of mine prevails.
The mind is fickle and wealth does not last; without the Beloved, there is no solace by any means.
Food, drink and adornment are in vain; without the Lord, my Husband, how can one live?
Night and day I am full of longing and thirst; I cannot endure (without him) for even an instant.
Nanak makes his plea: O Sant (Guru), I am your servant; through your grace my Beloved is met.
We share one bed, my Beloved and I, yet I do not get to see him.
Countless are my faults; how can I be called into his mansion?
The worthless, lowly, helpless (bride) prays: O God, treasure of grace, come and meet me.
Beholding you for an instant, O God, Master of the nine treasures, the wall of doubt falls and one rests in Sahaj.
When the Beloved comes into her home, she attains his mansion, and joining with him, the song of joy is sung.
Nanak makes his plea: O Sant (Guru), I am in your refuge; show me the sight (of my Beloved).
By the grace of the Sants I have found the Lord, Har Har.
My wish is fulfilled, peace has come into my mind, and the burning within is quenched.
Fruitful is that day and lovely that night; great is the bliss, the joy and the delight.
Gopal, the beloved Gobind, has been revealed; which of his virtues can I tell with my tongue?
Doubt, greed, attachment and vice have ceased; joining with my companions, I have sung the song of joy.
Nanak makes his plea and speaks to the Sant (the Guru) who, through the destined union, has united (him) with the Lord, Har Har.
543.1: Raag Bihagra, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
Show mercy, O great and perfect Supreme Lord, that night and day I may utter the Naam,
utter the Amrit Bani, the Lord's praise, and that your will may seem sweet to me.
Show kindness and mercy, O Gopal, O Gobind; there is no one but you.
O all-powerful, indescribable, boundless, all-pervading one, my life, body, wealth and mind are yours.
(I am) foolish, ignorant, without support, fickle, powerless, lowly and unknowing.
Nanak prays: I am in your refuge; save (me) from coming and going.
In the refuge of the Saadhs the dear Lord is found, and (there) we sing the Lord's praises every day.
