Sing the Lord's praises always, with love;
you will obtain every fruit the mind longs for, and (the Lord will be) a helper at the side of your soul.
Narayan is the support of (my) breath of life;
I am the dust of the Sants' feet.
(These Sants) have made the fallen pure;
in their grace, they have given (them) the Lord's praise.
ever beside the soul as its protector.
Let us sing the Lord's Kirtan day and night;
(then) one is not cast into births again.
The one to whom the all-pervading Being, the Creator, gives (this gift):
that one alone has known the Lord's sweet essence.
Jam's servant has not come near (him);
O Nanak, (he) has found peace in (God's) refuge.
624.1: Raag Sorath, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
The Perfect Guru has brought everything to fulfilment;
God pervades all, filling every place.
The bathing has taken place in peace and well-being;
I am a sacrifice to the Supreme Lord.
With the Guru's lotus feet enshrined in the heart,
not the least hindrance befalls; all (my) affairs have been set right.
Meeting the Saadh (the Guru), (people) have shed their evil-mindedness;
the fallen have all become pure.
Those who have bathed in the pool of Ramdas:
all the sins they committed have been washed off.
Let us sing Gobind's praises every day,
and, joining the Saadh Sangat, meditate (on him).
That one obtains the fruits the mind desires
who meditates on the Perfect Guru in the heart.
The great Gopal is bliss itself;
repeating again and again (the Name of) the Lord of supreme bliss, one lives.
Servant Nanak has meditated on the Naam;
God has kept to his own age-old way.
624.2: Raag Sorath, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
In all ten directions the clouds spread like a canopy, bank upon bank; the lightning flashes and frightens (me).
(My) bed is lonely, there is no sleep in (my) eyes: (my) Husband has gone away to a far land.
Now no message (from him) comes, O mother.
(Once,) when my Beloved travelled even one kos, four letters would reach (me).
How could this dear Beloved be forgotten, who has every virtue and gives every comfort?
Climbing up to the rooftop, I watch the road (for him), and my eyes have filled with tears.
The wall of ego, of I and I, has risen between (us); I hear that he is near, in (my own) land.
The screen (between us) is (as thin as) a butterfly's wing, yet, unseen, he seems far away.
The Master of all became merciful and wiped away all (my) pain.
Says Nanak, the Guru knocked down the wall of Haumai, and then (I) found Bithal, the Merciful.
All (my) anxiety is gone, O mother;
the Guru has brought (me) to the one I longed for:
the King, the treasure of every virtue.
624.3: Raag Sorath, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
(O Lord, you are) the Restorer of what was lost, the Releaser of captives, the Formless One, the Healer of pain.
I know nothing of good deeds, nothing of Dharma; I am greedy, clinging to Maya.
(Yet) I have come to be called Govind's devotee: keep this honour, which is yours.
Dear Lord, you are the honour of those without honour;
my Govind makes the worthless precious; I am a sacrifice to your might.
Just as a child, out of fondness and its own nature, commits a hundred thousand faults,
and the father, teaching it, scolds it in many ways, and then holds it close again,
(so) God forgives past failings and sets (one) on the path for what lies ahead.
The Lord, the Knower of hearts, knows every state; to whom else, then, should one tell it?
Gobind is not won over by mere talk and telling; if it pleases the Lord, (one's) honour is kept.
I have looked at every other shelter; yours is the one shelter I keep.
God the Master, kind and merciful, himself hears the prayer,
brings (one) to meet the Perfect True Guru, and all the mind's anxiety ends.
The medicine of the Name of the Lord, Har Har, has been put into (my) mouth; servant Nanak dwells in peace.
625.1: Raag Sorath, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
Remembering God over and over, (we) have come into bliss; all pain and strife have fled.
Singing the praises of our God and meditating on him, all (our) affairs have been set in order.
(O God,) your Name is the life of all the world.
From the Perfect Guru (we) received the teaching; repeating (the Name), (we) have been carried across the terrifying world-ocean.
You alone are (your own) counsellor, O God, and you hear (all); you alone are able to do all things.
It is you who give and you who enjoy; of what account is this poor creature?
What virtues of yours could I speak of and describe? Your worth cannot be told.
Beholding his God again and again, (one) lives; wondrous is your greatness.
O God, my Master, showing your favour, you yourself have made (my) honour and understanding whole.
Nanak is a sacrifice for ever and ever; I long for the dust of the Sants' feet.
625.2: Raag Sorath, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
God has set right all (his) affairs.
The Lord has shown his grace;
(God) has become the helper of his servant;
the Creator has fulfilled every wish; nothing is left wanting.
The Creator, the all-pervading Being, has had the pool made;
So it pleases my Perfect True Guru.
Remembering the Merciful One again and again,
all beings have become kind (to me).
All acclaim to the Lord of the world,
who has made the whole design complete.
this treasure is your own gift.
Servant Nanak has meditated on the One,
and has received the blessing that bears every fruit.
625.3: Raag Sorath, Ghar 3, Dupade, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
Ik Oankar: God is One, the all-pervading Creator, realised through the True Guru's grace.
Those who have bathed in the pool of Ramdas:
all the sins they committed have been washed away;
this is the gift of the Perfect Guru.
God has bestowed all peace and well-being;
everything has been kept safe and sound, by reflecting on the Guru's Shabad.
In the Saadh Sangat the filth (of the mind) has been washed off;
the Supreme Lord has become (our) companion.
Nanak has meditated on the Naam,
and has found God, the Primal Being.
625.4: Raag Sorath, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
The (house of the heart) in which the Supreme Lord has come to mind:
that house the Master has made to flourish.
When (one) found the Guru, the Ocean of peace,
The glory of the Lord's Name,
the singing of (his) praises at all hours:
(this gift I) have received from the Perfect Guru.
The story of God is beyond telling;
his servants speak the Bani that is Amrit.
having come to know (it) through the Perfect Guru.
626.1: Raag Sorath, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
Ahead, (in the world beyond,) the Guru has given peace;
behind, (in this world,) too, the Guru has brought peace and well-being.
(I) have found all treasures and comforts,
(for I) have meditated on my Guru in (my) heart.
(Such is) the greatness of my own True Guru:
(through him) one obtains the fruits the mind longs for;
O Sants, (this greatness) grows more and more, day by day.
All beings and creatures have become kind (to me); God has made (them) his own.
Gopal has been met, naturally, in Sahaj; O Nanak, (they) have found contentment in the True One.
626.2: Raag Sorath, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
a watch kept all around us.
The mind is fixed on the Name of Ram;
Dear God, it is you who give me peace;
cutting away the bonds (of Maya), the perfect, all-pervading Being, the Creator, makes the mind pure.
service done to him will not go in vain.
repeating (your Name), (their) hope has been fulfilled.
626.3: Raag Sorath, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
I am a sacrifice to my Guru,
(I) have found the fruit the mind longed for,
(for I) have always meditated on my God.
O Sants, without him there is no other;
that God alone is the Cause of creation.
My own God has granted blessings,
and has brought all beings under (his) sway.
Servant Nanak has meditated on the Naam,
and so (he) has wiped out all (his) sorrows.
626.4: Raag Sorath, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
The perfect Guru has taken away the fever;
God has brought about every blessing;
he himself has given them, out of his mercy.
The True Guru himself has taken away the pain;
all the Sikhs and Sants, meditating on the Name of the Lord, Har Har, have become full of joy.
Whatever (your Sants) ask for, they receive;
O God, you (yourself) give to your own Sants.
servant Nanak has uttered (the Name of) the True One.
626.5: Raag Sorath, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
(O Lord,) have (me) do only what pleases you;
I have no cleverness at all.
We, (your) children, are in your refuge;
O Lord King, (you are) my mother and father;
in your mercy you have taken (me) into your care; I do what you have me do.
All beings and creatures are upheld by you;
O God, (their) string is in your hands.
whatever he has (us) do, that alone is done;
servant Nanak is in your refuge.
627.1: Raag Sorath, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
The Lord's Name has been threaded into the heart,
(and so) all our work has been done.
The mind of that one has become attached to God's feet
Joining the Saadh Sangat, (I) have meditated on the Lord;
at all hours (I) have worshipped the Lord, Har Har, and have found the fruit the mind longed for.
The shoot (of deeds) from lives long past has sprung up,
(and) the mind has become attached to the Name of Ram.
Staying absorbed, in mind and body, in the sight of the Lord,
servant Nanak sings the praises of the True One.
627.2: Raag Sorath, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
(Whoever), meeting the Guru, has remembered God
O Sants, the Master's refuge is the one that stands for ever;
all beings and creatures are in his hands alone; that God is the Knower of hearts.
God has kept to his own age-old way (of grace).
servant Nanak is ever a sacrifice (to it).
627.3: Raag Sorath, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
The Supreme Lord fashioned (this child) and made (him) fair;
the Guru has saved this little one.
the Supreme God is the giver of life.
you keep the honour of your servant, and set (his) affairs right yourself.
My God does good to others,
he who has set his full power (in all creation).
and has found the fruit the mind longed for.
627.4: Raag Sorath, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
Repeat (the Name of) the Lord for ever and ever;
God himself is the protector of children.
through the Lord's praise the dangers have gone.
My God has ever been merciful;
he has heard the prayer of his devotee, and has become kind to all beings.
God is the Cause of creation, all-powerful;
remembering the Lord, all pain has gone.
(He) has heard the plea of his servant;
O Nanak, all the world sleeps in peace.
627.5: Raag Sorath, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
(and) meeting (him), (we) have come home safe and well.
(This is) the glory of the Naam;
O Sants, worship the Lord, Har, Har, Har;
worshipping the Lord, everything is obtained: (so) bring all (your) tasks to fulfilment.
Loving devotion to God has taken hold (of the mind);
only that one receives (this gift) whose fortune is great.
O servant Nanak, (whoever) has meditated on the Naam
has found the fruit that gives every comfort.
627.6: Raag Sorath, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
The Supreme God has raised a dam (against misfortune),
(and) has broken up the camp of pain and disease.
God, the Lord, Har Har, has shown mercy.
O Sants, there is peace everywhere;
the Supreme Lord, the perfect Supreme God, pervades every place.
The Bani has come from God, the very source;
it has wiped away all anxiety.
The merciful Being has been kind;
Nanak has uttered (the Name of) the Lord, the True One.
628.1: Raag Sorath, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
Here and hereafter (he is) the protector:
God, the True Guru, merciful to the meek.
in every heart (it is he who) speaks the word.
I offer myself as a sacrifice at the Guru's feet;
day and night, with every breath, I keep in mind (God), who pervades all places.
true is the gift of the True One.
Devotion to you and your praise
Nanak has found in your refuge, O God.
628.2: Raag Sorath, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
When it pleased the perfect True Guru,
then (I) repeated the Name of Ram.
The Lord's feet ever give peace;
whatever (those who hold to them) wish for, that very fruit they receive; (their) hope does not go empty.
The one on whom the Lord of life, the Giver, shows mercy: that Sant alone sings (his) praises.
his mind is absorbed in loving devotion, and he is pleasing to the mind of the Supreme Lord.
With the Lord's praise uttered at all hours, the swindler's drug of the senses' pleasures has worn off.
My Creator has united (me) with himself; the Sants, the holy ones, have become (my) companions.
He has taken (me) by the hand, given (me) all things, and himself joined (me) to himself.
Says Nanak, every undertaking has been fulfilled: (I) have found the perfect True Guru.
628.3: Raag Sorath, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
(to be) the dust and ashes beneath the feet of all is (our) double-edged sword.
Before this no evildoer can stand;
the perfect Guru has taught this.
The Name of the Lord, Har Har, is the shelter of the Sants;
whoever remembers it is set free, and millions upon millions are saved.
In the company of the Sants (I) have sung (his) praise,
(and) have found this perfect wealth of the Lord.
(and) everywhere the Supreme Lord has come into view.
628.4: Raag Sorath, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
The perfect Guru has shown (his) full (grace),
(I) have found lasting bliss and peace;
(he) has made every place dwell in peace.
Devotion to the Lord gives (every) fruit;
the perfect Guru in his mercy has given it; only some rare one has known it.
Let us sing Gurbani, O brother;
it ever bears fruit and gives peace.
O Nanak, (whoever) has meditated on the Naam
has received what was written for him beforehand.
628.5: Raag Sorath, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
O Sants, repeating (the Name of) Ram, (I) have found peace;
(I) have come to dwell in the abode of the Sants in peace and Sahaj, and have wiped away all sorrows.
The Bani of the perfect Guru
is pleasing to the mind of the Supreme Lord.
(it is) the pure story of the One beyond words.
629.1: Raag Sorath, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
A hungry man feels no shame in eating;
just so does the Lord's servant sing the Lord's praises.
Why be slack about our own task,
the remembrance through which the face is bright in the Lord's court, and peace is found for ever and ever?
As the lustful man is lured by lust,
so the Lord's praise is dear to the Lord's servant.
As a mother clings to her child,
so the one who knows (God) practises the Naam.
(The one who) receives (this gift) from the perfect Guru,
O servant Nanak, (he alone) meditates on the Naam.
629.2: Raag Sorath, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
(I) have come home in peace and well-being;
ash has fallen on the slanderer's face.
The Perfect Guru has robed (me) in honour,
O Sants, this is the greatness of the True One,
who has brought about a wondrous glory.
the servant utters the Bani and proclaims God.
O Nanak, God is the Giver of peace,
who has made a perfect arrangement.
629.3: Raag Sorath, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
Meditating on our own God in the heart,
(we) have come home safe and sound.
Contentment has come about in the world;
the Perfect Guru has taken hold of (us) and carried (us) across.
O Sants, my God is ever merciful.
He does not count up the account of his devotee; Gopal protects his children.
Whoever keeps the Lord's Name enshrined in the heart
has set all things in order.
The Perfect Guru, pleased, has given (the gift of the Name);
since then, O Nanak, there has been no sorrow.
629.4: Raag Sorath, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
That same Lord has come to dwell in (my) mind and body;
This is the greatness of the Perfect Guru;
I am a sacrifice to your Name.
O my Beloved, the one whom you forgive sings your praise.
the Sants put their trust in you.
O God, Nanak has come to your refuge;
ash is on the slanderer's face.
629.5: Raag Sorath, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
Ahead, in the world to come, there is peace, my friend,
and behind, in this world, bliss: God has brought it about.
The Supreme God has made such an arrangement
(My) mind has come to trust the True Master;
(I) have known the Lord to be in all, through and through.
All beings are yours, O Merciful One;
Nanak meditates on the Naam every day.
630.1: Raag Sorath, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
Death's messenger does not come near (me).
Holding (me) close to his bosom, God protects (me):
(this is) owing to the True Guru's teaching of the Truth.
The Perfect Guru has made all complete:
he has struck down and routed all the enemies, and given his servant good understanding.
God has made all the places flourish;
(we) have come back in peace and well-being.
Nanak has come to the refuge of God,
who has wiped away all diseases.
630.2: Raag Sorath, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
The True Guru is the Giver of all comforts; let us fall into his refuge.
On receiving the sight of him bliss arises and sorrow has gone; let us sing of the Lord.
Drink the Lord's sweet essence, O brother;
repeat the Naam, worship the Naam alone, in the refuge of the Perfect Guru.
It comes to him alone for whom it is written from the start; he alone is perfect, O brother.
Dear God, this is Nanak's prayer: that I may stay with my mind attuned to the Naam.
630.3: Raag Sorath, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
The Lord, who does and causes all to be done, the Knower of hearts, keeps (the honour) of his own servant;
(that servant) is hailed throughout the world, and tastes the sweet essence of the Guru's Shabad.
Dear God, O Lord of the world, I have your shelter.
You are all-powerful, the Giver of refuge; at all hours I meditate on you.
O God, the servant who worships you has no anxiety;
touching the True Guru's feet, his fear is wiped away, and he has sung the Lord's praises in his mind.
O True Guru, those you have comforted (have) peace, Sahaj and bliss in plenty;
victorious, they have come home with honour, and their hope is fulfilled.
The Guru is perfect, and perfect is his teaching; the works of God are perfect.
Clinging to the Guru's feet and repeating the Name of the Lord, Har Har, Nanak has crossed the world-ocean.
630.4: Raag Sorath, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
The destroyer of the pains of the poor has become merciful; he himself has arranged everything.
He has saved his own servant in an instant; the Perfect Guru has cut through (his) fetters.
O my mind, let us always meditate on the Guru, Govind;
all troubles are wiped from this body, and one obtains the fruit the mind longs for.
The God by whom all beings and creatures were made is lofty, beyond reach, without limit.
In the Saadh Sangat Nanak has meditated on the Naam, and (his) face is radiant in the Lord's court.
630.5: Raag Sorath, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
day and night I meditate on him always,
who has given his hand and saved (his servants);
they have tasted the Lord's Name, the supreme sweet essence.
(I am) a sacrifice to my own Guru:
the perfect God, the Giver, has become merciful, and (all) beings have become kind (to me).
Servant Nanak has come to the refuge of the One
who has kept (his) honour in full
631.1: Raag Sorath, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
Hear (my) prayer, O my Master: all beings and creatures are upheld by you.
Keep the honour of your own Name, O you who do and cause all to be done.
Dear God, my Beloved, do a Master's part by (us):
bad or good, we are yours.
The almighty Master has heard the plea; cutting away (their) bonds, he has made (them) fair.
Dressing his servants in robes of honour, he has joined them (to himself); O Nanak, they have become known throughout the world.
631.2: Raag Sorath, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
(God) has made all beings and creatures subject (to his servants), and all (his) servants (are honoured) at (his) court.
God has taken his own as his own, and carried them across the world-ocean.
He has set right all the affairs of the Sants,
our perfect Master, merciful to the meek, kind, the treasure of mercy.
Bidden come and sit, (they are) honoured everywhere, and lack nothing in any way.
He has given his servants the robe of honour of devotion; O Nanak, God's glory has become known.
631.3: Raag Sorath, by the Ninth Guru (Guru Tegh Bahadur Ji).
Ik Oankar: God is One, the all-pervading Creator, realised through the True Guru's grace.
O mind, give your love to Ram;
let your ears hear Gobind's praises, and your tongue sing (his) songs.
Join the Saadh Sangat and remember Madho; (so) the fallen become pure.
Death roams like a snake, its jaws spread wide, my friend.
Today or tomorrow it will swallow you too; grasp this and hold it in your mind.
Says Nanak: worship Ram; the moment is passing.
631.4: Raag Sorath, by the Ninth Guru (Guru Tegh Bahadur Ji).
The mind's longing has stayed within the mind itself:
(he) neither worshipped the Lord nor served the holy, who are the true tiraths, and Death has seized (him) by the hair.
Wife, friends, sons, chariots, property, wealth, the whole earth entire:
know these and all else to be false; only the worship of Ram is real.
Wandering on and on through many ages you grew weary, and (now) you have gained the human body.
Says Nanak: this is your turn to meet (him); why do you not remember (him)?
631.5: Raag Sorath, by the Ninth Guru (Guru Tegh Bahadur Ji).
O mind, what evil understanding have you taken up?
You are wrapped up in the relish of other men's wives and of slander, and have not practised devotion to Ram.
You have not known the path of liberation, and have run about to amass wealth.
In the end no one has kept (anyone) company; you have had yourself bound for nothing.
You have neither worshipped the Lord nor served the Guru, and no wisdom at all has welled up (in you).
The Stainless One is right within your own heart, and you search the wilderness (for him).
Wandering through many births you have grown weary, yet have not gained a steady understanding.
Having gained the station of the human body, worship the Lord: this is the counsel Nanak has given.
632.1: Raag Sorath, by the Ninth Guru (Guru Tegh Bahadur Ji).
O mind, reflect upon the refuge of God;
Ganika was saved by remembering him: keep his praise enshrined in your heart.
By remembering him Dhru became immovable and reached the fearless state;
such a Master, the remover of sorrow: why have you forgotten him?
The moment he took the shelter of the treasure of mercy, Gaj, the elephant, was freed from the crocodile.
How far can I tell the glory of the Name? As he uttered Ram, his bond was broken.
The world knows Ajamal as a sinner; in the twinkling of an eye he was carried across.
Says Nanak: remember (God), the wish-fulfilling jewel, and you too will cross over.
632.2: Raag Sorath, by the Ninth Guru (Guru Tegh Bahadur Ji).
What means should a mortal take up,
by which he may gain devotion to Ram and shake off the dread of Jam?
Tell me: what deeds, what sort of learning, and then what dharma should he practise?
Which Name is it, O Guru, by remembering which one may cross the world-ocean?
In Kalyug the Name of the treasure of mercy is the one (way); whoever repeats it attains liberation.
No other dharma equals it; so the Veda declares.
He whom (people) call the Lord of the world is beyond pleasure and pain, ever untouched;
O Nanak, he dwells within you yourself, through and through, like (a reflection) in a mirror.
632.3: Raag Sorath, by the Ninth Guru (Guru Tegh Bahadur Ji).
O mother, how am I to recognise the Lord of the world?
My mind remains entangled in great attachment, in the darkness of ignorance.
I have wasted my whole life wandering in doubt upon doubt, and have not gained a steady understanding.
Night and day I have stayed attached to the pleasures of the senses, and (my) baseness has not left me.
I have never kept the Saadh Sangat, nor sung the praises of God.
In me, servant Nanak, there is no virtue at all; keep me safe in your refuge.
632.4: Raag Sorath, by the Ninth Guru (Guru Tegh Bahadur Ji).
O mother, my mind is not in my power.
Night and day it runs after the pleasures of the senses; by what means am I to hold it back?
It hears the teachings of the Vedas, the Puranas and the Simritis, yet does not let them dwell in the heart for a single moment;
absorbed in others' wealth and others' wives, it passes its life in vain.
In the intoxication of Maya it has gone mad; it has no inkling of wisdom at all.
The Stainless One dwells within the heart itself, (yet) it has not known his secret.
As soon as it came to the refuge of the Saadh, all (its) evil understanding was destroyed;
then, O Nanak, it remembered (God), the wish-fulfilling jewel, and the noose of Jam was cut.
633.1: Raag Sorath, by the Ninth Guru (Guru Tegh Bahadur Ji).
O man, hold this truth fast in your heart:
the whole world is like a dream; it takes no time at all to perish.
A wall of sand, though raised and plastered with care, does not last four days;
just so are these pleasures of Maya; you fool, why are you caught up (in them)?
Understand even now, nothing is lost yet; worship the Name of Murari.
Says Nanak: I have proclaimed to you aloud the Saadhs' own counsel.
633.2: Raag Sorath, by the Ninth Guru (Guru Tegh Bahadur Ji).
In this world (I) have seen no friend at all.
The whole world is bent on its own comfort; in sorrow (no one) stands by.
Wife, friends, sons and kin are all attached to wealth;
the moment they saw the man penniless, they all left his company and fled.
What am I to say to this crazed mind? It has given its love to these,
and the praise of the Master of the meek, who dispels every fear, it has forgotten.
Like a dog's tail, (it) has not become straight, though I have tried hard.
Says Nanak: (O God,) keep the honour of your age-old way; I have taken your Name.
633.3: Raag Sorath, by the Ninth Guru (Guru Tegh Bahadur Ji).
O mind, you have not taken up the Guru's teaching.
What of it, if you have shaved your head and put on saffron robes?
Leaving the True, (man) has clung to the false, and lost his life to no purpose;
by deceit he has fed his own belly, and slept like a beast.
He has not known the way of Ram's worship, and has sold himself into Maya's hands;
the madman has stayed entangled in the pleasures of the senses, and forgotten the jewel of the Naam.
He has stayed heedless, not remembered Gobind, and his span of life has run out in vain.
Says Nanak: O Lord, keep in mind your age-old way; mortals are forever going astray.
633.4: Raag Sorath, by the Ninth Guru (Guru Tegh Bahadur Ji).
The man who in sorrow does not feel sorrow,
who has no fondness for pleasure and no fear, who holds gold as clay;
in whom there is neither slander nor praise, nor greed, attachment and pride;
who stays aloof from joy and grief, (for whom) there is neither honour nor dishonour;
who gives up all hope and desire, and expects nothing of the world;
whom lust and anger do not touch: in his heart Brahm (God) dwells.
The man on whom the Guru has shown grace has recognised this way;
O Nanak, he has merged with Gobind as water merges with water.
634.1: Raag Sorath, by the Ninth Guru (Guru Tegh Bahadur Ji).
Know this in your mind, dear friend:
the world is bound up in its own comfort alone; no one belongs to anyone.
In good times many come and sit together (with one), and keep (him) surrounded on all four sides;
when hardship falls, all of them leave his company, and no one comes near.
The wife of the house, so dearly loved, who always stays close at his side,
the moment the swan (the soul) left this body, fled from him, crying, pret, pret (a ghost).
Such are the dealings of those to whom (one) has given his love;
at the last moment, O Nanak, no one but the dear Lord has been of any use.
634.2: Raag Sorath, Ghar 1, Ashtapadis Chautuki, by the First Guru (Guru Nanak Dev Ji).
Ik Oankar: God is One, the all-pervading Creator, realised through the True Guru's grace.
I do not fall into duality, I worship none but the Lord, I go to no tomb or cremation ground.
Caught up in craving, I do not go to another's house; the Naam has quenched (my) craving.
Within the home (of the heart) the Guru has shown (God's) home; it is pleasing to (my) mind, dyed in Sahaj.
You yourself are the Knower, you yourself the Discerner; it is you who give understanding, O Master.
Dyed in bairag (longing for the Lord), the mind has become a bairagi (detached from the world); my mind is pierced by the Shabad, O my mother.
Within is (God's) Light, the Bani through and through, and the mind is attuned to the True Master.
Countless bairagis talk of bairag, (but) he is the bairagi who pleases the Master;
(who), through the Shabad, is steeped in his heart in (God's) fear always, and does the Guru's work;
(who) remembers the One alone, whose mind does not waver, (who) checks it as it runs and holds it still;
(who), rapt in Sahaj, ever dyed in (God's) love, sings the praises of the True One.
If the mind, (restless as) the wind, dwells even a little in the Name, the home of peace, there is peace, O brother;
(his) tongue, eyes and ears are dyed in the True One; the burning (of craving) is put out: (O God,) it is you who have put it out.
The bairagi stays free of hopes, and sits in deep absorption in his own home (within).
Sated with the alms of the Naam, (such ones) are content; in Sahaj they have been given Amrit to drink.
In duality there is no bairag, so long as there is even a mustard-seed of other (hope).
The whole world is yours, you are the one Giver; there is no other, none second, O dear one.
Manmukh creatures dwell in sorrow always; to the Gurmukh (God) gives glory.
(He) is limitless, without end, unreachable, beyond the senses; (his) worth is not found by telling.
(He) abides in Sunn Samadhi, the Lord of the three worlds; (his) Name is the highest good of all.
On the foreheads of beings born into the world is a writ; each one bears the writ upon his own head.
(God) himself has (beings) do their deeds and good deeds; he himself makes devotion firm (in them).
By heeding (God's) fear, the filth of mind and mouth is removed; the Unreachable One himself (grants) wisdom.
Only those who have tasted (it) know its flavour, like the sweet a mute has eaten.
What can be said of the Indescribable, O brother? May I walk ever in (his) Will.
If the Guru unites (one) with the Giver, then understanding comes; one without a Guru has no understanding at all.
As he makes us walk, so we walk, O brother; what other cleverness can anyone try?
Some are led astray in doubt, some are dyed in devotion; your play is boundless.
Whatever you have set (beings) to, such fruit (they) have received; you are the One who moves (all) by your Hukam.
Had I something that was mine, I would serve (you) with it; this soul and body are yours.
On meeting the True Guru, grace has been shown, and the Amrit Name is (my) support.
He who dwells in the inner sky (the highest spiritual realm): in him virtues shine forth, and in virtues are (his) wisdom and meditation.
The Naam is pleasing to (his) mind; he utters it and has (others) utter it, and tells of the Essence of essences alone.
The Shabad of the Guru, the Pir, is deep and profound; without the Shabad the world has gone mad.
O Nanak, the one whose mind accepts the True One is the perfect bairagi, blessed with good fortune, (abiding) in Sahaj.
635.1: Raag Sorath, a Tituki, by the First Guru (Guru Nanak Dev Ji).
Hopes and desires are bonds, O brother, and religious rites bring bondage;
through sin and merit the world is born, O brother, and forgetting the Naam it perishes;
this Maya bewitches the world, O brother, and all (such) rites are vain.
Listen, O pandit, you who perform rites:
the deed from which peace springs, O brother, is reflection on the essence of the self.
(The pandit) stands up and recites the Shastra and the Veda, O brother, (but) the deeds you do are worldly;
by hypocrisy the filth does not go, O brother; within is the filth of vice.
In this way the spider perishes, O brother, hanging head down (in its own web).
Through evil understanding many have been ruined, O brother, led astray by the love of another.
Without the True Guru the Naam is not found, O brother, and without the Naam doubt does not go.
If (one) serves the True Guru, then he finds peace, O brother, and his coming and going ends.
Lasting Sahaj springs from the Guru, O brother, and the mind, made pure, merges in the True One.
He who serves the Guru understands, O brother; without the Guru the path is not found.
What do rites avail the one within whom is greed, O brother? Speaking falsehood, he eats poison.
O pandit, when curd is churned, O brother, the essence (butter) comes out of it;
churn water, and water is all one sees, O brother; this world is just such a thing.
Without the Guru one is ruined in doubt, O brother, (though) the unseen Lord is in every heart.
This world is a thread of cotton yarn, O brother, tied by Maya in all ten directions;
without the Guru the knot is not untied, O brother; (people) have grown weary performing rites.
This world is led astray by doubt, O brother; nothing can be said (of it).
On meeting the Guru, the fear (of God) dwells in the mind, O brother; to die in (that) fear is the true writ.
Bathing (at tiraths), charity, good deeds: (yet) in the Lord's court the Naam excels, O brother.
The Guru is the goad (that drives the elephant), who has made the Naam firm (within), O brother; (the Naam) has come to dwell in the mind, and the outward garb is gone.
This body is the Assayer's shop, O brother, and the merchandise is the infinite Naam.
That trader secures this merchandise, O brother, who reflects through the Guru's Shabad.
Blessed, O Nanak, is the trader, O brother, who carries on (this) trade in the company (of the holy).
636.1: Raag Sorath, by the First Guru (Guru Nanak Dev Ji).
Those who have served the True Guru, beloved: their companions (too) have crossed over.
No bar is put in their way, beloved; on (their) tongue is the Lord's Amrit.
Without (God's) fear, those heavy (with sins) have drowned, beloved; (God) carries (one) across when he casts his glance of grace.
Ever you alone are to be praised, O Beloved; ever, your praise (is to be sung).
Without the ship (of this praise) one drowns in the fearful (ocean), Beloved; where is the shore to be reached?
The Praiseworthy One is to be praised, beloved; there is no other, none second.
Those who praise my God are good, beloved; those dyed in the Shabad are coloured with (his) love.
If one gains the company of such a one, beloved, he tastes the sweet essence and, churning, (reaches) the Essence (God).
Honour is the pass of the True One, beloved, and the Naam is (its) true seal.
Whoever has come must write (this pass) and take it along, beloved; recognise the Hukam of the One who commands.
Without the Guru the Hukam is not understood, beloved; the True One's might stands for ever.
By the Hukam (a being) is conceived, beloved; by the Hukam (it grows) within the womb;
by the Hukam it is born, beloved, upside down, head first.
The Gurmukh is known in the Lord's court, beloved; he departs having set his task right.
By the Hukam (a being) has come, beloved; by the Hukam alone he departs.
By the Hukam he is bound and driven off, beloved; the manmukh receives punishment.
By the Hukam (God) is recognised through the Shabad, beloved, and (one) goes to the Lord's court robed in honour.
By the Hukam accounts are reckoned, beloved; by the Hukam are Haumai and duality.
By the Hukam (a being) wanders and is made to wander, beloved; robbed by its faults, (the world) weeps.
If the Hukam of the Banker (God) is recognised, beloved, the True One is met, and glory comes.
It is said to be hard to utter, beloved; how is the True Name to be heard?
Those who have praised him, beloved: I am a sacrifice to them.
May I gain the Name and be content, beloved; may I be united in union with the Gracious One.
If the body becomes the paper, beloved, and the mind is made the inkpot,
and the tongue the pen of Truth, beloved, then reflect on the Lord's virtues and write them down.
Blessed, O Nanak, is the scribe, beloved, who enshrines the Truth in his heart and writes it.
636.2: Raag Sorath, a Dutuki, by the First Guru (Guru Nanak Dev Ji).
You are the Giver of virtues, the Pure One, O dear one; (our) mind does not become pure.
We are offenders, without virtue, O dear one; that virtue (comes) from you alone.
O my Beloved, you are the Creator: having made (me), watch over (me).
I am a sinner, a hypocrite, O dear one: (grant that) the Name stand foremost in my mind and body.
The poison of Maya has bewitched the mind, O brother; by cleverness (one) loses honour.
The Master dwells in the mind through Truth, O brother, if the Guru's wisdom sinks in.
Call (him) beautiful, beautiful, O brother: beautiful, a deep crimson.
If the mind longs for the Lord, O brother, then at the door and in the home (of the heart) is the True One, who never errs.
In the underworlds and in the sky are you, O dear one; in every heart are you, (giving) the knowledge of virtues.
On meeting the Guru, peace is found, O brother, and pride has left the mind.
Rub and scour the body with water, O brother, and still the body grows unclean.
Bathe in wisdom, the supreme essence, O brother, and mind and body become pure.
If one worships goddesses and gods, O brother, what am I to ask of them? What can they give?
The stone (idol) is washed with water, O brother, yet such (stones) sink in water.
Without the Guru the Unseen is not seen, O brother; the world drowns, having lost its honour.
Glories are in my Master's hands, O brother; he gives them to whom he pleases.
The bride who speaks sweetly, O brother, and in love of her Husband speaks the Truth,
pierced by the pain of separation, dwells in the True One, O brother, and stays deeply absorbed in the Lord's Name.
Each one calls (God) his own, O brother; (but) through the Guru (one) comes to understand the All-wise One.
Those who are pierced (by love) are saved, O brother; the Shabad is (their) true seal.
Gather a great heap of firewood, O brother, and put in it a spark of fire, (and it all burns away);
(so) if the Naam dwells in the heart even for an instant, O brother, then, O Nanak, union (with God) comes with ease.
637.1: Raag Sorath, Ghar 1, a Tituki, by the Third Guru (Guru Amar Das Ji).
Ik Oankar: God is One, the all-pervading Creator, realised through the True Guru's grace.
Dear Lord, you ever protect your devotees; you have been protecting them from the very beginning.
Dear Lord, you saved your servant Prahlad, and destroyed Harnakhash.
The Gurmukhs have faith (in you), dear Lord; the manmukhs are led astray by doubt.
Dear Lord, this (keeping your devotees' honour) is your greatness.
Keep the honour of your devotees, O Master; the devotees are in your refuge.
Jam cannot so much as eye the devotees; death does not go near them.
The Name of Ram alone dwells in their minds; through the Name itself they have found liberation.
All the riddhis and siddhis cling to the feet of the devotees, who (abide) through the Guru in Sahaj and in love.
The manmukhs do not come to have faith; within them is greed and self-interest.
Through the Guru, the Shabad has not pierced their hearts, and they have no love for the Lord's Name.
The veneer of falsehood and deceit will come off; the manmukhs' speech is insipid.
You yourself are at work within your devotees, dear God; it is the devotees who have known you.
The whole world is in attachment to your Maya; you alone are the Being, the Creator.
(Those who) have killed Haumai, and whose desire has merged into the mind itself, have recognised (you) through the Guru's Shabad.
O God, you do the tasks of those who love the Lord's Name, and they are free of care.
By the Guru's grace he ever dwells in their minds, the One who sets all tasks right.
Whoever vies with those who have the Lord God as their protector is ruined.
Without serving the True Guru no one has found (him); the manmukhs have died babbling and wailing.
They come and go and find no resting place; in pain they are absorbed in pain.
Whoever becomes Gurmukh drinks the Amrit, and merges in Sahaj in the True One.
Without serving the True Guru the round of births does not let (one) go, though one perform countless rites in plenty.
(They) read the Vedas and expound disputes; without the Lord they have lost (their) honour.
True is the True Guru, whose Bani is true; those who run to the Guru's refuge are set free.
Those in whose minds the Lord dwells are true at (his) door; at the True door they are found truthful.
Their glory has shone in every age; there is no one who can erase it.
Nanak is ever a sacrifice to those who have kept the Lord enshrined in their hearts.
638.1: Raag Sorath, a Dutuki, by the Third Guru (Guru Amar Das Ji).
(God) himself forgives those without virtue, O brother, setting them to the service of the True Guru.
The service of the True Guru is sublime, O brother; (through it) the mind is fixed on the Name of Ram.
The dear Lord himself forgives and unites (us with himself).
We are without virtue, and sinners, O brother; the perfect True Guru has taken (us) in among (his own).
So many sinners has he forgiven, O dear one, through reflection on the true Shabad;
he has carried (them) across the terrifying world-ocean, O brother, putting (them) aboard the True Guru's boat.
From burnt iron they have become gold, O brother, as the Guru, the paaras, joined them in union (with God).
Once they gave up self, the Name came to dwell in their minds, O brother, and their light was merged into the Light.
I am a sacrifice, I am devoted, O brother; to the True Guru I am ever a sacrifice,
who has given (me) the treasure of the Naam, O brother; through the Guru's teaching I am merged in Sahaj.
Without the Guru Sahaj does not arise, O brother; go and ask those who have wisdom.
Serve the True Guru always, O brother, ridding yourself of self from within.
Through the Guru's teaching the fear (of God) arises, O brother; that fear is the deed to be done, true and sublime.
(Through it) the precious gift of love is found, O brother, and the True Name (becomes one's) support.
Those who serve their True Guru, O brother: I fall at their feet.
(Thus) I make my life worthy, O brother, and win forgiveness for my family as well.
The true (Name), the Bani and the true Shabad, O brother, come by the Guru's grace.
O Nanak, the one in whose mind the Lord's Name dwells, O brother, meets no obstacle at all.
639.1: Raag Sorath, by the Third Guru (Guru Amar Das Ji).
The dear Lord is known through the Shabad, O brother; by perfect fortune (the Guru) unites (one with him).
The happy soul-brides are ever in peace, O brother; keeping love (for him), night and day they are dyed (in it).
Dear Lord, you yourself dye (the soul) in your love.
Sing, sing (his praises), you who are dyed in his love, O brothers, with your love fixed on the Lord.
She who does the Guru's work, O brother, giving up self and fixing her mind (on it),
has Sahaj forever, and no pain touches her again, O brother; the Lord himself comes to dwell in her mind.
She who does not know her Husband's Hukam, O brother, is an ill-mannered, unworthy wife;
she does her work out of the mind's stubbornness, O brother; without the Name she is false.
They alone sing (his praises) on whose foreheads there is good fortune, O brother; through love of the True One (comes) detachment.
Dyed (in his love), night and day they dwell on his virtues, O brother; free of fear, they hold their attention fixed through the Guru.
He kills all and brings them to life, O brother: serve him day and night.
Why should he be forgotten from the mind, O brother, whose gift is so great?
The self-willed (soul-bride) is filthy and double-minded, O brother; she has no place in the Lord's court.
If she becomes Gurmukh, she dwells on his virtues, O brother, and meeting the Beloved she merges in the True One.
One who has not remembered the Lord in this birth, O brother: what face will he show on going (there)?
Even as the calls (of warning) were sounding, he let himself be robbed, O brother, lured by Maya.
Those who cherish the Name dwell in peace, O brother; their bodies are ever at peace and calm.
Says Nanak, O brother, cherish the Name of the Infinite, the Treasure of virtues, the Profound.
639.2: Raag Sorath, Ghar 1, Ashtapadis, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
Ik Oankar: God is One, the all-pervading Creator, realised through the True Guru's grace.
He who himself created the whole world, O brother, is the Cause of creation, all-powerful;
he who fashioned the soul and the body, O brother, giving (them) his own power:
by whom can he be told, how can he be seen, O brother? The Creator is One, beyond telling.
Let us praise the Guru, (who is) Govind, O brother, through whom the essence (of all) becomes known.
O my mind, let us repeat (the Name of) the Lord God,
who gives the gift of the Name to his servants, and destroys pain and suffering.
He in whose house is everything, O brother, whose storehouses are full of the nine treasures:
his worth cannot be put, O brother; he is lofty, unreachable and boundless.
He sustains all beings and creatures, O brother, and takes care of them day after day.
Let us meet the perfect True Guru, O brother, who through the Shabad unites (us with him).
Let the feet of the True One be served, O brother; (then) doubt and fear are destroyed.
Joining the gathering of Sants, let the mind be scoured, O brother; (then one) dwells in the Lord's Name.
The darkness of ignorance is dispelled, O brother, and the lotus (of the heart) blossoms.
Through the Guru's words peace wells up, O brother; all fruits are with the True Guru.
Let us give up mine and yours, O brother, and become the dust of all.
God (Brahm) is spread out in every heart, O brother; ever present, he sees and hears.
On the day the Supreme Lord is forgotten, O brother, on that day one dies in grief.
He is all-powerful, and does and causes all to be done, O brother; he is full of every power.
The Name is the precious gift of love, O brother, the end of attachment to Maya.
When it pleases him he unites (one with himself), O brother, and the Name dwells in the heart.
Through the Guru the lotus (of the heart) blossoms, O brother, and light dawns in the heart.
God's glory has become manifest, O brother; earth and sky are in bloom.
(The one whom) the perfect Guru has made content, O brother, is attached in love (to God) day and night.
With his tongue he ever dwells on Ram, O brother; (this is his) true relish and aim.
Hearing (the praises) with his ears again and again he lives, O brother; he has found the unmoving place.
One to whom faith does not come, O brother: may that wretched soul burn!
My Master has many virtues, O brother; I am a sacrifice to him.
He cherishes the worthless, O brother, and gives a place to the placeless.
He provides sustenance with every breath, O brother, he whose Name is of a deep colour.
The one who meets the True Guru, O brother, has perfect fortune.
Without him one cannot live for a moment, O brother; he is full of every power.
With no breath or morsel is he forgotten, O brother; I see him ever present.
In the Saadh's company (he) has united (me with himself), O brother, the One who fills all.
Those in whom love (for him) has not arisen, O brother, die in grief day after day.
Attaching (me) to the hem of his robe, he has carried (me) across the terrifying ocean, O brother, the world of pain.
In his grace he has looked on (me) with his glance, O brother; he has taken (my) side beyond measure.
Mind and body have become cool, O brother; the Name is (my) food and support.
Nanak (has come to) the refuge of him, O brother, who cuts away sins.
640.1: Raag Sorath, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
The mother's womb is an ocean of pain, O dear one; there (God) had (the being) repeat his own Name.
Once (he) brought (it) out, the poison (of Maya) spread, O dear one, and (he) made attachment to Maya grow.
The one on whom (God) himself has shown his grace, O dear one, he has united with the perfect Guru.
That one worships (God) with every breath, O dear one, with attention fixed on the Name of Ram.
In (my) mind and body is your support, O Beloved; in (my) mind and body is your support.
There is no doer but you, O Beloved; you are the One, the Inner-knower.
Having wandered through millions of births, (the being) has come (here), O dear one, suffering pain in countless species.
(Here) the True Master is forgotten, O dear one, and great punishment is received.
Those whom the perfect True Guru meets, O dear one, are attached to the True Name.
Following those who are in the true refuge, O dear one, one is set free.
What (one) ate taking it for sweet, O dear one, has brought disease into the body.
It turned bitter and settled in, O dear one; from it grief has sprung.
Feeding (beings) on pleasures, (God) has led (them) astray, O dear one; (their) separation does not end.
Those whom (God) has saved by uniting them with the Guru, O dear one, had their union ordained from the very Source.
In one steeped in greed for Maya, O Beloved, you never come into the mind at all.
Those who forget you, O Supreme Lord, O Master, their bodies have turned to dust.
They wail a great deal, O dear one, (but their) agony does not leave.
Those whom (God) has set right by uniting them with the Guru, O dear one, their capital is kept safe.
Do not keep company with a Saakat, O dear one, as far as it lies in your power,
meeting whom the Lord is forgotten, O dear one; such a one rises and departs with a blackened face.
The manmukh finds no shelter, O dear one; in the Lord's court he receives punishment.
Those whom (God) has set right by uniting them with the Guru, O dear one, succeed in full.
A thousand disciplines and clevernesses, O dear one: not one has gone along (with anyone).
Those who turn their faces from Gobind, O dear one, bring a stain upon their family.
(They) have not known the thing that is (theirs, within), O dear one; falsehood has not gone along (with anyone).
Those whom (God) has united with the True Guru, O dear one, cherish the True Name.
Truth, contentment, wisdom and meditation, O dear one, (come to the one) on whom (God) casts his glance of grace.
Night and day he sings his praises and dwells on his virtues, O dear one, filled to the brim with Amrit.
They have crossed the ocean of pain, O dear one; they have gone across the terrifying world-ocean.
Whoever is pleasing to you, you unite with yourself, O Beloved; they alone are ever genuine.
God is the all-powerful Being, the merciful Lord, O dear one; the devotees lean on his strength.
(The devotees) have fallen into the refuge, O dear one, of him who is the Inner-knower, the wise.
(He) has set right this world and the next for them, O dear one; on their foreheads is the true mark.
May that God never be forgotten, O dear one; Nanak is ever a sacrifice (to him).
641.1: Raag Sorath, Ghar 2, Ashtapadis, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
Ik Oankar: God is One, the all-pervading Creator, realised through the True Guru's grace.
One has read the holy texts and pondered the Vedas, and practised nivli and bhuangam;
(yet) the company of the five has not left, and (such people) are bound all the more by a proud intellect.
O dear one, (the Lord) cannot be met in these ways; I have done many (such) deeds.
Defeated, I have fallen at the Master's door: (O Master,) give (me) an intellect that discerns.
One has kept silence, lived as a karpati, and wandered naked in the forest;
one has roamed the river banks, the tiraths and all the earth; (but) duality does not leave.
Driven by the mind's desire, one has gone to live at a tirath, and had the saw put to the head;
but the mind's filth does not go in this way, though one make a hundred thousand efforts.
Gold, women, fine horses and elephants: one gives gifts of many kinds;
one offers grain, clothes and land in plenty; (yet) one does not reach the Lord's door.
One stays absorbed in worship, the worship of images, bowing, prostrating and the six rites;
(but) saying I, I, one falls into bonds; (the Lord) is not met by this method.
The yoga of the Siddhs, the eighty-four postures: one has done these too, over and over, till weary.
Living to a great age, one is born again and again, (for one) has not grasped union with the Lord.
Royal pleasures, the pomp of kings, issuing commands none can refuse,
a beautiful bed, sandal and perfume: (these are) the gate of terrible hell.
The Lord's praise in the Saadh Sangat is the deed above all deeds.
Says Nanak, it has come to the one whose due was written from before.
Your servant is intoxicated with this love.
The destroyer of the pains of the poor has shown mercy; this mind is dyed in the Kirtan of the Lord, Har Har.
642.1: Raag Sorath Vaar: by the Fourth Guru (Guru Ram Das Ji).
Ik Oankar: God is One, the all-pervading Creator, realised through the True Guru's grace.
Salok, by the First Guru (Guru Nanak Dev Ji).
Sorath is ever beautiful if the True One is in the mind,
if there is no filth (of slander) on the teeth and no rift in the mind, and that True One is on the tongue.
In her in-laws' home and in her parents' home (such a soul-bride) lives in the fear (of God), and serving the True Guru she is free of all hesitation.
If, putting off (the show of) fine clothes, she meets her Husband, the Husband gladly takes his delight in her, keeping her by him.
With the Name in her mind she is adorned for ever, and never is there the least speck of dirt (on her).
Her husband's younger and elder brothers have died in anguish; what fear is there now of the mother-in-law?
If she is pleasing to her Husband, O Nanak, the jewel of (his) grace (shines on her brow), and everywhere (she sees) the True One.
642.2: By the Fourth Guru (Guru Ram Das Ji).
Sorath is beautiful only then, when (through it the soul-bride) searches out the Lord's Name,
wins the favour of her own great Husband, and through the Guru's teaching utters the Lord's Name, Har Har;
and, drawn by the Lord's love, is steeped in the Lord day and night, her robe (the body) dyed in the Lord's colour.
No being like the Lord is to be found; I have searched the whole world and seen it.
The Name has been made firm (in me) by the Guru, the True Guru; (my) mind does not waver towards anything else.
Servant Nanak is the Lord's slave, and of the Guru, the True Guru, the slave of slaves.
642.3: You yourself are the maker of the world, O Creator.
You yourself set up the play, and you yourself have made it beautiful.
You yourself are the Giver and the Maker, and you yourself, O Enjoyer, (partake of all).
Your Word (your Hukam) is at work in everything, O Maker of all.
Through the Guru I praise you for ever; I am a sacrifice to the Guru.
643.1: Salok, by the Third Guru (Guru Amar Das Ji).
Burning in Haumai, (the people of the world) burned to death; those who, after wandering in the love of another, came (to the Guru's door),
the perfect True Guru saved, taking them into his own keeping.
Through the Guru's Shabad they came, of themselves, to see that this world is burning.
Those steeped in the Shabad have become cool, O Nanak, living by the Truth.
643.2: By the Third Guru (Guru Amar Das Ji).
Fruitful is serving the True Guru; blessed (is the server's) life, and approved.
Those who never forget the True Guru, living or dying, are the ones who are wise.
Such a one saves his own lineage; that person is approved.
The Gurmukhs are approved, dead or alive; the manmukhs go on being born and dying.
O Nanak, those who merge in the Guru's Shabad are not to be called dead.
643.3: Serving the immaculate Lord, the Purakh, let us meditate on the Lord's Name;
joined to the Sat Sangat of the Saadh (the Guru), we merge in the Lord's Name.
O Lord, set me, a fool, to your great task.
I am your slave, your servant; give me your command.
May I, through the Guru, do the work that has been made clear (to me) by the Guru.
643.4: Salok, by the Third Guru (Guru Amar Das Ji).
One must act out what was written from before (by past deeds), which the Creator himself has written.
He has given (the world) the drugging herb of attachment, and (it) has forgotten the treasure of virtues.
Do not think the world is alive: it has died in the love of another.
Those who have not remembered the Name through the Guru are not given a seat near (the Lord).
Pain, very great and heavy, has struck them; no one, neither son nor wife, will go along with them.
Among people their faces are blackened (in disgrace), and within they heave deep sighs.
No one puts faith in the manmukhs; all trust (in them) is gone.
O Nanak, great is the peace of the Gurmukhs, within whom the Name dwells.
643.5: By the Third Guru (Guru Amar Das Ji).
They alone are kin, they alone friends, who through the Guru meet (the Lord) in love.
Those who live by the True Guru's will night and day remain merged in the True One.
Those caught in the love of another, who act in pride and do wrong, are not to be called friends.
The manmukhs serve only themselves; they cannot set any task right.
O Nanak, one must act out what was written from before (by past deeds); no one can erase it.
643.6: You yourself brought forth the world, and yourself set the play in motion.
The three qualities you fashioned yourself, and you made the attachment to Maya grow.
(Living) in Haumai, one is called to account, and comes and goes again.
Those on whom the Lord himself has mercy have been given understanding by the Guru.
I am a sacrifice to my Guru; for ever and ever I give myself to him.
643.7: Salok, by the Third Guru (Guru Amar Das Ji).
The sense of owning Maya is an enchantress, who has devoured the world without teeth.
The manmukhs are devoured; the Gurmukhs, who have fixed their minds on the True Name, come through safe.
Without the Name the world is crazed and wanders; through the Guru this is seen.
Busy with worldly affairs, it has thrown away its life to no purpose, and has not enshrined the Giver of peace in the mind.
O Nanak, the Name has come to those for whom it was written from the very source.
644.1: By the Third Guru (Guru Amar Das Ji).
Within the home itself (the heart) the Amrit is brimming, but the manmukhs have not had its taste,
as the deer does not know of (its own) musk, and roams about, led astray by doubt.
Forsaking the Amrit, (the manmukh) gathers poison; the Creator himself has led him astray.
Few are they who have come to understand, through the Guru; to them God has been shown within.
Their body and mind have become cool, and the tongue has come to relish the Lord.
Through the Shabad alone the Name wells up, and through the Shabad (the Lord) has brought (them) into union.
Without the Shabad the whole world has gone mad, and has wasted its life in vain.
The Shabad alone is the Amrit; O Nanak, it is found through the Guru.
644.2: That Lord, the Purakh, is beyond reach; say, by what means is he found?
He has neither form nor feature, and is invisible; say, O servant (of the Lord), how is one to meditate on him?
The Lord is formless, immaculate, unreachable; what can we say as we sing his praises?
One to whom he himself gives understanding is set on the Lord's path.
The perfect Guru has revealed (him); through service of the Guru he is found.
644.3: Salok, by the Third Guru (Guru Amar Das Ji).
If the body is crushed in the oil-press and yields not a drop of blood,
if the soul is cut into four pieces for the love of the True One,
then, O Nanak, the union (with him) is not broken, by night or by day.
644.4: By the Third Guru (Guru Amar Das Ji).
My Friend is full of colour; he takes the mind and dyes it with his colour,
as cloth is dyed in madder once it has first been given the mordant.
O Nanak, this colour does not fade, and no other colour at all takes hold.
644.5: The Lord himself pervades (all); the Lord himself makes (all) speak.
The Lord himself, having fashioned the world, sets each and every one to work.
Some he joins to devotion, and some he himself leads astray.
Some he sets on the path, others he throws into the wilderness.
Servant Nanak meditates on the Naam, and through the Guru sings (the Lord's) praises.
644.6: Salok, by the Third Guru (Guru Amar Das Ji).
Service of the True Guru bears fruit, if one does it with the mind set on it.
The fruit the mind longs for is obtained, and Haumai departs from within.
(Such a one) breaks (his) bonds, is set free, and remains merged in the True One.
In this world the Name is hard to find; through the Guru it comes to dwell in the mind.
Those who serve their own Guru: to them I, Nanak, am a sacrifice.
644.7: By the Third Guru (Guru Amar Das Ji).
The manmukh's mind is unconquered; it goes and clings to another (than the Lord).
He has no peace even in dreams; (his life) passes in sorrow upon sorrow.
Pandits in house after house have grown weary of reading and reading, and Siddhas of sitting in samadhi;
this mind does not come under control; (people) have grown weary of performing rites.
Those who wear holy garbs have grown weary of putting them on and of bathing at the sixty-eight places of pilgrimage.
They do not know the mind's true state, led astray by Haumai and doubt.
By the Guru's grace the fear (of God) has arisen, and by great fortune it has come to dwell in the mind.
With the fear (of God) come, and Haumai burnt away through the Shabad, the mind has been brought under control.
Those steeped in the True One are pure, merging their light in the Light.
On meeting the True Guru (they) have obtained the Name, O Nanak, and are absorbed in peace.
645.1: These pleasures of kings and chiefs are lovely for four days.
This colour of Maya is the safflower's: it is bound to fade in an instant.
It does not go along when one departs; (one) must carry (one's) sins away on (one's) head.
When he is seized and driven off by Death, that hour is truly terrifying.
That time (of human life) does not come to hand again; then one can only repent.
645.2: Salok, by the Third Guru (Guru Amar Das Ji).
Those who have turned their faces away from the True Guru suffer pain, held in bonds.
They do not attain union (with the Lord); they are born and they die, again and again.
The sickness of anxiety does not leave them; in pain they suffer pain upon pain.
O Nanak, if the Lord of grace forgives them, they are brought into union (with him) through the Shabad.
645.3: By the Third Guru (Guru Amar Das Ji).
Those who have turned their faces away from the True Guru have no shelter and no resting place.
(They are) like a cast-off wife of ill conduct, who wanders from house to house with a bad name.
O Nanak, those who are forgiven through the Guru are brought into union with the True Guru.
645.4: Those who serve the True Murari (the Lord) have crossed the world-ocean.
Those who utter the Name of the Lord, Har Har, are let go by Jam.
Those who have repeated the Lord's Name go to the Lord's court robed in honour.
They alone serve the Lord on whom, O Lord, is your mercy.
May I sing your praises day after day, O Beloved; through the Guru, (my) doubt and fear have gone.
645.5: Salok, by the Third Guru (Guru Amar Das Ji).
In the plate three things have been laid, and this is the Lord's food, the sublime Amrit,
eating which the mind is sated and the door of liberation is found.
This food is hard to find, O Sants; it is found through reflection on the Guru('s teaching).
Why should this Mudavani (riddle) be cast out from within? Let it be kept ever enshrined in the heart.
This Mudavani has been set by the True Guru; the Guru's Sikhs have searched it out and found it.
O Nanak, the one to whom (the Lord) gives understanding will understand; through the Guru, by hard toil, he has found the Lord.
645.6: By the Third Guru (Guru Amar Das Ji).
Those united (by the Lord) from the very source stay united, fixing their minds on the True Guru.
Those he himself has parted (from him) stay parted, led astray by the love of another.
O Nanak, without (the Lord's) grace what can be obtained? One acts out what was written from before.
645.7: Sitting together, the singing friends sing (the Lord's) glory.
Praise the Lord's Name every day, (they say,) and they are a sacrifice to the Lord.
To those who have listened to the Lord's Name and accepted it, I give myself in sacrifice.
The Gurmukh (friends) are those who bring (one) into union with the Lord.
Day and night I am a sacrifice to those who behold the Guru.
645.8: Salok, by the Third Guru (Guru Amar Das Ji).
Without the Name all wander astray; in the world they suffer loss every day.
The manmukhs do their deeds in Haumai, in blind darkness.
O Nanak, the Gurmukhs drink the Amrit, reflecting on the Shabad.
646.1: By the Third Guru (Guru Amar Das Ji).
(The Gurmukh) wakes in Sahaj and sleeps in Sahaj;
within the Gurmukh, praise (of the Lord) goes on night and day.
The manmukh wanders about, gripped by dread;
with anxiety within him, he gets no sleep.
Those who know (God) wake and sleep in (his) love.
Nanak is a sacrifice to those who are dyed in the Naam.
646.2: They meditate on the Lord's Name who are dyed in the Lord('s love).
They meditate on the one Lord, the One, the sole Lord, who is ever true.
The one Lord alone pervades (all); the One alone has created (all).
Those who meditate on the Lord's Name have cast off fear.
(God) himself gives (this gift) through the Guru's teaching, and through the Guru (they) have repeated the Lord's Name.
646.3: Salok, by the Third Guru (Guru Amar Das Ji).
The (divine) knowledge through which some understanding might be gained has not come within;
without seeing (him), what praise can one give? The blind one does only blind deeds.
O Nanak, if the Shabad is recognised, the Naam comes and dwells in the mind.
646.4: By the Third Guru (Guru Amar Das Ji).
The Bani is one, the Guru is one; reflect on the one Shabad alone.
(This is) the true merchandise and the true shop, its storehouses filled with jewels.
They are obtained by the Guru's grace, if the Giver gives.
(Whoever deals in) the true merchandise has earned the profit that lasts for ever: the infinite Naam.
In the midst of poison the Amrit has been revealed; the One who gives it to drink gives it by his grace.
O Nanak, let us praise the True One: blessed is he who sets (all) right.
646.5: Those within whom falsehood prevails do not like the truth.
If someone speaks the truth, the false one burns (with rage).
The false one is sated by falsehood, as the crow eats filth.
The one on whom the Lord is merciful meditates on the Naam.
When the Lord's Name is worshipped through the Guru, falsehood and sin are washed away.
646.6: Salok, by the Third Guru (Guru Amar Das Ji).
O Sheikh, running to the four quarters, tossed by the four winds, bring this mind to rest in the one home.
Leave your talk of this and that, and recognise the Guru's Shabad.
Fall down before the True Guru: the Knower knows everything.
Burn away hope and desire, and live as a guest (in this world).
If you also walk in the True Guru's will, you will receive honour in the Lord's court.
O Nanak, those who do not remember the Naam: cursed is their wearing, cursed their eating.
646.7: By the Third Guru (Guru Amar Das Ji).
The Lord's virtues never run short, and their worth cannot be told.
O Nanak, the Gurmukhs dwell on the Lord's virtues, and (such a one) stays merged in (those) virtues.
646.8: The Lord has fashioned the body as a bodice; embroidered with devotion, it is worn.
The silk of the Lord('s Name) is worked into it in abundance, in many, many ways and patterns.
Some rare one who understands grasps (this), weighing it with discernment within.
He alone understands this discernment whom the Lord himself makes understand.
Servant Nanak speaks this thought: through the Guru (it is known that) the Lord is true, the Lord (alone).
647.1: Salok, by the Third Guru (Guru Amar Das Ji).
The great souls speak (their) teaching with someone in view, (yet) it belongs to the whole world.
Whoever becomes Gurmukh keeps the fear (of God), and recognises his own self.
When by the Guru's grace one dies while yet alive, then the mind is won over through the mind itself.
O Nanak, those whose mind has no faith: what can they say of (divine) knowledge?
647.2: By the Third Guru (Guru Amar Das Ji).
Those who have not fixed their mind (on the Lord) through the Guru: in the end pain has come upon them.
Blind within and without, they gain no understanding at all.
O Pandit, the whole world eats by the blessing of those who are dyed in the Lord's Name,
who have praised (him) through the Guru's Shabad, and stay merged in the Lord.
O Pandit, in the love of another there is no blessing, nor does the wealth (of the Naam) come into one's hands.
They have grown weary of reading, but contentment has not come; night and day (their life) passes in burning.
Their cries and complaints do not end, nor does doubt leave from within.
O Nanak, bereft of the Naam, one rises and departs with a blackened face.
647.3: O beloved Lord, bring me to meet (your) friends, so that meeting them I may ask the way (to you).
Whoever tells me of the Lord, my Friend, to him I am a sacrifice.
With them I would make a partnership of virtues, and meditate on the Lord's Name.
I would serve the beloved Lord every day, and serving the Lord, find peace.
I am a sacrifice to that True Guru who has given (me) this understanding.
647.4: Salok, by the Third Guru (Guru Amar Das Ji).
The Pandit's filth is not removed, even if he reads the Vedas for four ages.
Maya of the three qualities is the root (of it); in Haumai he forgets the Naam.
The Pandits have strayed; they cling to another (than God), to the trade of Maya.
Within them is craving and hunger; the ignorant fools die hungry.
When the True Guru is served, peace is found, through reflection on the true Shabad.
Craving and hunger have gone from within, through love for the True Name.
O Nanak, those dyed in the Naam, who have kept the Lord enshrined in the heart, are sated in Sahaj.
647.5: By the Third Guru (Guru Amar Das Ji).
The manmukh has not served the Lord's Name, (so) great pain has come and struck (him).
Within (him) is the darkness of ignorance; he gains no understanding at all.
In the stubbornness of his mind he did not sow (the seed of the Naam) in Sahaj; hungry, what will he eat hereafter?
He has forgotten the treasure of the Naam, and gone and attached himself to another.
O Nanak, through the Guru glories are received, if (the Lord) himself brings (one) into union (with him).
647.6: The tongue that sings the Lord's praise, (uttering) Har, is truly beautiful.
The (tongue) that utters the Lord with mind, body and mouth is dear to the Lord.
The (tongue) that tastes the flavour (of the Naam) through the Guru is satisfied.
It sings the virtues of the Beloved every day, and singing (his) virtues, makes (others) understand the Virtuous One.
The (tongue) on which (the Lord) himself is merciful calls out: True Guru, Guru.
647.7: Salok, by the Third Guru (Guru Amar Das Ji).
As the goad is over the elephant's head, as the anvil gives its head (to the hammer),
so (the servant) places mind and body before (the Guru), and serves standing (at the ready).
In this way, through the Guru, self-conceit is cast off, and (one) takes the rule of the whole world.
O Nanak, through the Guru this is understood, when (the Lord) himself casts his glance of grace.
648.1: By the Third Guru (Guru Amar Das Ji).
Those who have meditated on the Naam through the Guru: approved is their coming (into the world).
O Nanak, they save their own family, and receive honour in the Lord's court.
648.2: The Guru has brought together the Gurmukh companions, his Sikhs.
Some serve beside the Guru; others the Guru has set to (his) work.
Those who hold the beloved Guru in mind and heart, the Guru has blessed with love.
The Guru has one and the same love for his Sikhs, for friends, sons and brothers.
All of you, say Guru, True Guru: saying Guru, (the Sikhs) have been given life by the Guru.
648.3: Salok, by the Third Guru (Guru Amar Das Ji).
O Nanak, those who do not remember the Naam, the ignorant and blind, do other deeds.
Bound at Jam's door they are beaten, and then they rot in filth.
648.4: By the Third Guru (Guru Amar Das Ji).
O Nanak, those who serve their True Guru are true and approved.
They remain merged in the Lord's Name, and their coming and going is ended.
648.5: Wealth, riches and Maya are amassed, but in the end they bring pain.
Houses, mansions and palaces are adorned, (but) nothing goes along (at the end).
Horses of every colour are kept and tended every day, (but) none of it is of any use.
O people, fix your mind on the Lord's Name: at the end it will be your companion.
O servant Nanak, (whoever) has meditated on the Naam finds peace through the Guru.
648.6: Salok, by the Third Guru (Guru Amar Das Ji).
Without (his) grace the Name is not obtained; it is obtained through perfect grace.
O Nanak, should (the Lord) cast his glance of grace, then through the Guru's teaching he brings (one) into union (with him).
648.7: By the First Guru (Guru Nanak Dev Ji).
Some (of the dead) are burnt, some buried, some eaten by dogs;
some are cast into water, and some again are laid in a hasan.
O Nanak, from this it is not known where (the souls) go and merge.
648.8: Pure is all that they eat and wear, and (all) their wealth, who are dyed in the Lord's Name.
Pure are all their houses, mansions, palaces and inns, where the Gurmukh servants, the Sikhs and wayfaring guests go and take their ease.
Pure are all their horses, saddles and saddle-cloths, on which the Gurmukh Sikhs, the Saadhs and the Sants mount and ride.
Pure are all the deeds, duties and works of those who speak the Name of the Lord, Har Har, Ram, the ever-true Lord.
Those who have merit in their store, those Gurmukh Sikhs, go to the Guru.
648.9: Salok, by the Third Guru (Guru Amar Das Ji).
O Nanak, for those who have strayed from the Name, this world and the next are all lost.
All their chanting, austerity and self-discipline is stolen away; (the soul) is robbed through the love of another.
Bound at Jam's door they are beaten, and receive severe punishment.
649.1: By the Third Guru (Guru Amar Das Ji).
(The slanderers) bear enmity towards the Sants, and love and cling to the wicked.
Neither hereafter nor here do they find peace; they die and are born again and again.
Their craving is never quenched; through duality they are ruined.
Blackened are the faces of those slanderers in that true court.
O Nanak, those bereft of the Naam (find a place) neither on this shore nor on the far one.
649.2: Those who meditate on the Lord's Name are dyed within their minds in the Name of the Lord, Har Har.
Those who have worshipped the One with mind and heart have none other but the One.
They alone serve the Lord on whose foreheads the writ was written by the Lord from the start.
They sing the Lord's virtues every day, and singing the Lord's virtues, make (others) understand the Virtuous One.
Great is the Gurmukhs' glory: through the perfect Guru they merge in the Lord's Name.
649.3: Salok, by the Third Guru (Guru Amar Das Ji).
Service of the True Guru is hard: one must give one's head, giving up the self.
Those who die through the Shabad do not die again; then all their service is accepted.
Touching the paaras, one becomes the paaras, and stays attuned in love to the True One.
The one for whom it was written from before: the True Guru meets him, and God comes and meets him.
O Nanak, by keeping account (of service) the servant does not meet (the Lord); whomever he forgives is accepted.
649.4: By the Third Guru (Guru Amar Das Ji).
In their own self-interest, the fools cannot tell the mansion (the true abode) from a false one.
If they recognise the Shabad, they find the mansion, and their light merges in the Light.
When the fear of the True One ever dwells in the mind, one gains all understanding.
The True Guru dwells in his own home, and he himself unites (the seeker with the Lord).
O Nanak, on meeting the True Guru, all is fulfilled for the one on whom (God), in his will, shows grace.
649.5: Blessed, blessed is the fortune of those devotees who utter the Lord's Name with their mouths.
Blessed, blessed is the fortune of those Sants who hear the Lord's praise with their ears.
Blessed, blessed is the fortune of those holy ones who sing the Lord's Kirtan and so become virtuous.
Blessed, blessed is the fortune of those Gurmukhs who take the Guru's teaching and conquer the mind.
The fortune of the Guru's Sikhs is the greatest of all: the Sikhs who fall at the Guru's feet.
649.6: Salok, by the Third Guru (Guru Amar Das Ji).
Whoever knows Brahm, God, attuning himself to the one Shabad, keeps his Brahminhood.
The nine treasures and the eighteen siddhis follow behind the one who keeps the Lord ever enshrined in the heart.
The Name is not found without the True Guru; reflect on this and understand.
O Nanak, the one who meets the True Guru by perfect fortune finds peace through the four ages.
649.7: By the Third Guru (Guru Amar Das Ji).
Be he young or old, the manmukh's thirst and hunger do not leave him.
The Gurmukhs, dyed in the Shabad, have shed self and become cool and calm.
Their inner being is sated and content, and hunger does not come upon them again.
O Nanak, whatever the Gurmukhs do is accepted; they remain attuned in love to the Name.
650.1: I am a sacrifice to the Sikhs who are Gurmukhs.
Those who meditate on the Lord's Name: may I behold the sight of them.
Hearing the Kirtan, may I sing the Lord's virtues and write the Lord's praise upon my mind.
With love may I praise the Lord's Name and destroy all my sins.
Blessed, blessed and beautiful is that body, that place, where my Guru sets his foot.
650.2: Salok, by the Third Guru (Guru Amar Das Ji).
Without the Guru there is no wisdom, nor does peace come to dwell in the mind.
O Nanak, bereft of the Naam, the manmukhs will depart, having wasted their lives.
650.3: By the Third Guru (Guru Amar Das Ji).
The Siddhas and the seekers all search for the Name, and have worn themselves out in concentration.
Without the True Guru no one has found it; through the Guru one meets (the Lord), brought into union (by him).
Without the Name, all one wears and eats is in vain; cursed is (such) siddhi, cursed (such) miracle.
That is the siddhi, that the miracle, when the Carefree Lord grants someone (the) gift (of the Name).
O Nanak, through the Guru the Lord's Name dwells in the mind: this is the siddhi, this the miracle.
650.4: We are minstrels (dhadhis) of the Lord God, our Master; every day we sing songs of the Lord's virtues.
We sing the Kirtan of the Lord and hear the praise of the Lord, the Husband of Kavla (Lakshmi).
The Lord is the Giver; the whole world is a beggar, and all beings and creatures beg (at his door).
O Lord, in your mercy you give your gifts (even) to the worms and creatures inside stones.
Servant Nanak has meditated on the Naam, and through the Guru has become rich.
650.5: Salok, by the Third Guru (Guru Amar Das Ji).
Reading and studying (the scriptures) is worldly business, while within lies the sickness of craving.
In Haumai all have read until they are weary; in the love of another they are ruined.
He alone is learned, he the wise Pandit, who reflects through the Guru's Shabad.
He searches within himself, finds the essence, and reaches the door of liberation.
He has found the Lord, the treasure of virtues, and reflects (on him) in Sahaj.
Blessed is that trader, O Nanak, who through the Guru has the Name for his support.
650.6: By the Third Guru (Guru Amar Das Ji).
Without subduing the mind no one succeeds; let anyone attend closely and see.
